questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Archaeological evidence of a bead-making industry in the Sangam Era, using precious and semi-precious stones, has been found in Kodumanal. It is located in which of the following present day states of India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Archaeological evidence of a bead-making
industry, using precious and semi-precious stones, has
been found in Kodumanal. At present, it is located in
Tamil Nadu. The site is located on North bank of river
Noyyal. It was an important ancient trade city
belonging to the Sangam Era.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the methodology of excavation of mound, which among the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. Vertical excavations results in uncovering the period-wise sequence of cultures.
2. Horizontal excavation is generally confined to entire or part of a particular site.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
with reference to the methodology of excavation of
mound. A mound can be excavated vertically or
horizontally.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, New NCERT)

With reference to John Marshall’s stint as Director-General of Archaeological Survey of India, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. During his stint, the Indus Valley Civilisation was excavated.
2. He recognised while excavating that it was necessary to follow stratigraphy of the site.
3. He brought his experience of working in Greece and Crete to India.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct with reference
to John Marshall’s stint as Director-General of
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
John Marshall as Director-General of the ASI worked in
the excavations of Indus Valley Civilisation. He was the
first professional archaeologist to work in India who
brought his experience of working in Greece and Crete
to the field of archaeology. He was interested in
spectacular findings and was equally keen to look for
patterns of everyday life.
Statement (2) is incorrect as Marshall usually excavated
along regular horizontal units, measured uniformly
throughout the mound, ignoring the stratigraphy of
the site.
Coins
6. The history of Punjab and Haryana in first
century AD has been reconstructed on the basis
of study of several thousand copper coins issued
by
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)
(a) tribal republics of Kanva
(b) tribal republics of Yaudheya
(c) tribal republics of Gandhara
(d) Karkota dynasty of Kashmir
Ans. (b)

Exp. The history of Punjab and Haryana in first century
AD has been reconstructed on the basis of several
thousand copper coins issued by tribal republics of
Yaudheya. This republic was formed in the areas
between the Indus river and the Ganges river and was
contemporaries to Shunga, Indo-Greek and Kushan
Empire. The God Kartikeya is depicted on their coins
which only utilised Brahmi script.
7. With reference to the coins issued in ancient
India, which of the following statements is/are
incorrect?
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. Ancient coins are made up of metals such as
copper, silver, gold and lead.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List II List I (Historical (Ingredients of the Coins) Reconstruction) A. Names of kings and dates 1. Flourishing trade and commerce. B. More circulation of gold 2. Ruling dynasties and coins their extent C. Religious symbols and 3. Socio-economic aspect of gods history D. Coins used for donations 4. Art and religion
Codes A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.
Names of kings, gods and dates on coins help in finding
the area of their circulation and about ruling dynasties at
that time. It had helped in reconstruction of history of
tribal republic of Yaudheyas based in Haryana and
Punjab between first to second century AD.
More circulation of gold coins indicates flourishing
trade and communication as it helped in large scale of
transactions and helped commerce in the areas. For
instance, the large circulation of gold coins in Gupta era
attested the flourishing trade with Roman Empire.
Religious symbols and gods help us understand the
people’s culture and religious traditions. It also
portrayed their artistic sense. The portrayal of god and
goddesses helps in figuring out the religion patronised
by the ruling dynasty.
Coins used for donations tell about the socio-economic
conditions of the period. For instance, land and
monetary grants (through coins) by ruler of Satavahana
dynasty.
Inscriptions

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The earliest inscriptions in India was recorded on which of the following material ?

answerOptions.rationale:
The earliest inscription in India was recorded on
stone. These inscriptions were commissioned by the
rulers as well as by guilds and provincial governors.
They give an useful insight into the socio-political and
economic progress in ancient India. Large number of
stone inscriptions belonging to the megalith and
Sangam Era had been discovered from South India.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2018)

The Hathigumpha inscription gives year-wise account of the reign of

answerOptions.rationale:
The Hathigumpha inscription gives year-wise
account of the reign of king Kharvela of Kalinga. This
inscription is near Udayagiri hills in Bhubaneswar,
Odisha and is dated between second century BC to first
century AD. This inscription also highlights the
patronage of Jainism by the king Kharavela.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The office of Chief Epigraphist of India which contains the largest number of inscriptions is located at which of the following places?

answerOptions.rationale:
The largest number of inscriptions are found
in the office of the Chief Epigraphist at Mysore.
It was established in 1886 in Bangalore with
Dr. E Hultzsch as the head of the office.

The earliest inscriptions are found on the seals of
Harappa belonging to about 2500 BC. They have not

form.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The Girnar rock inscription states that repair of Sudarshana lake was undertaken by the rulers of various dynasties of ancient India. The kings of
which among the following dynasties were associated with Girnar rock inscriptions?
1. Mauryan Empire 2. Saka Empire
3. Gupta Empire 4. Kushan Dynasty
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The kings of Mauryan Empire, Saka Empire and
Gupta Empire are associated with the Girnar
inscription. This inscription mentions that Sudarshana
lake, with embankments and water channels, was built
by a local governor during the rule of the Mauryas.
However, a terrible storm broke the embankments and
water gushed out of the lake.
Then, Saka ruler Rudradaman, who was then ruling in
the area, got the lake repaired using his own resources,
without imposing any tax on his subjects. Another
inscription on the same rock (c. fifth century) mentions
how one of the rulers of the Gupta dynasty got the lake
repaired once again.
Kushan dynasty was associated with the Rabatak
inscription.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-VI, New NCERT)

The Allahabad Pillar Inscriptions helped in historical reconstruction of which of the following Kingdoms/ Empires of ancient and medieval India? (UP RO/ARO Pre 2016)
1. Maurya Empire 2. Gupta Empire
3. Delhi Sultanate 4. Mughal Empire
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Allahabad Pillar Inscription helped in historical
reconstruction of Maurya Empire, Gupta Empire and
Mughal Empire.
This inscription also known as Prayag Prashasti. It was
commissioned during the reign of Ashoka. It also has
eulogy about Samudragupta and his exploits as king. It
also had writings about Mughal Emperor Jahangir.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

With reference to limitations of inscriptions as a source of historical reconstruction, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. The content of the inscriptions only projects the perspective of the person(s) who commissioned them.
2. History regarding socio-cultural life of the common people is often missing in the inscriptions.
3. As all of them are recorded on perishable materials which provides scope for alteration.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to limitations of inscriptions as a source of historical
reconstruction. Inscriptions were commissioned by
people who were kings or in power and usually contain
what they wanted to show or perspective of the ruling
elites. The history regarding socio-cultural life of people
is often missing in the sculptures.
Statement (3) is incorrect as some of the inscriptions
were also recorded on non-perishable materials such as
stones and metals.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The ancient manuscripts of India were written on
which of the following materials?

answerOptions.rationale:
The ancient manuscripts of India were written on
birch bark. Although the ancient Indians knew writing
as early as 2500 BC, most ancient manuscripts, not
older than the fourth century AD have been found in
Central Asia. In India, they were written on birch bark
and palm leaves, but in Central Asia, where the Prakrit
language had spread from India, manuscripts were also
written on sheep leather and wooden tablets.

questions.question:
(Chap-2, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

In which of the following texts the list of the sixteen great states (Shodasa Mahajanapadas) of ancient India occur? (RAS, RTS 2016)
1. Arthashastra 2. Anguttara Nikaya
3. Digha Nikaya 4. Bhagavati Sutra
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, the Buddhist text,
Anguttara Nikaya and Digha Nikaya give the list of
sixteen great states (Shodasa Mahajanapadas) of ancient
India. These sixteen Mahajanapadas occured around
600 BC and is referred as the period of second
urbanisation in India. The list of sixteen Mahajanapadas
is also found in Jaina text Bhagavati Sutra.
Arthashastra is treatise on statecraft written by Kautilya.
It gives information regarding the state of polity
prevalent in Mauryan Empire.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the earliest Buddhist texts,
which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. They helps in historical reconstruction of the Magadha, North Bihar and Eastern Uttar Pradesh.
2. They were written in Pali language and were finally compiled in the second century BC in Sri Lanka.
3. The Buddhist canonical literature, Jataka throws invaluable light on social and economic conditions ranging from the fifth to second century BC.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to earliest Buddhist text.
The earliest Buddhist texts tell us not only about the life
of the Buddha but also about some of his royal
contemporaries who ruled over Magadha, North Bihar
and Eastern Uttar Pradesh.
They were written in the Pali language, which was
spoken in Magadha or South Bihar. They were finally
compiled in the second century BC in Sri Lanka.
Statement (3) is incorrect because the most important
and interesting portion of the ‘non-canonical’ literature
is provided by the stories of the previous births of
Gautama Buddha. Each birth story is called a Jataka
which is a folk tale. These Jatakas throw invaluable light
on social and economic conditions.
27. With reference to earliest Jaina literature, which
of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. They were written in Prakrit and were finally
compiled in the sixth century AD in
Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
2. They help in reconstructing the political history of
Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar in the age of
Mahavira.
3. It also throws light on the state of trade and crafts
and repeatedly refers to trade and traders.
Codes
(a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3
(c) 1 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3
Ans. (b)

Exp. Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to earliest Jaina literature.
The Jaina texts contain political history of Eastern Uttar
Pradesh and Bihar in the age of Mahavira.
It also has details and information which provides
valuable data about trade, crafts, and about traders.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Biographical Accounts) (Authors) A. Harshacharita 1. Sandhyakara Nandi B. Ramacharita 2. Banabhatta C. Vikramanakadevacharita 3. Bilhana D. Mushika Vamsha 4. Atula
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
Harshacharita is a biographical account of
Harshavardhana. It was written by his court poet
Banabhatta in 7th century AD.
Ramacharita was written by Sandhyakara Nandi in 12th
century AD. It tells the story of conflict between the
Kaivarta peasants and the Pala Prince Ramapala.
Vikramanakadevacharita was written by Bilhana, which
tells the achievements of his patron Vikramaditya VI
(1076-1127 AD). He was a Chalukyan king.
Mushika Vamsha was written in the 11th century by
Atula. It gives record of dynasty of Mushikas which
ruled in Northern Kerala.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The identification of an Indian king who was contemporary of Alexander as ‘Sandrokottas’ by Greek writers has served sheet-anchor in the ancient Indian chronology.
Which Indian ruler is described in the description given above?

answerOptions.rationale:
Indian ruler Chandragupta Maurya is described at
Sandrokottas by Greek writers. The Greek writers
mention Sandrokottas, a contemporary of Alexander the
Great who invaded India in 326 BC. Sandrokottas is
identified with Chandragupta Maurya, whose date of
accession is fixed at 322 BC. This identification has
served as the sheet-anchor in ancient Indian
chronology.
31. Which among the following ancient text
originally written in Latin, provides information
about trade between India and Roman Empire in
first century AD?
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Indika written by Megasthenes
(b) Geography written by Ptolemy
(c) Naturalis Historia written by Pliny
(d) Periplus of Erythrean Sea by an anonymous writer.
Ans. (c)

Exp. Naturalis Historia written by Pliny that belongs to
the first century AD, was originally written in Latin,
and provides information about trade between India
and Roman Empire.
Indika written by Megasthenes describes the state of
society and polity during the reign of Chandragupta
Maurya.
Ptolemy was Greek Geographer, who in his
Geography of India described about flora and fauna of
the country.
Periplus of Erythrean Sea was written by an anonymous
Greek writer. It provides information regarding trade
relation between South India and Roman Empire.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Foreign Travellers/ (Historical Writers) Reconstruction of) A. Megasthenes 1. Trade between India and Roman Empire B. Ptolemy 2. India in fourth century BC C. Fa-Hien 3. India in fourth and fifth century AD D. Hiuen Tsang 4. India in seventh century AD
Codes A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
Megasthenes’s Indika tells about Maurya rule in the
time of Chandragupta Maurya in the 4th century and
helps reconstruct the history of the period.
Ptolemy’s Geography was written in Greek and
provides information about ancient geography and
commerce between India and the Roman empire
around 150 AD.
Fa-Hien a Chinese traveller/pilgrim came in the age of
Guptas in fifth century AD and describes the social,
religious and economic situations.
His writing inspired other Buddhist scholars and
travellers from China to visit India in subsequent years.
Hiuen Tsang came to India in the seventh century AD.
He gave an elaborate account of state of polity, society,
economy and culture of India during the reign of
Harshavardhana.
Historians of Ancient India

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following authors is credited with the first systematic history of Ancient India?

answerOptions.rationale:
Vincent Arthur Smith is credited with the first
systematic history of Ancient India. He has prepared
the first systematic history of ancient India in 1904.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

‘A History of South India’ is the first modern book to give a detailed historiography of the South India. It was written by

answerOptions.rationale:
‘A History of South India’ is written by K A
Nilakanta Sastri (1892-1975). Most writers on early
Indian history did not give adequate attention to
South India.
Even KA Nilakanta Sastri , the great historian from
South India, followed the same approach in his ‘A
History of Ancient India’. This was more than rectified
in ‘A History of South India’ written by him.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the contributions of Max Mueller in Indian historiography, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. Under his editorship ancient Indian scriptures were translated on the massive scale and were published under the Sacred Books of the East Series.
2. He opposed the popular belief that ancient Indian lacked a sense of chronology and were accustomed to the despotic rule.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Only statement (1) is correct with reference to
the contribution of Max Mueller in the Indian
historiography.
The greatest push to Indological or Indian studies was
given by the German-born scholar F. Max Mueller
(1823-1902) who spent most of his time in England.
Ancient scriptures were translated on a massive scale
under the editorship of Max Mueller. Altogether fifty
volumes, some in several parts were published under the
Sacred Books of the East Series.
Statement (2) is incorrect as he didn’t oppose but put
down the popular belief that ancient Indians lacked a
sense of chronology and were accustomed to despotic
rule.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Colonial school of historiography, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? 
1. It believed that India did not experienced political modern unity until the establishment of British rule in India.
2. It made generalisation to serve as propaganda material for perpetuation of the despotic British rule in India.
3. It didn’t write about the prevalence of caste system in early Indian society.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to the colonial school of historiography.
British colonial historians stated that the ancient Indians
lacked a sense of history especially of the factor of time
and chronology. They added that the Indians were
accustomed to despotic rule.
The Western scholars stressed that the Indians had
neither experienced feelings of nationhood nor any kind
of self-government. So, they justified the British rule
over India.
Statement (3) is incorrect as they wrote about caste
systems, and considered it as worst form of
discrimination.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Nationalist school of historiography, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. They exploded the myth of Indian despotism and highlighted that republic existed in ancient India and enjoyed a measure of self-government.
2. They focused on the political history alone and ignored the cultural and social history.
3. They reconstructed ancient Indian history in such a manner as to make a case for social reforms and self-government.
Codes

(Chap 2, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Scholars related with List II Nationalist School of (Books) Historiography) A. Rajendra Lal Mitra 1. History of Institutions of Marriage B. R G Bhandarkar 2. Political history of Deccan under Satavahanas C. V K Rajwade 3. Indo-Aryans D. Pandurang Vaman Kane 4. History of the Dharamasastra
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4.
Rajendra Lal Mitra (1822-1891) wrote a book named
‘Indo-Aryans’. He took rational view of ancient society.
RG Bhandarkar (1837-1925) reconstructed the political
history of the Deccan under Satavahanas and History of
Vaishnavism and other sects.
VK Rajwade (1869-1926) wrote a book named ‘History
of Institutions of Marriage’.
Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880-1972) wrote ‘History
of Dharamasastra’ for which he received Bharat Ratna
in 1963. It is 6500 pages research work conducted in
40 years.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Palaeolithic phase of the cultural evolution of man is also referred as

answerOptions.rationale:
The old stone age is known as palaeolitic age. In
India, it is divided into three phases according to the
nature of the stone tools used by the people and also
according to the nature of change in climate. This period
is also known as Ice age, as the stone age started during
the Pleistocene period of ice age.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Pre-history, the three major tool types- hand axes, choppers and flake implements are associated with which phase of human cultural evolution?

answerOptions.rationale:
With reference to the Pre-history, the three major
tool types- hand axes, choppers and flake implements
are associated with Palaeolithic Phase. The Lower
Palaeolithic or the Early Old Stone age covers the
greater part of the Ice age. Its characteristic feature is
the use of hand-axes, cleavers and choppers.
The axes found in India are more or less similar to those
of Western Asia, Europe and Africa. Stone tools were
used mainly for chopping, digging and skinning.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which one the following pre-historic sites of India, is not related with Lower Palaeolithic age?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options sarai Nahar Rai is not
related with Lower Paleolithic age. It is a Mesolithic
site discovered from Pratapgarh district of Uttar
Pradesh.
Soan or Sohan valley is among the earliest discovered
Lower Palaeolithic Site in India. It was discovered
under Yale-Cambridge expedition and is presently
found in Pakistan. Sites belonging to Lower Paleolithic
age have also been discovered form Didwana in
Rajasthan and Bhimbetka, Adamgarh and Narsinghpur
in Madya Pradesh.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the cultural phase of Lower Palaeolithic in India, which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect?
1. It was characterised by glaciations and covered greater part of ice age.
2. During this phase, rock shelters served as seasonal camps for human beings.
3. The cultivation of crops and domestication of animals started in Lower Palaeolithic age.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to the
cultural phase of Lower Palaeolithic in India as in the
Lower Palaeolithic period there wasn’t domestication of
animals or any kind of agricultural activities, it only
started in the Mesolithic Age.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The modern Homo sapiens emerged in which phase of Human’s cultural history?

answerOptions.rationale:
The modern Homo sapiens emerged in Upper
Paleolithic phase. In this period, the climate became
warmer and it coincided with the last phase of the
Ice age.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Upper Palaeolithic phase of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka gives evidences of which of the following types of tools?

answerOptions.rationale:
Upper Palaeolithic phase in Andhra Pradesh and
Karnataka has evidence of use of blades and burins.
These tools have also been found in upper levels of
Gujarat dunes.
Caves and rock shelters of this age have been
discovered at Bhimbetka near Bhopal. Homo sapiens
also mark their presence in upper Palaeolithic age.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statement with reference to cultural phase of Upper Palaeolithic in India.
1. It coincided with last phase of the Ice age when climate became comparatively warm.
2. Caves and rock shelters used by early human beings in the Upper Palaeolithic phase have been discovered at Bhimbetka.
3. Most of the sites belonging to the Upper Palaeolithic phase have been discovered in alluvial plains of the Indus and the Ganga.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to
Cultural phase of Upper Palaeolithic in India as the
sites belonging to the Upper Palaeolithic phase are
absent in alluvial plains of the Indus and the Ganga.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following changes in the Mesolithic phase paved the way for formation of civilisation in later phases?
1. Climate became warm and dry.
2. People started fishing and food gathering.
3. Domestication of animals was introduced.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Changes mentioned in statements (1) and (3) are
the changes in Mesolithic phase that paved the way for
formation of civilisation in later phases.
The Upper Palaeolithic Age came to an end with the
end of the Ice Age around 9000 BC and the climate
became warm and dry. Climatic changes brought about
changes in flora and fauna and made it easier for
humans to travel.
It is seen as a transitional phase between the
Palaeolithic Age and the Neolithic or New Stone Age.
The Mesolithic people lived on hunting, fishing and
food gathering and at a later stage, they also
domesticated animals.
Statement (2) is incorrect as fishing and food gathering
were present already in the Upper Palaeolithic phase.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Mesolithic Sites) (Present day states) A. Bagor 1. Uttar Pradesh B. Adamgarh 2. Tamil Nadu C. Belan Valley 3. Rajasthan D. Theni 4. Madhya Pradesh
Codes A C B D A C B D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.
Bagor is presently in Bhilwara district in Rajasthan. It
had a microlith industry and inhabitants lived pastoral
lives and hunted animals.
Adamgarh is in Madhya Pradesh. This site is placed
around 5000 BC and is characterised by domestication
of animals. It is presently in Hoshangabad district.
Belan Valley is in Uttar Pradesh at the Northern side of
Vindhyan ranges. It has evidence of all three phases of
Palaeolithic, and also of Mesolithic and Neolithic age.
Theni is located in Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu,
here microliths tools of Mesolithic Age have been found.

(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Neolithic site of which among the following places is noted for the cultivation of rice in the sixth millennium BC?

answerOptions.rationale:
Neolithic sites of Koldhiwa in Prayagraj district is
noted for the cultivation of rice in the sixth millennium
BC. This site is dated around 7000 BC and contains
earliest evidences suggesting cultivation of rice in
Indian subcontinent.
19. Which among the following ancient pre-historic
site contains archaeological evidences of all the
three phases of Paleolithic followed by the
Mesolithic and Neolithic cultural phase?
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Belan Valley in Uttar Pradesh
(b) Bagor in Rajasthan
(c) Mehargarh in Pakistan
(d) Inamgaon in Maharashtra
Ans. (a)

Exp. On the Northern spurs of the Vindhyas in the
Belan valley in Uttar Pradesh, all the three phases of
the Palaeolithic followed by the Mesolithic and then by
the Neolithic have been found in a sequence, and same
is the case with the middle part of the Narmada valley.
The Pre-historic sites of Belan valley include Mahgara,
Chopani Mando and Koldihwa in Belan valley have
provided earliest evidence of rice cultivation.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Neolithic sites of South India are distinguished on the basis of tools used. They were

answerOptions.text: axes with oval sides and pointed butt
answerOptions.rationale:
The Neolithic sites of South India are
distinguished on the basis of axes with oval sides and
pointed butt. Based on the types of axes used by
Neolithic settlers, there are three important areas of
Neolithic settlements; North-Western, North-Eastern
and Southern. The Southern group is distinguished by
axes with oval sides and pointed butt. The
North-Western group of Neolithic tools represents
rectangular axes with curved cutting edges. The
North-Eastern group shows polished stone axes with
rectangular butt and has occasional shouldered hoes.

answerOptions.text: rectangular axes with curved cutting edge
polished stone axes with rectangular butt
polished stone axes with triangular butt

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Neolithic age in South India.
1. People of this age usually settled on the top of Granite hills or on plateaus near the river banks.
2. They used rubbing stone querns, which shows that they were acquainted with the art of producing cereals.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to the Neolithic age in South India.
A group of Neolithic people lived in South India, South of
the Godavari river. They usually settled on the tops of
Granite hills or on plateaus near the river banks. They
used stone axes and also some kind of stone blades.
Fire-baked earthen figurines suggest that they kept a
large number of cattle. They possessed cattle, sheep and
goats. They used rubbing stone querns, which shows that
they were acquainted with the art of producing cereals.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Which among the following innovations started in the Neolithic age is still used by the people of India?
1. Mortars and pestles for grinding grain.
2. Earthen pots for cooking and storing grains.
3. Needles for weaving clothes.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the Neolithic innovations mentioned in the
question are still used by the people of India.
Mortars and pestles for grinding grain, earthen pots for
cooking and storing grains and needles for weaving
clothes, all three techniques of Neolithic age are still
used in different forms, by people of India.

answerOptions.rationale:
The metal to be first used by man was copper.
Several cultures were based on the use of stone and

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Mains 2009)

In which state, the Navdatoli is located?

answerOptions.rationale:
Navdatoli is a Chalcolithic site located near
Indore in Madhya Pradesh. It was excavated by
eminent archaeologist HD Sankalia and is the most
extensively studied rural Chalcolithic site of India. It is
dated to be around 1600 BC and 1300 BC.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Chalcolithic communities of South India were specialised in the production of which of the following crops?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Chalcolithic communities of South India
were specialised in the production of rice. The
communities of this age founded the first large village
in Peninsular India and cultivated far more cereals than
the Neolithic communities.
In particular, they cultivated barley, wheat and lentil
in Western India, and rice in Southern and Eastern
India.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The people of Chalcolithic age domesticated
which of the following animals?
1. Cow 2. Camel
3. Horse 4. Sheep
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
People in the Chalcolithic period domesticated
cattle, sheep, goats, cows and camels. They were used
for meats and not milked for drink or dairy products.
Horse was not known to Indians in this period and it
came to be used later in Rig Vedic period.

Chalcolithic cultures appear after the end of the bronze
Harappan culture. Such cultures appear in the later
part of the mature Harappan culture or after its end.

Consider the following statements.

Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

(Chap 4, Class-VI, New NCERT)

In Megaliths, the dead were buried with distinctive pots, which are called

answerOptions.rationale:
Burials in Megaliths were done with distinctive
pots, they are called Black and Red ware. Sometimes
tools, weapons made of iron, ornaments of gold and
stones have also been found in these graves.
46. With reference to the ‘Megalith’ culture, which
of the following statement(s) are correct?
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. The practice of building Megalith began around
3000 years ago and was prevalent in South India
only.
2. The Megalith people of Southern Tamil Nadu
buried the skeletons of dead in urns made of red
pottery in pits.
3. The Megalith people did not practice an advanced
type of agriculture.
Codes
(a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3
(c) 1 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3
Ans. (b)

Exp. Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to the ‘Megalith’ culture.
Megalithic period of India was characterised by the use
of iron weapons and tools such as arrowheads,
spearheads, sickles etc. This tools points to the
occupation of hunting and fighting.
And very few tools related to agriculture activities have
been discovered. In Southern districts of Tamil Nadu,
dead bodies were buried in red pots or urns.
These graves were also not surrounded by stones like
other Megalithic graves.
Statement (1) is incorrect as the practice of building
Megalith began around 1000 BC. It was also found in
the Peninsular region, but was concentrated in Andhra
and Tamil Nadu.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VI, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Mains 2010)

The earliest evidence of agriculture in the Indian sub-continent has been obtained from

answerOptions.rationale:
The earliest evidence of agriculture in the Indian
sub-continent has been obtained from Mehargarh. This
site is located in Kachi plains in Baluchistan, Pakistan and
is dated around 7000 BC. Evidences of cultivation of
wheat and cotton is found from this site. The Cultural
remains from Stone Age (Neolithic) to Harappan
Civilisation have been also obtained from Mehargarh.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Which among the following pairs is incorrectly
matched?

answerOptions.text: Archaeology – Study of material remain of past
Anthropology – Study of physical characteristic and culture of man

answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (c) is matched incorrectly. The study of
non-human primates is called Primatology.
Ethnology is the study of characteristics of different
people. Archaeology is the study of human past using
material remains. Anthropology is the study of
physical characteristics and culture of man and his
customs, his mode of behaviour and his relation with
other men.

With reference to evolution of man, arrange the following hominids species in correct chronological order.
1. Australopithecus
2. Sinanthropus
3. Neanderthal
4. Cro-Magnon
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Chronological order of hominids species with
reference to evolution of man is first
Australopithecus, Sinanthropus, Neanderthal,
Cro-Magnon.
Australopithecus existed in Africa and remains of
Sinanthropus have been found in China. Neanderthal
were inhabitants of Eurasian region and Cro-Magnon
were the early Homo sapiens who came in upper
Palaeolithic phase.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following statements do not entails that the Harappan culture was a civilisation?

answerOptions.text: People were living a more advanced life than those of the previous primitive ages.
The cities were well planned and great care was taken to look after them properly.
The Harappan people knew how to write and their language was written in picture like signs called ‘pictographs’.
The Harappan culture was spread over Sind, Baluchistan, Punjab, Haryana, Western Uttar Pradesh, Jammu, Northern Rajasthan, Gujarat and Northern Maharashtra.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) do not entails that the Harappan
culture was a civilisation. It only tells about the
geographical extent of this cultivation that the
Harappan culture was spread over the whole of Sind,
Baluchistan, Punjab, Northern Rajasthan, Kathiawar,
and Gujarat but not in Northern Maharashtra. The
presence of advanced life-style, planned urbanisation
and prevalent of writing are some of the features that
show that Harappan culture was a civilisation.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Archaeological evidences of granary had been excavated from, which of the following Harappan site(s)?

answerOptions.rationale:
Archaeological evidences of granary had been
excavated from Mohenjodaro, Harappa and Kalibangan.
In Mohenjodaro the largest building is a granary, which
is 45.71 metres long and 15.23 metres wide. In citadel of
Harappa as many as 6 granaries are found.
There are also areas for threshing grains in rows of
circular brick platform. In Kalibangan, in Rajasthan also
the brick platforms have been found, which indicate
they had been used for granaries.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The burnt bricks were used in construction of buildings in which of the following civilisations?
1. Harappa 2. Egypt
3. Mesopotamia
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The burnt bricks were used in construction of
building in Harappa and Mesopotamia civilisations. In
Mesopotamia burnt bricks have been used but in
smaller scale than that of Harappa. While in Egypt
mainly dried bricks were used.

questions.question:

Consider the following statements with reference to the drainage pattern of Harappan cities.
1. Most of the houses big or small had its own courtyard and bathroom.
2. Water flowed from the house to streets, which did not have drains.
3. The remains of streets and drains have also been found at Banawali.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

(Chap 1, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Among, which of the following sites, the terracotta models of plough has been found?
1. Chanhudaro 2. Cholistan
3. Banawali 4. Rakhigarhi
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The terracotta models of plough has been found
Cholistan and Banawali. Cholistan is the portion of
Thar desert found in Pakistan. Banawali is located in
Harayana. This along with terracotta model of bull
discovered from other Harappan sites suggest
prevalence of flourishing agriculture in the Harappa
Civilisation. Archaeologist have also found evidence of
ploughed field at Kalibangan.
Chanhudaro located in Sindh Region of Pakistan was
almost exclusively devoted to the craft production.
Rakhigarhi situated in Haryana is the largest Harappan
site of India.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following animals were known to Harappans?
1. Elephants 2. Rhinoceros
3. Camels 4. Lions
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Elephants, Rhinoceros and Camels were known
to Harappans. These animals are found on seals,
pictographs, etc of that period. Besides these animals,
oxen, buffaloes, goats, sheep and pigs were
domesticated by the Harappans. The humped bulls
were favoured by the Harappans from the very
beginning.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

1. Cotton 2. Rice
3. Barley 4. Sugarcane
5. Potato

(Chap 1, Class-XII, New NCERT)

With reference to weights and measurement in Harappan culture, consider the following statements.
1. Exchanges were regulated by a precise system of weights, usually made of a stone called chert and generally cubical with no markings.
2. The lower denominations of weights were binary while the higher denominations followed the decimal system.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to weights and measurement in Harappan
culture.
Economic exchanges as well as trade and commerce
were managed with an accurate system of weights,
usually made of a stone called chert and generally
cubical with no markings.
The lower denominations of weights were binary (1, 2, 4,
8, 16, 32, etc up to 12,800), while the higher
denominations followed the decimal system. The
smaller weights were probably used for weighing
jewellery and beads.

(a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3 (c) 1 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3

j (d)

respect to seals used in Harappan Culture.
Seals and sealings of Harappa were used to facilitate
long-distance communication by pictures on them.
Mouth of bag was tied with rope and on the knot was
affixed some wet clay on, which one or more seals were
pressed, leaving an impression. If the bag reached with
its sealing intact, it meant that it had not been tampered
with. This sealing also conveyed the identity of the
sender.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which among the following suggests for the end of Harappan Civilisation?
1. Disappearance of seals, and the script.
2. Disappearance of distinctive beads and pottery.
3. Shift from a standardised weight system to the use of local weights.
4. The decline and abandonment of cities.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct regarding end
of Harappan Civilisation.
In the few Harappan sites, that continued to be
occupied after 1900 BC, there seems to have been a
transformation of material culture, marked by the
disappearance of the distinctive artefacts of the
civilisation – weights, seals, special beads, etc.
Long distance trade and craft specialisation disappeared
which lead to a shift from standard weights to local
weights.
House construction techniques deteriorated and large
public structures were no longer constructed. The
settlements like of Cholistan were abandoned and
population moved towards Gujarat, Haryana and
Western Uttar Pradesh.

Consider the following statements regarding administrative machinery of the Rigvedic Aryans.
1. The Rigveda does not mention any officer for administering Justice and collection of taxes.
2. In the Rigvedic period the King’s post was hereditary.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding administrative machinery of the Rigvedic
Aryans.
The Rigveda mention different functionaries for tasks.
But there is no mention of any officer for Judicial
Administration or tax collection.
King who used to be earlier from tribes, had become
hereditary in this period and to take decisions he used
to consult tribal assemblies.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding tribal polity of the Indo-Aryan.
1. They were divided into five tribes called Panchjanya.
2. They introduced Chariot driven by horses in India.
3. The Bharata ruling clan of the Aryan was supported by host of ten kings.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect regarding tribal polity
of the Indo-Aryans as the host of ten kings were
opposed to Bharata ruling clan.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following pairs is incorrectly
matched?

answerOptions.text: Rajasuya – Conferred supreme power to the king.
Asvamedha – Unquestionable control over the area where horse ran interrupted
Vajapeya – Blessed King with a male child.
answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (c) is incorrectly matched as Vajapeya was a
chariot race, in which royal chariot was run and was
supposed to win against his kinsmen.
These rituals, Rajasuya, Asvamedha and Vajapeya
increased kings prestige and influence over people. It
also increased the material wealth of the Brahamana
who were rewarded with the gifts for conducting these
rituals.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The tenth Mandala (chapter) of Rigveda contains references to the Shudra.
2. The Vedic god Agni acted as intermediary between the gods on one hand and the people on the other.
3. Child marriage was very common in the Rigvedic era.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct regarding state
of religion during the Rigvedic Period.
The dominant mode of worshipping the gods was through
the recitation of prayers and offering of sacrifices.
Prayers played an important part in Rigvedic times.
Both collective and individual prayers were offered.
Originally every tribe or clan was the votary of a special
god. Prayers were offered to Gods in chorus by the
members of a whole tribe.
Statement (1) is incorrect as there is no finding of any
large temple of Rigvedic times.

answerOptions.text: Exp. Statement (3) is incorrect as there was no examples of child marriage in the Vedic era. The marriageable age in the Rigveda seems to have been 16 and 17. The practice of levirate and widow marriage was prevalent in Vedic era. 22. Consider the following statements regarding state of religion during the Rigvedic period. 1. Large temples were constructed for the worship of Gods. 2. Dominate mode of worship of Gods was through recitation of prayers and offering of sacrifices. 3. Every tribe or clan was the votary of the special God. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct regarding state
of religion during the Rigvedic Period.
The dominant mode of worshipping the gods was through
the recitation of prayers and offering of sacrifices.
Prayers played an important part in Rigvedic times.
Both collective and individual prayers were offered.
Originally every tribe or clan was the votary of a special
god. Prayers were offered to Gods in chorus by the
members of a whole tribe.
Statement (1) is incorrect as there is no finding of any
large temple of Rigvedic times.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Who composed the ‘Gayatri Mantra’?

(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Functionaries) (Responsibilities) A. Upanayana 1. Fourfold division of society B. Varna 2. Decent from the common ancestors C. Ashrama 3. Sacred thread ceremony D. Gotra 4. Four stages of life
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2.
Upanayana was sacred thread ceremony for which all
three higher caste were entitled but not Shudras.
Varna was the fourfold division system of Rigvedic
times.
Ashrama was the four stages of life. They were
Brahmcharya or student, Grihastha or householder,
Vanaprastha or hermit and sanyasin or ascetic.
Gotra, appeared in later Vedic times. It signified
descent from a common ancestor.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following changes was/were observed in the state of religion during Later Vedic phase?
1. Prominent Rigvedic God Indra and Agni lost their importance.
2. People began to worship idols.
3. Brahmanas lost their ritual dominance.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Changes mentioned in statements (1) and (2)
were observed in the state of religion during Later
Vedic phase as in this period the most important Gods
of Rigvedic period the Indra and Agni lost their
importance and Prajapati the creator came to occupy
the supreme position.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding position of women in the Later Vedic era.
1. Women were thought to be inferior and subordinate to the men.
2. They were barred from participating in activities related with Sabha.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding the position of women in Later Vedic
era. The families started to be dominated by
father and it became patriarchal. Women were
generally given lower position.
As the importance and character of tribal assemblies
changed. The women were no longer allowed to take
part in Sabha. It came to be dominated by nobles and
princes.
Economy

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which was the main source of copper for the Indo-Aryans?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Khetri mines of Rajasthan was the chief
source of copper for the Indo-Aryans. Tools and
artefacts belonging to 1500-1000 BC have been
discovered from many parts of North India. Among
these, tools made up of copper has also been discovered.
It was one of the first metal used by Indo-Aryans. It
was used for making tools utensils and ornaments.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

In Vedic texts , the term ayas and syama denotes

answerOptions.rationale:
In Vedic texts, the term ayas and syama denotes
to copper and iron respectively. The Rigveda mentions
that they practiced crafts, carpenter, the chariot maker,
weaver etc. The term ayas used for copper or bronze
shows that metal-work was known.
Towards the end of Vedic period knowledge of Iron
implements spread in Eastern Uttar Pradesh. Earliest
iron implements discovered in this area belong to
seventh century BC and the metal is called shyama or
Krishna ayas.
32. Which type of pottery is/are associated with the
archaeological sites of Indo-Aryans?
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Northern Black Painted Ware (NBPW)
(b) Painted Grey Ware ( PGW)
(c) Black and Red Ware ( BRW)
(d) Both ‘b’ and ‘c’
j Ans. (d)
Exp. Painted Gray Ware (PGW) and Black and Red
Ware (BRW) are associated with the archaeological
sites of Indo-Aryans.
Later Vedic period people were acquainted with four
types of pottery- black and red ware, painted grey ware ,
black slipped ware, and red ware. It has been found all
over Western Uttar Pradesh.
It consisted of mostly of bowls and dishes. It was used
for rituals or eating or both.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The term vrihi in Vedic texts referred to

answerOptions.rationale:
Rice is referred to the term vrihi in Vedic text as
for the first time in area around Western Uttar Pradesh
and Punjab, Vedic people came across Rice. Earlier
they used barley, now rice and wheat became their
chief crops.
It is called vrihi in Vedic texts and its remains have been
found in Hastinapur belonging to eight century BC.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Agriculture and various crafts enabled the Later Vedic people to live a settled life.
2. They gave up the pastoralist and semi-nomadic lives practiced in Rigvedic era.
3. Iron was the first metal used by the Vedic people.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect as iron was used by
people of later Vedic period, earlier Rigvedic people
used metals such as copper, tin, gold and silver.
Statements (1) and (2) are correct. The later Vedic
period was characterised by increased artisan activities
and expansion of agriculture. The clearing of forests
with iron implements paved the way for cultivation of
large number of crops. Supported by agriculture,
people started performing different crafts. It enabled a
settled life for the people. Thus, the people of later
Vedic period gave up the pastoralist way of life
practised in Rigvedic period.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Besides agriculture, cattle rearing, fishing, metal work and carpentry were the main occupation of the people in later Vedic phase.
2. The use of iron axe – heads helped in the clearing heavy forests in the Ganga valley.
3. All persons in the same families were strictly advised to follow same occupations.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect as there is no such
restrictions on following any particular occupation on
family members.
Statements (1) and (2) are correct. Later Vedic people had
primarily became agriculturist. But the knowledge of
metals like iron and copper gave rise to crafts.
With knowledge of Iron, Vedic people defeated the
adversaries in Doab region. Excavations show weapons
made up of iron at that time. The iron axe may have helped
them clear the forests of Gangetic regions.
Miscellaneous

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-IX, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Mains 2003)

Which one of the following Vedic literature talks about Salvation?

answerOptions.rationale:
Vedic literature Upanishads talk about Salvation.
They were compiled around 600 BC and criticised the
rituals and laid stress on the value of right belief and
knowledge. Upanishads further emphasised that the
knowledge of the self or atman should be acquired and the
relation of atman with Brahma should be properly
understood.
38. The famous battle of ‘Ten Kings’ as described in the
Rigveda was fought on the bank of
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT) (UPPSC Mains 2008)
(a) Parushni (b) Saraswati (c) Vipasa (d) Asikni
Ans. (a)

Exp. The famous battle of ‘Ten Kings’ as described in the
Rigveda was fought on the bank of Parushni river. This
river is identical with the modern-day Ravi river. This
battle was fought between the Bharatas on the one hand
and host of ten chiefs on the other. In this battle, Sudas
emerged victorious and established the supremacy of
Bharatas.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Spl Mains 2008)

Which of the following river among the following referred as Matetama, Devitama and Naditama in the Rigveda?

answerOptions.rationale:
In the Rigveda, the Saraswati river was
referred as Matetama, Devitama and Naditama. It
was considered the most pious river of all and is
identified with the Ghaggar-Hakra Channel in
Harayana and Rajasthan.
The name Saraswati was derived from Avestan river
Harakhwati or the present Helmand river in the
South Afghanistan.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2010)

Which of the following rivers mentioned in the Rigveda indicates the relations of Aryans with Afghanistan?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given rivers, Kubha and Kramu
mentioned in Rigveda indicates the relations of
Aryans with Afghanistan.
The earliest Aryans lived in the geographical area
covered by Eastern Afghanistan. Kubha river is
identified with modern day Kabul river of
Afghanistan.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-IX, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Gambling was the chief mode of the amusements for the people in Vedic era.
2. Cow was the non-native animal species brought by Aryans in India.
3. The archaeological site of Antjrikhera belonged to the Vedic culture.
Which of the statement given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect as cow was not a
non-native animal species brought by Aryans in
India. Horse was the non-native animal species
brought by Aryans in India.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-VI, New NCERT)

The growth and maintenance of the mighty cities called Mahajanapada was centered on highly efficient agriculture. Which of the following method (s) was/were responsible for increase in the agricultural production?

answerOptions.rationale:
In Mahajanapadas, practice of transplantation was
the method responsible for increase in the agricultural
production. As the agricultural ways changed and
paddy was now being transplanted instead of seeds
being thrown in fields. It led to more production.
The use of ploughshare was other reason for increasing
production in those times and there were no
well-developed irrigation infrastructure.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The terms Nishka and Satamana referred in texts written during Mahajanapada era denoted

answerOptions.text: Fire altars used for performing rituals

answerOptions.rationale:
The terms Niksha and Satamana referred in texts
written during Mahajanapada era denoted coins. In age
of Mahajanapadas trade was facilitated by the use of
money. The terms Nishka and Satamana in Vedic texts
are taken to be name of coins, but they could have been
objects or prestige metals also as coins are not found
earlier than the sixth century BC.

questions.question:
(Chap-6, Class-XI, New NCERT)  (UPPSC GIC 2010)

The earliest extant coin of India were of

answerOptions.rationale:
The earliest extant coin of India were made up of
silver. The marks on these coins were made by the
stamp. These coins were also known as Aahat or punch
marked coins. It was used for both short and long
distance trade.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding reign of Bimbisara.
1. He strengthened the position of Magadha through matrimonial alliances.
2. He conquered the territories of Anga and placed it under the viceroyalty of his son.
3. He was succeeded by his son Mahapadma Nanda.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect regarding reign of
Bimbisara as he was succeeded by his son Ajatashatru,
who killed him and seized the throne for himself.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2003)

By, which ruler Pataliputra was chosen as the capital for the first time?

answerOptions.rationale:
Pataliputra was chosen as the capital for the first
time under the reign of Magadh ruler Udayin. Udayin
(460-444 BC) built the fort upon the confluence of the
Ganga and Son at Patna.
This was done because Patna lay in the centre of the
Magadhan kingdom, which now extended from the
Himalayas in the North to the hills of Chota Nagpur in
the South.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Name the minister of Ajatashatru who was successful in sowing the seeds of dissension in the rank of Lichchhavis of Vaishali and enabled the Ajatashatru to conquer the republic.

answerOptions.rationale:
Varasakara of Magadha was an able minister who
succeeded in sowing seeds of dissension in the rank of
Lichchhavi of Vaishali and enabled Ajatashatru to
conquer the republic.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The capital of the Magadha empire ‘Pataliputra’ was called water-fort (Jaldurga) as it was surrounded by

answerOptions.rationale:
The capital of Magadha Empire, ‘Pataliputra’ was
called water-fort ( Jaldurga), as it was surrounded by
Ganga river from the West, Son river from the North
and Punpun river from the South. It was strategically
located near the confluence of Ganga , Gandak and Son
river and was instrumental in providing connectivity to
all four directions through waterways. The Magadha
ruler, Udayin laid the foundation of the city of
Pataliputra.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding effect of Alexander invasion in India.
1. It opened up four distinct routes by land and sea between India and Greece.
2. The historians and geographers who accompanied Alexander left detailed account of India in the fourth century BC.
3. By destroying the power of petty states in North-West India, the Alexander invasion paved the way for expansion of Mauryan Empire.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
regarding effect of Alexander invasion in India.
The important outcome of Alexander’s was the
establishment of direct contact between India and
Greece. It opened up four distinct routes by land
and sea.
Alexander’s historians have left valuable geographical
accounts. They have left clearly dated records of
Alexander’s campaign, which enabled to build
Indian chronology for subsequent events on a definite
basis.
Alexander’s historians also give important information
about the Sati system, the sale of girls in market places
by poor parents, and the fine breed of oxen in
North-West India.
By destroying the power of petty states in North-west
India, Alexander’s invasion paved the way for the
expansion of Mauryan empire in that area.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Before the advent of Buddhism and Jainism under Gautama Buddha and Mahavira, many religious thoughts were prevalent in India.
Which among the following was/were religious idea(s) followed by the people before them?

answerOptions.text: People worshipped the Vedic gods such as Agni, Indra and Soma.
People were discussing and writing about questions regarding the meaning of life.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements were the religious ideas
followed by people before the advent of Buddhism and
Jainism.
People followed religious thoughts influenced by Vedic
literatures such as Vedas and Upanishads were
prevalent in India. People were worshipping the Vedic
gods such as Agni, Indra and Soma.
Similarly to please the Gods, people also started
performing collective sacrifices. It was also performed
by the heads of households for the well being of the
domestic unit.
Upanishads, which mostly contain philosophical
thoughts and ideas influenced people to write
and discuss about questions regarding the meaning
of life.

questions.question:
(Chap-9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to early life of Gautama Buddha.
1. He belonged to the Republican Sakya clan of Kapilavastu.
2. His childhood name was Siddharth.
3. He was born at Kushinagar.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect regarding early life of
Gautama Buddha as the Lumbini, presently in Nepal is
considered as the birthplace of Gautama Buddha. He
was born in 563 BC in a Sakya Kshatriya family in
Kapilavastu. His father Suddhodana was the elected
ruler of Kapilavastu. His childhood name was
Siddharth.

questions.question:
(Chap-9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The first human statue worshipped in India was of , (RAS, RTS Pre 2010)

answerOptions.rationale:
The first human statue worshipped in India was of
Buddha. The Mahayana sect of Buddhism, which
emerged during first century AD emphasised on
worship of Buddha through idols. The faithful devotees
portrayed the various events in life of Buddha in stone.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding traditions of debate and discussion in the sixth century BC.
1. During this phase, teachers travelled from place to place, trying to convince one another as well as laypersons, about the validity of their philosophy.
2. Debates took place in the Kutagarashala, which was a hut with a pointed roof where travelling mendicants halted.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding tradition of debate and discussion in the sixth
century BC.
A glimpse of lively discussions and debates is shown
from Buddhist texts, which mention as many as 64 sects
or schools of thought. Teachers travelled from place to
place, trying to convince one another as well as
laypersons, about the validity of their philosophy or the
way they understood the world.
Debates took place in the Kutagarashala – literally, a hut
with a pointed roof – or in groves where travelling
mendicants halted.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The earliest Buddhist literatures were written in,
which of the following languages?

answerOptions.rationale:
The earliest Buddhist literatures were written in
Pali language. It was also used by the Buddha to preach
the masses. The use of Pali, helped in spreading
Buddhism to masses, as it was language of common
people.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Who among the following were not allowed to be the member of Sangha?

answerOptions.rationale:
Debtors were not allowed to be the member of
Sangha. This helped moneylenders and richer section
of the society, from whose clutches debtor could not be
saved.
Similarly, the slaves were also not allowed to be part of
Sangha, this helped slave owners. Women were
allowed to be part of Sangha.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

In, which one of the following aspects, there is similarity between the Vedic philosophy and Buddhist teaching?

answerOptions.text: Both agreed on the authority of the Veda.
Both accepted the social division based on the caste system.
Both believed in the doctrine of Karma.
answerOptions.rationale:
The similarity between the Buddhist and the
Vedic philosophy is that they both believed in the
doctrine of Karma. Vedic philosophy placed value on
Karma as according to it people were born into
different Varna and rebirth was accordingly.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

In, which one of the following states, the Buddhist monasteries of Karle and Bedsa has been discovered?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Buddhist monasteries of discovered Karle and
Bedsa caves are in Western Ghats near Pune,
Maharashtra. They are Buddhist monasteries built for
monks to live, called chaitya. They are built by
Satavahana rulers. They were built by cutting rocks and
were also decorated by sculptures.

answerOptions.rationale:

in Varanasi.

answerOptions.text: place where Buddha attained the enlightenment.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which one of the following statements regarding the doctrine of middle path is incorrect?

answerOptions.text: It was preached by the Gautama Buddha.
According to this doctrine, a person should avoid excess of both luxury and austerity.
This concept was borrowed from the Jaina philosophy.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) is incorrect regarding the doctrine
of middle path because this concept was exclusively
propounded by Lord Buddha and was not borrowed
from Jaina philosophy. Lord Buddha was a practical
reformer and through the concept of middle path he
taught that a person should avoid the excess of both
luxury and austerstity. It can be followed by monks as
well as by the laypersons.

answerOptions.text: It can be followed by monks as well as by the laypersons.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

In the Buddhist literature, Sutta and Vinaya Pitaka are considered as the most authentic text for understanding Buddhism. What was the main theme of both of these texts?

answerOptions.text: Sutta Pitaka consisted of Buddha’s teachings and Vinaya Pitaka dealt with rules for maintaining the monastic orders.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) states the main theme of both of
these texts. Sutta Pitaka was composed of Buddha’s
teachings. Vinaya Pitaka included rules and regulations
for those who joined monastic orders or Sangha.
Apart from these two pitakas, the third pitaka is
Abhidhamma Pitaka, which dealt with philosophical
matters.

answerOptions.text: Vinaya Pitaka consisted of Buddha’s teachings and Sutta Pitaka dealt with rules for maintaining the monastic orders.
Sutta Pitaka comprises Buddha’s sayings and Vinaya Pitaka dealt with Buddhist philosphy.
Sutta Pitaka consisted of history of Buddhism in Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) and Vinaya Pitaka consisted of Buddha’s teachings.

questions.question:

Consider the following features. 
1. Deification of the Buddha
2. Trading the path of Bodhisattvas
3. Image worship and rituals
Which of the above is/are the features of Mahayana Buddhism?

(Chap-10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2016)

Consider the following statements with reference to the religious history of India. 
1. The concept of Bodhisattva is central to Hinayana sect of Buddhism.
2. Bodhisattva is a compassionate one on his way to enlightenment.
3. Bodhisattva delays achieving his salvation to help all sentient beings on their path to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to the religious history of India. In Buddhism,
Bodhisattva is considered as a compassionate one who
is on his way to enlightenment. Once they attained
enlightenment, they could live in complete isolation
and meditate in peace.
However, instead of doing that, they remained in the
world to teach and help other people. Thus, they delay
achieving his own salvation to help all sentient beings
on their path to it.
Statement (1) is incorrect as the concept of Bodhisattva
is central to Mahayana sect of Buddhism.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The Buddhist text, which described that the Emperor Ashoka distributed portions of the Buddha’s relics to every important town and ordered the construction of stupas over them was

answerOptions.rationale:
The Buddhist text was Ashokavadana, which
described that the Emperor Ashoka distributed
portions of Buddha’s relics to every important town and
ordered the construction of Stupa over them. The
tradition of erecting stupas may have been
pre-Buddhist, but they came to be associated with
Buddhism.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

‘Anda, harmika, yashti and chhatri’ are integral part of, which one of the following Buddhist monuments?

answerOptions.rationale:
‘Anda, harmika, yasti and chhatri’ are integral part
of stupas. Stupas were a simple semi-circular mound of
Earth, later called anda. Gradually, it evolved into a
more complex structure, balancing round and square
shapes. Above the anda was the harmika, a balcony-like
structure that represented the abode of the gods.
Arising from the harmika was a mast called the yashti,
often surmounted by a chhatri or umbrella. Around the
mound was a railing, separating the sacred space from
the secular world.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding causes of the decline of Buddhism in India.
1. From the first century AD onwards, they practised idol worship on large scale and received numerous offerings from devotees.
2. The enormous wealth of the monasteries with women living in them led to further degeneration of Buddhism in India.
3. They established the seats of learning at Nalanda and Vikramshila.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct regarding the
causes of the decline of Buddhism in India.
The decline of Buddhism started as the evils of
Brahminism seeped into it. Some monks started to treat
Buddha as God and worship his idols and statues.
They started to take donations and offerings from
devotees and turned into ease-loving people. This sect
was called Vajrayana.
Monks started to see women as object of lust. Allowing
of women in monasteries, which was done by mediation
of disciple Ananda, led to further degeneration of
Buddhism.
Statement (3) is incorrect as development of schools of
learning at Nalanda and Vikramshila led to expansion of
Buddhism.

Who of the following had first decipher the edicts of Emperor Ashoka?

answerOptions.rationale:
The edicts of the Emperor Ashoka were first
deciphered by James Prinsep. He was an employee of
East India Company and was associated with the
Asiatic Society of Bengal. In 1833 AD, he deciphered
the Brahmi script, which was used in the inscriptions of
Ashoka.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following inscriptions speaks about the success of the Ashoka’s Dhamma policy with hunters and fishermen, who gave up killing animals and possibly took to a settled agricultural life?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Kandhar inscription speaks about the success
of Ashoka’s Dhamma policy with the hunters and
fishermen, who gave up killing animals and possibly
took to a settled agricultural life.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

The finely polished stone sculpture of the bull,
which has now been placed in the Rashtrapati Bhavan had been taken from?

answerOptions.rationale:
The finely polished stone sculpture of the bull
which has now been placed in the Rashtrapati Bhavan
(President house) had been taken from Ashoka’s pillar
inscription at Rampurwa.
The bull capital of Rampurva was originally constructed
in the West Champaran district of Bihar. It is one of the
seven remaining animal capitals from the pillars of
Ashoka. It has strong influence of Greek, Persian and
Indian art.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding inscriptions erected under the reign of Ashoka.
1. The name of Ashoka occurs only in copies of Minor Rock Edict I found at three places in Karnataka and at one in Madhya Pradesh.
2. All the other inscriptions referred Ashoka as Devanampriya Priyadarshi.
3. They throw light on the career of Ashoka, his external and domestic policies, and extent of his empire.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All of the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are
correct regarding inscriptions erected under the reign
of Ashoka.
The history of Ashoka is reconstructed on the basis of
his inscriptions, numbering 39. They are classified into
Major Rock Edicts, Minor Rock Edicts, Separate Rock
Edicts.
The name of Ashoka occurs only in copies of Minor
Rock Edict I found at three places in Karnataka and at
one in Madhya Pradesh. All the other inscriptions
mention only Devanampriya Priyadarshi, dear to Gods,
and leave out the word Ashoka.
The Ashokan inscriptions are found in India, Nepal,
Pakistan and Afghanistan. Altogether they appear at 47
places. These inscriptions throw light on the career of
Ashoka, his external and domestic policies, and the
extent of his empire.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding Ashokan inscriptions.
1. The stone pillar were made in Vaishali near Pataliputra and from there it was transported to North and South India.
2. These inscriptions were erected on all the important highways.
3. These inscriptions conveyed Ashoka’s messages to his subjects.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect regarding Ashokan
inscriptions because the stone pillars were made in
Chunar, in Uttar Pradesh near Varanasi; from here they
were transported to North and South India.

(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The Emperor Ashoka appointed the official, Dhamma mahamatras for

answerOptions.rationale:
The Emperor Ashoka appointed the official,
Dhamma mahamatras for propagating dharma among
various social groups. Ashoka tried to hold his empire
together by propagating dhamma, the principles of
which were simple and virtually universally applicable.
According to him, this would ensure the well-being of
people in this world and the next.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding administration of armed forces during the reign of Mauryan Empire.
1. It was carried on by a board of 30 officers divided into six committees.
2. The six wings of the armed forces– the army, the cavalry, the elephants, the chariots, the navy and the transport were administered by a separate committee.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding administration of armed forces during the
reign of Mauryan empire.
The administration of the armed forces, according to
Megasthenes, was carried on by a board of 30 officers
divided into six committees, each committee consisting
of five members.
It seems that the six wings of the armed forces–the
army, the cavalry, the elephants, the chariots, the navy
and the transport were each assigned to the care of a
separate committee.

(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to foreign policy of Ashoka, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. Ashoka treated foreign dominions as legitimate areas for military conquests.
2. Ashoka had sent foreign mission to Syria, Egypt and Greece to spread ideas about the dhammas.
3. Ashoka’s son, Mahendra preached Buddhism in Sri Lanka.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct regarding
foreign policy of Ashoka. He sent ambassadors of peace
to Greek Kingdoms in West Asia (Syria, Egypt) and
Greece. It was done to propagate the message of
Dhamma. He also sent missionaries for the propagation
of Buddhism to Sri Lanka and Central Asia. He tried to
enlarge his political influence through propaganda. He
had sent his son Mahendra to Sri Lanka to preach
Buddhism.
Statement (1) is incorrect as Ashoka after witnessing the
horrors of Kalinga war, didn’t treat foreign dominion as
legitimate areas for military conquests. Rather he tried
to conquer them ideologically.

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Officials in List II Mauryan Empire) (Functions) A. Rajukas 1. Reporter B. Pativedaka 2. Chief custodian of the state treasury C. Sannidhata 3. Administering Justice D. Samaharta 4. Highest officer in charge of assessment.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following method(s) was/were utilised by the Mauryan Emperors to increase the area under cultivation?

answerOptions.text: Provisions for cattle, seed and money

answerOptions.rationale:
Remission in tax and provisions for cattle, seed
and money were utilised by the Mauryan Emperors to
increase the area under cultivation. The Mauryan
emperors in order to increase the area under
cultivation, employed various strategies recommended
in Arthashastra of Kautilya.
Some of the measures included-employing shudras for
agricultural operation, providing remission in tax,
ensuring provisions for cattle, seed and money to the
new settlers. This policy led to the opening of large
areas to cultivation and settlement.
Irrigation facilities at the state expense wasn’t made for
new cultivation areas.

answerOptions.text: Irrigation facilities at the state expense

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The characteristic feature of the Mauryan pottery was

answerOptions.rationale:
Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) was the
characterstic feature of Mauryan pottery. Megasthenes
has mentioned in high praise the skill shown by artisans
of Pataliputra palace. They show high technical skills
attained by them. The polishing of stone pillars, which
are known as Northern Black Polished Ware are still
found in sites of Mauryan Empire. There are sculptures
of peacock, bulls or lions made of them.

questions.question:
(Chap-15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Mains 2005)

Which of the following South kingdoms is not mentioned in the Ashokan inscriptions?

answerOptions.rationale:
The kingdom of Satavahana is not mentioned in
the Ashokan inscriptions. This Kingdom emerged in
Peninsular India after the downfall of the Mauryan
Empire. The Rock Edict II and XIII mention that
Chola, Chera, Pandya and Satyaputras lived on the
borders of the Mauryan state. The Pandyas were known
to Megasthenes who visited the Mauryan Capital.
