questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following monument(s) was/were constructed during the reign of Mauryan Empire?
1. Barabar Caves 2. Ajanta Caves
3. Sanchi Stupa 4. Kailasa Temple
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Barabar caves and Sanchi Stupa were constructed
during the reign of Mauryan Empire. The Mauryan
artisans also started the practice of cutting out caves
from rocks for monks to live in. Its examples are
Barabar caves at the distance of 30 km from Gaya, Bihar.
Sanchi stupa is in Madhya Pradesh. It was ordered to be
constructed by Ashoka. It is also a rock cut structure.
Ajanta caves and Kailasa temples (Ellora) are in
Maharashtra. They date back to different reigns
(Satavahanas and Rashtrakutas) not to Mauryan
Empires.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following statements regarding the Mauryan capital is correct?

answerOptions.text: It was located in Kumrahar on the outskirts of modern Prayagraj.
The fragments of the stone pillars and stumps indicate existence of 80 pillared hall in the Mauryan Capital.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is correct regarding the Mauryan
Capital. The Mauryas made a remarkable contribution to
art and architecture. They introduced stone masonry on
a wide scale. Megasthenes states that the Mauryan
palace at Pataliputra was as splendid as that in the capital
of Iran. Fragments of stone pillars and stumps, indicating
the existence of a 80-pillared hall, have been discovered
at Kumrahar on the outskirts of modern Patna.

answerOptions.text: Chanakya in the Arthashastra states that the Mauryan Palace was as beautiful as that of Iran.
It was constructed by using unburnt bricks on the large scale.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the contribution of Mauryan in the art and architecture.
1. They introduced stone masonry on a wide scale.
2. The polished pillars were made up of a single piece of buff coloured sandstone.
3. They started the practice of hewing out caves from rocks for monks in India.
4. They started the use of burnt bricks for the first time in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct with
reference contribution of Mauryan in the art and
architecture.
Mauryan artisans attained high technical skills in
polishing the stone pillars, which are as shining as
Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW).
Each pillar is made of a single piece of buff coloured
sandstone. Only their capitals, which are beautiful
pieces of sculpture in the form of lions or bulls, are
joined with the pillars on the top.
They also introduced stone masonry on a wide scale.
The Mauryan artisans also started the practice of
hewing out caves from rocks for monks to live in.
The earliest examples are the Barabar caves at the
distance of 30 km from Gaya, Bihar.
Statement (4) is incorrect as burnt brick was first used
in Indus Valley Civilisation.

questions.question:
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following statements regarding the state of society under the Mauryan Empire is incorrect?

answerOptions.text: Slaves were engaged in the agricultural operations.
Ashoka tried to strengthen the institution of family and existing social classes.
The Mauryan Emperors prohibited the inter- mingling between the peasants and tribal societies.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect regarding the state of
society under the Mauryan Empire as Mauryan
emperors supported be inter-mingling between
the peasants and tribal societies. Ashoka launched a
deliberate and systematic policy of acculturation.
He states that as a result of the diffusion of dhamma
men would mingle with Gods.
This implies that tribal and other people would take to
the habits of a settled, taxpaying, peasant society and
develop respect for paternal power, royal authority and
for monks, priests and officers who helped enforce his
authority.
51. With reference to the welfare policy(s) undertaken
by Ashoka, which of the following statements is/are
correct?
(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. He taught people to live and let live and
emphasised compassion towards animals.
2. He arranged for medical facilities for both human
beings and animals.
3. He prohibited the practice of sati.
Codes
(a) 1 and 2 (b) 1, 2 and 3
(c) 2 and 3 (d) 1 and 3
Ans. (a)

Exp. Statements (1) and (2) are correct regarding
welfare policies undertaken by Ashoka. Ashoka taught
people to live and let live.
He emphasised compassion towards animals, birds and
proper behaviour towards relatives. He built roads, dug
wells and rest houses. He arranged for medical
treatment for both human beings and animals.
Statement (3) is incorrect as there is no evidence of
prance of sati during the reign of Ashoka, the refore the
emperor didn’t made any attempt to prohibit it.

answerOptions.text: The Shudras were regarded as the collective property of the three higher varnas.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Ashoka’s perspective on religion.
1. He intiated dhamma yatras in which, he undertook pilgrimages to the Buddhist shrines.
2. He organised the first Buddhist Council and sent missionaries to South India and Sri Lanka.
3. He aspired to attain nirvana, which was the goal of the Buddhist teaching.
4. He respected and made donations to religious sect other than the Buddhism.
Which of the statements given above are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are incorrect with reference
to Ashoka’s perspective on religion as Ashoka held third
Buddhist Council (Sangiti) at Pataliputra.
Further, instead of attaining nirvana he sought a policy
of development and empowerment of masses.
He never stated that his aim was to attain nirvana.
Miscellaneous

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Even before Ashoka, which among the following rulers had pursued pacifist policy of administration?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Akhnaton of Egypt had followed the pacifist
policies even before Ashoka. However, Ashoka was
probably unknown of his policies. He therefore,
initiated his own policies based on the edifice of peace
and compassion.

(Chap 15, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Kanva dynasty, which of the statement(s) given below is/are correct?
1. It ruled Magadha after the downfall of Shunga dynasty.
2. They were greatest patron of Jainism in ancient India.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with reference to the
Kanva dynasty. Shunga dynasty was followed by Kanva

killed the last Shunga king, Devabhutti. Its capital was

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Simuka founded the Satavahana dynasty in Deccan and Central India.
2. The Satavahana capital, Paithan or Pratishthan is identified with modern day city of Aurangabad in Maharashtra.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct.
Satavahana dynasty ruled parts of Deccan and Central
India in first century BC to second century AD. They
were successful in defeating the Kanvas.
Simuka is considered as the founder of Satavahana
dynasty. Their capital, Paithan or Pratishthan is
identified with modern day city of Aurangabad in
Maharashtra.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following with reference to the Satavahana dynasty.
1. It succeeded the Mauryas in the Deccan and Central India after the gap of 100 years.
2. The rulers of this dynasty were identified through matronymics.
3. Similar to the Mauryas, the rulers of this dynasty established matrimonial alliances with Indo-Greeks.
Which of the statements given above are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to the
Satavahana dynasty because Satavahanas practiced
endogamy, marriage within the kin group, which was
prevalent amongst several communities in South India.
Such marriages amongst kinfolk (such as cousins)
ensured a close-knit community. They didn’t
established matrimonial alliances with Indo-Greeks.

mentioned in the Satavahana inscriptions meant

Skandhavaras were fortified and represented feudal
character of kingdom. Both of these settlements served
as administrative centre as long as king was there.

questions.question:
(Chap 17, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the extraction of minerals during the age of Satavahana, which of the following statements are correct?
1. They exploited the iron-ores of Karimnagar and Warangal region of the Andhra Pradesh.
2. During the reign of Satavahana, iron was introduced in the Deccan and Central India for the first time.
3. Lead was used for the minting of coins on a very large scale.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct regarding
extraction of minerals during the age of Satavahana.
The mines of Karimnagar and Warangal region of
Andhra Pradesh was the chief source of iron-ore for the
Satavahana. It greatly benefitted their economy.
Under Satavahana, lead was the chief metal used for
mining of coins. They also commissioned coins made up
of potin (mixture of copper, tin and lead), copper and
bronze.
Statement (2) is incorrect because iron had been used
before the Satavahanas, the megalithic (stone builder)
were familiar with iron.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, New NCERT)

With reference to Amravati Stupa, which of the following statements are correct?
1. It was constructed during the reign of Satavahana rulers.
2. It is full of sculptures which depicts the various scenes from the life of the Buddha.
3. Similar to the Sanchi Stupa it was also preserved by the local authorities till the 19th century.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference to
Amravati Stupa. The Godavari region is famous for
independent Buddhist structures, mostly in the form of
stupas. The most famous of them are Amravati and
Nagarjunakonda. The Stupa was a large round structure
erected over some relic of the Buddha. The construction
Amravati stupa began in about 200 BC but was
completely reconstructed in the second half of the
second century AD. It was patronised by the Satavahana
rulers. It is full of sculptures which depicts the various
scenes from the life of Buddha. The theme of this
sculptures were drawn from Jataka and was narrative in
outlook.
Statement (3) is incorrect because Amravati Stupa is not
well preserved and its stones and parts were taken to
other places and used.

Consider the following statements with reference to the architecture in the reign of Satavahana.
1. Large number of Chaityas and Vihara were constructed in the regions of Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
2. Influenced by the Mahayana tradition of Buddhism, the sculptures of Satavahana times depicted the image of Buddha and other Bodhisattva from the Jataka tales.
3. The construction of Buddhist monuments were commissioned by the rulers only.

undertaken by the rulers as well as by merchant guilds.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Indo-Greeks.
1. They were the first to invade India after the downfall of the Mauryan Empire.
2. They introduced a practice of military governorship in India.
3. Taxila was the capital of Indo-Greeks in India.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to
Indo-Greeks because Taxila was not capital of
Indo-Greeks. There were different kings in
Indo-Greeks and they had different capitals, e.g. the
most famous Indo-Greek ruler Milinda had his capital
at Sialkot, now in Pakistan.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the King Vikramaditya of Malwa.
1. Vikram Samvat is reckoned from the event of his victory over the Shakas in 57 BC.
2. He constructed Sudarshana lake in the semi-arid zone of Kathiawar.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:

Vikramaditya of Malwa.
In about 57-58 BC, king of Ujjain effectively fought
against the Shakas and succeeded in driving them out in
his time. He called himself Vikramaditya and an era
called the Vikrama Samvat is reckoned from the event of
his victory over the Shakas in 57 BC. From this time
onwards, Vikramaditya became a coveted title.
Statement (2) is incorrect as Sudarshana lake was
constructed during the reign of Mauryan emperor,
Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Shaka ruler Rudradaman-I.
1. He commissioned the first ever long inscription in Chaste Sanskrit.
2. He ruled parts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Bengal.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect regarding the Shaka
ruler Rudradaman-I as Rudradaman-I ruled parts of
Western India comprising modern territories of Sindh,
Gujarat, Konkan, Malwa and Kathiawar.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Sudarshana lake.
1. It was an artificial reservoir constructed in the Girnar region of Gujarat.
2. It was built by the local governor during the reign of Mauryas.
3. A rock inscription of the Saka ruler, Rudradaman gives information about this lake.
4. It was destroyed by the Indo-Greek rulers in India.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (4) is incorrect as terrible storm broke
the embankments and water gushed out of the lake
with reference to the Sudarshana lake. It was not
destroyed by the Indo-Greek rulers in India.
Rudradaman, a Shaka ruler, ruling in the area, claimed
to have got the lake repaired using his own resources,
without imposing any tax on his subjects.
Statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct.
The Sudarshana lake was an artificial reservoir in Girnar
region of Gujarat. It is mentioned in a rock inscription

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the reign of the Parthians in India.
1. In comparison with the Greeks and the Shakas they occupied a large portion of North-Western India.
2. The most famous Parthian king was Gondophernes in whose reign St. Thomas visited India for the propagation of Christianity in India.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect about the reign of the
Parthians in India because in comparison with the
Greeks and the Shakas they occupied only a small
portion of North-Western India.
The Kushans

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Kushans belonged to which one of the following tribes of the Central Asia?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Kushans belonged to Yuechis tribes of the
Central Asia. The Parthians were followed by the
Kushans, who are also called Yuechis or Tocharians.
The Kushanas were one of the five clans into which the
Yuechis tribe was divided. They were nomadic people
from Steppes of North Central India.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2018)

Which among the following first issued gold coins on a large scale?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given rulers, Vima Kadphises first
issued gold coins on a large scale. He was the father of
greatest Kushan ruler Kanshika and was successful in
extending his kingdom East of Indus.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Kushan dynasty.
1. The ruler of this dynasty controlled the silk route passing from China to the territories of the Roman empire.
2. It was the first dynasty to issue gold coins on the wide scale.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding Kushan dynasty.
The Kushans controlled the silk route, which started
from China and passed through their empire in Central
Asia and Afghanistan to Iran and Western Asia which
formed part of the Roman empire. Kushans were the
first rulers in India to issue gold coins on a wide scale.
They levied heavy tolls on traders because of that they
were able to manage prosperous empire.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

The colossal statues of Kushan rulers have been found installed in

answerOptions.rationale:
Colossal statues of Kushan rulers have been found
installed in a shrine at Mat near Mathura (Uttar
Pradesh). Similar statues have been found in a shrine in
Afghanistan as well. Some historians feel this indicates
that the Kushana considered themselves godlike. Many
Kushan rulers also adopted the title devaputra, or ‘son
of God’.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The modern day territories of which of the following countries were part of the Kushan empire?
1. India 2. Iran
3. Afghanistan 4. Vietnam
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
As per modern dry territories India, Iran and
Afghanistan were the part of the Kushan empire.
Kushan empire extended from the Oxus river to the
Ganga, from Khorasan in Central Asia to Varanasi in
Uttar Pradesh. A good part of Central Asia now
included in the Commonwealth of Independent States
(in former USSR), a portion of Iran, a portion of
Afghanistan, almost the whole of Pakistan and almost
the whole of Northern India were brought under one
rule by the Kushans.
Vietnam was not a part of the Kushan empire.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the Kushan dynasty.
1. Its kings adopted the pompous titles of King of Kings and Sons of God.
2. They introduced the satrap system of government.
3. Hereditary dual rule was also prevalent during the reign of the Kushan dynasty.
Which of the statement(s) given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct about
the Kushan dynasty.
Kushans solidified idea of their godly right of kingship.
Kushan kings were called sons of God. It was used to
legitimise the royal authority.
The Kushans also introduced the satrap system of
government. In satrap system, the empire was divided
into numerous satrapies and each satrapy was placed
under the rule of a satrap. The hereditary dual rule, two
kings ruling in the same kingdom at same time, were
also there.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to Kushan ruler, Kanishka, which of the following statements are correct?
1. He defeated the Chinese ruler from the Hun dynasty in the first century AD.
2. To consolidate the teachings of Mahayana Buddhism, he convened a Buddhist Council in Kashmir.
3. He started the Saka Era in 78 AD.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to Kushan ruler, Kanishka.
Kanishka (78-101 AD) was most famous Kushan ruler.
He started an era in 78 AD, which is now known as Saka
era and used by Government of India.
Kanishka was a great patron of Mahayana Buddhism. He
convened Buddhist Council in Kashmir, in which
teachings of Mahayana Buddhism were finalised.
Statement (1) is incorrect as he was defeated by the Hun
Dynasty Chinese ruler in first century AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class XI, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2006)

Which one of the following is the correct chronological order with reference to the invaders in ancient India?

(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Indo-Greeks in India.
1. They issued coins which can be definitely attributed to the kings.
2. They were the first to issue gold coins in India.
3. They introduced features of Hellenistic art in the North-West frontier of India.
4. They introduced spoked wheel in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct with
reference to Indo-Greeks in India.
The Indo-Greeks were the first rulers in India to issue
coins which can be definitely attributed to the kings.
This is not possible in the case of the early
punch-marked coins, which cannot be assigned with
certainty to any dynasty.
The Indo-Greeks were the first to issue gold coins in
India, which increased in number under the Kushanas.
The Greek rule introduced features of Hellenistic art in
the North-West frontier of India. This art was not purely
Greek. It was the result of Greek contact with
non-Greeks.
Statement (4) is incorrect as spoked wheel were in use
even in Maurya rule.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Greek ambassador, Heliodorous set up a pillar in honour of Vasudeva in

(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The images of God, Shiva and Buddha appeared on the coins of the rulers of which one of the following dynasties?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Kushan rulers worshipped both Shiva and the
Buddha and the images of these two gods appeared on
the Kushan coins. Several Kushan rulers were
worshippers of Vishnu. This was certainly the case with
the Kushan ruler Vasudeva, whose very name is a
synonym for Krishna.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The period of Saka-Kushan phase in the Indian history was characterised by which one of the following Potteries?

answerOptions.rationale:
The period of Saka-Kushan phase in Indian
history was characterised by Red Ware Pottery.
They are similar of red pottery with thin fabric found in
the same period in Kushan layers in Central Asia. Red
pottery techniques were widely known in Central Asia
and they are found even in regions like Farghana, which
were on the peripheries of the Kushan cultural zone.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The ancient texts, Mahavastu and Divyavadana are related with which of the following sects of the Buddhism?

answerOptions.rationale:
The ancient texts, Mahavastu and Divyavadana
are related with Mahayana sect of Buddhism. These
texts were written after the advent of Shaka and
Kushan rule in India to propagate the teaching of
Mahayana Buddhism. It was written in hybrid Sanskrit.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the contribution of Shakas and Kushans in military technology.
1. They popularised the use of spears and lances for the horseman.
2. They introduced the use of caps, helmets and boots in warfare.
3. They also introduced the use of gun powder for storming the fortress of the adversaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to the contribution of Shakas and Kushans in military
technology.
Shakas and Kushans brought better cavalry and the use
of riding horse on a large scale. Some of their horsemen
were heavily armoured and fought with spears and
lances. They also brought caps, helmets and boots.
They were used by warriors.
Statement (3) is incorrect as they didn’t introduced gun
powder. It was introduced later in medieval period.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about Ashvaghosha.
1. He enjoyed the patronage of Kushans.
2. He wrote Buddhacharita, the biography of the Buddha.
3. He also composed the Saundarananda which is a fine example of Kavya in Prakrit language.
Which of the statement(s) given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct regarding
Ashvaghosha. Ashvaghosha was the greatest luminary at
the court of Kanishka. He is credited with the
composition of Buddhacharita, which is a biography of
Buddha.
Statement (3) is incorrect because Saundarananda was
also composed by Ashvaghosha in Sanskrit language (not
Prakrit).

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the development in the field of medicine in Post-Mauryan times.
1. The Indian benefitted immensly from the Greeks in the field of medicine.
2. The Charaka Samhita contains names of numerous plants and herbs from which drugs are to be prepared for the use of patients.
3. For the cure of ailments the ancient Indian physician relied chiefly on plants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to the development in the field of medicine in
Post-Mauryan times.
The ancient treatise on medicine, Charaka Samhita was
written by Charak. It contains names of numerous
plants and herbs from which drugs are to be prepared
for the use of patients. For the cure of diseases, ancient
Indian Physician relied mainly on plants, for which the
Sanskrit word is Oshadhi and as a result medicine itself
came to be known as Aushadhi.
Statement (1) is incorrect because Indians didn’t benefit
from Greeks in medicine, they relied on works of
Charaka and Sushruta.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following ancient cities was the great center for the manufacture of the special type of clothes called Shataka?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, the ancient city of
Mathura was the great centre for the manufacturing of
the special type of clothes called Shataka. It was the
second capital of Kushan ruler and was famous centre
for indigenous art (famously called as Mathura school of
Art). It was also the thriving centre for trade and
commerce during the Post-Mauryan age.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

What is the significance of Yelleshwaram with reference to the cultural history of India?

answerOptions.text: The largest number of terracottas and moulds has been discovered from the Satavahana period.
answerOptions.rationale:
In the cultural history of India, the ancient site of
Yelleshwaram ( located in Present day East Godavari
district of Andhra Pradesh) is very important. From this
site, the largest number of terracotta and moulds has
been discovered from the Satavahana period. Besides
Satavahana, archaeological findings of this site had
revealed artifacts associated with Ikshvakus and Pallava
dynasty.

answerOptions.text: It was the centre for making fake Roman coins.
An inscription mentioning the types of crafts practised in the Satavahana period has been discovered from this site.
Largest Chaitya hall from the Satavahana period has been excavated.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The ancient cities of Khairadih and Mason,
which prospered greatly during the Kushan Phase is located in which of the following present-day state of India?

answerOptions.rationale:
The ancient cities of Khairadih and Mason, which
prospered greatly during the Kushan Phase are located
in present day state of Uttar Pradesh. During the reign
of Kanishka, the territories of Kushan dynasty also
covered parts of Uttar Pradesh and Eastern Bihar.
Besides these two cities, Chirand, Sonpur and Buxar ,
in Bihar also witnessed prosperous Kushan phases.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about trade routes in ancient India.
1. The Shakas and the Kushans used two routes from the North-Western frontiers to the Western coast of India.
2. Both of these routes converged at the Mathura and were connected with the silk route.
3. Uttarpatha was the most frequently used trade route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct about trade
routes in ancient India. The Shakas and the Kushans
used two routes from the North-Western frontier to the
Western sea coast. The first route directly ran from the
North to the South connecting Taxila with the lower
Indus basin from where it passed on to Broach, Gujarat.
The second route called the Uttarpatha was in more
frequent use. From Taxila it passed through modern
Punjab upto Western coast of Yamuna. It further went
to Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.
Statement (2) is incorrect as both these routes
converged at Taxila and were connected with the silk
route passing through Central Asia.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to trade between India and Roman Empire in the Post-Maurya age.
1. Articles of daily use of common people dominated the trade between Indian and Roman Empire.
2. Roman mainly imported spices, muslins, pearls, jewels and precious stones from Central and South India.
3. India also served as the intermediary station for exporting goods from Central Asia and China to Roman Empire.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect with reference to trade
between India and Roman Empire in the Post-Maurya
age as the volume of trade between India and Rome
seems to have been large, but it was not carried on in
articles of daily use for the common people. There was
a trade in luxury goods, which are also called articles of
aristocratic necessities.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to balance of trade between India and Roman Empire in the Post-Maurya age.

Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to balance of trade between India and Roman Empire
in the Post-Maurya age. Both Kushans and Satavahanas
kingdom profited from trade with Romans, but the
maximum profit went to Satavahanas.
Roman Empire took measures to ban India made steel
cutlery and pepper. Roman nobles used to pay high

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the coinage in the Post-Mauryan age, which of the following statements are incorrect?
1. The Kushan issued the dinar type of gold coins in India.
2. For day to day transactions coins made up of lead and copper was used.
3. All the gold imported from the Roman Empire was used in mining of coins in India.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to
coinage in the Post-Mauryan age as it is wrong to think
that all Kushan gold coins were minted out of Roman
gold. In fifth century BC, India had paid a tribute of
320 talents of gold to the Iranian empire. This gold may
have been extracted from the gold mines in Sind.
The Kushans probably obtained gold from Central Asia.
They may also have procured it either from Karnataka,
or Dhalbhum in South Bihar.

answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (a) is not correctly matched because Nagas
ruled over the Central India not Eastern India.
Pairs (b) and (c) are correctly matched Mitras ruled in

Yaudheyas ruled Rajasthan together with the adjacent
areas of Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the growth of urbanisation in Post-Mauryan phase.
1. Most Indo-Greek towns in India lay exactly on the Uttarpatha route passing from Mathura to Taxila.
2. The rulers of Kushan dynasty ensured security on the important trade routes.
3. Ujjain was the most important city administered by the rulers of Saka dynasty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to the growth of urbanisation in Post-Mauryan phase.
The Kushan empire ensured security on the routes,
which lay on Kushan towns. Its end in the third century
AD dealt a great blow to these towns.
Ujjain was most important town of this period, as it lay
on the nodal point of these two trade routes, one from
Kaushambi and other from Mathura. It was also
important because of its export of agate and carnelian
stones.
Statement (1) is incorrect as most Kushan towns in India
lay exactly on the North-Western or Uttarpatha route
passing from Mathura to Taxila.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Terms associated List II with Post-Mauryan (Meaning) Phase) A. Mleccha 1. Curtains B. Gandhika 2. People outside Varna order C. Yavanika 3. Pepper D. Yavanpriya 4. Artisans specialising in manufacture of perfumes

answerOptions.rationale:

Mleccha were people who were kept outside the Varna

Romans.

Gupta dynasty was famous for

answerOptions.rationale:
Gupta dynasty was famous for its splendid art and

which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the reign of Samudragupta.
1. He defeated the four kings of Northern India and added the region of present day Delhi and Western Uttar Pradesh to his kingdom.
2. In one of his coins, he is shown playing a veena.
3. He incorporated the territories of nine tribal republics of Afghanistan.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect regarding reign of
Samudragupta as he didn’t incorporate areas of
Afghanistan, but of Rajasthan. From the nine tribal
areas of Rajasthan, he also collected taxes and received
regular tributes.
Statements (1) and (2) are correct. Samudragupta
defeated four kings of Northern India and added the
region of the present day Delhi and Western Uttar
Pradesh to his kingdom. He fought against a number of
kings in the Deccan and South India, such as those in
Orissa, Andhra and Madras.
Samudragupta was not merely a conqueror, he was also
a poet and a musician. In one of his coins, he is shown
playing a veena.

Which among the following Gupta ruler was successful in defeating the Hunas?

The Gupta king Skandagupta succeeded in

(Chap 21, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following was the most important official in the Gupta Empire?

answerOptions.rationale:
The most important official in the Gupta Empire

questions.question:
(Chap 21, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Gupta administration, the term ‘Vishti’ refers to

answerOptions.rationale:
The term Vishti, in Gupta administration refers to
forced labour. In Central and Western India, the
villagers were subjected to forced labour, Vishti, for
serving the royal army and officials.

questions.question:
(Chap 21, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the provincial and local administration under the Gupta Empire, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. The empire was divided into divisions called bhuktis and were placed under the charge of Rajuka.
2. The bhuktis were divided into districts called Vishyas and were placed under the charge of Vishayapati.
3. In Eastern India, the Vishayas were divided into Vithis, which were further divided into villages.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct regarding
provincial and local administration under the Gupta
Empire. The Guptas organised a system of provincial
and local administration. The empire was divided into
divisions which were called Bhuktis.
The bhuktis were divided into districts (Vishyas), which
were placed under the charge of Vishayapati.
In Eastern India, the Vishyas were divided into Vithis,
which again were divided into villages.
Statement (1) is incorrect as bhukti was placed under
the charge of an Uparika.

questions.question:
(Chap 21, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The vassals who lived on the fringes of the Gupta Empire were obliged to certain function(s), such as

answerOptions.text: homage to the sovereign by personal attendance at his court.
to present their daughters in marriage.

answerOptions.rationale:
The vassals who lived on the fringe of the Gupta
empire carried out three obligations: they offered
homage to the sovereign by personal attendance at his
court; paid tribute to him and presented to him
daughters in marriage. The major part of the Gupta
empire was held by feudatory chiefs, many of whom
had been subjugated by Samudragupta.

questions.question:
(Chap 21, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the difference between administrative mechanism of the Mauryas and Guptas.
1. In the Mauryan empire, administration was highly centralised whereas in Gupta Empire, it was feudalistic in character.
2. The Mauryan Empire regulated the major economic activities of the state whereas in Gupta Empire, guilds were authorised to carry out many important functions of regulation.
3. They retained the elaborate political machinery of the Mauryan times.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct regarding the
difference between administrative mechanism of the
Mauryas and Guptas. The Guptas neither needed nor
possessed the centralised administrative machinery of
Mauryan times, and in some ways, their political system
appears to be feudal.
Guptas did not require too many officers because,
unlike the Mauryan state, the Gupta state did not
regulate economic activities on any big scale. The
participation of leading artisans, merchants, elders, etc.,
in rural and urban administration also reduced the need
for maintaining a large numbers of officers.
Statement (3) is incorrect as they didn’t keep the
elaborate systems of Mauryas because they didn’t
need it.

money did not touch the common people so much as it
did under the Kushans.

With reference to the state of religion under the Gupta Empire, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. Vaishnavism became the most prominent religion.

3. The Gupta kings, in order to promote Hinduism, persecuted the followers of Buddhism and Jainism.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct regarding state
of religion under the Gupta Empire.
Vaishnavism became the new prominent religion as
took Vishnu, a Vedic God, Krishna, a legendary hero of
Vrishni tribe, and Narayana, a non-Vedic tribal God
and merged their worshippers into one.
Idol worship became a common feature of Hindu
religion from Gupta period. And many festivals also
started to be celebrated.
Statement (3) is incorrect as Gupta king didn’t persecute
different religious sects and follow tolerant religious
policy.

In Sanskrit plays, such as Mrichchhakatika by

Yashodharman a king from Malwa (Central India,

rulers in Central India.

532 AD pillars of victory, commemorating his conquest.

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Arab invasion was not

sixth century AD.

Monarch over their vassals. Later, Guptas accepted
Buddhism and followed pacifist policies.

What was the capital of the Mukhari dynasty

Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh was the capital of the

Uttar Pradesh in the sixth century AD. Late Guptas of
Magadha also established their power in Bihar
alongside Mukharis.

Consider the following statements with reference to the Judicial system prevalent during the Gupta age.
1. For the first time, civil and criminal laws were clearly demarcated.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect regarding Judicial
system prevalent during the Gupta age. As during the
Gupta age, theft and adultery came under criminal law
(not civil law) whereas disputes regarding various types
of property came under civil law (not criminal law).

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Harshacharita and
account of Chinese pilgrim, Hiuen Tsang help in the
historical reconstruction of the reign of Harshavardhana.

the reign of Gupta Empire, gives a detailed account of
reign of Chandragupta Vikramaditya.

of Pandya Kingdom. The Pandyas were occupied the
region of modern districts of Tirunelveli, Ramnad and
Madurai in Tamil Nadu. Madurai was their capital,
which is situated on the bank of river Vagai.
Kallikudi inscription of Pandyan King Sriseevalla Devar
states that Pandyas ruled over Ramnad Ramnathpuram
which was the Southernmost district of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the ancient city of Puhar under the Chola Kingdom.
1. It was founded by the famous king Karikala and served as the capital of the Chola Kingdom.
2. It was great centre of trade and commerce and had a large dock.
3. It is identical with the present day city of Chennai.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to the
ancient city of Puhar under Chola kingdom. Puhar is
identical with city of Kaveripattinam in Tamil Nadu
and not with Chennai. Puhar was the capital of Cholas.
Puhar was founded by Chola King Karikala.
Excavations shows that it had a large dock and was a
centre of trade and commerce.
The Port city of Puhar became an emporium of foreign
trade in Sangam period as big ships entered this port
with precious goods.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Keralaputras mentioned in the inscription of Ashoka was identical with the Tamil Kingdom of

answerOptions.rationale:
The Keralaputras mentioned in the inscription of
Ashoka were identical with Cheras. The same
inscription of Ashoka also mentions the Southern
Kingdom of Pandyas, Cholas and Satyaputras (not
recognised yet). The ancient Chera Kingdom covered
modern day territories of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which one of the following statements on the ‘Chera’ is not correct?

answerOptions.text: The first Chera king Udiyanjeral was called Imayavaraman.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is not correct because the first
Chera king Udiyanjeral was not called Imayavarman, it
was second king of Chera and son of Udiyanjeral (also
spelled as - Uthiyan Cheralathan), Nedum Cheralathan
was known as Imayavarman.
Imayavarman Nedum Cheralathan (Nedunjeral Athan)
was the second king of Chera dynasty of the Sangam era
of South India.

answerOptions.text: Their great ruler was Sanuguttuvan or Red Chera.
They used modified version of Tamil.
They were in alliance with the Pandyas.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding relations between the Cheras and the Roman Empire.
1. They carried lucrative trade with the Roman Empire.
2. The Romans set up two regiments at Muziris in the Chera Kingdom to protect their interests.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding the relations between the Cheras and the
Roman Empire. The Chera Kingdom owing to its
strategic location, carried lucrative trade with the Roman
Empire. The Romans set up two regiments at Muziris
identical with Cranganore in the Chera Kingdom to
protect their interests. The temple of Roman Emperor,
Augustus was also built by Romans in Muziris.
Pandyas

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The rulers of which among the following Kingdoms, convened the three Sangam Assemblies?

answerOptions.rationale:
The rulers of Pandya Kingdom convened the
three Sangam assemblies. Sangam was a college or
assembly of Tamil poets held under chiefly or royal
patronage. The texts compiled in these assemblies is
the main source of historical reconstruction of the reign
of Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which one of the following statements is incorrect regarding the Pandya kingdom?

answerOptions.text: Its territory occupied the Southernmost and the South-Eastern portion of the Indian peninsula.
Madurai was the capital of the Pandya kingdom.
The Pandya kings profited from trade with the Roman Empire and sent embassies to the Roman Emperor Augustus.
The rulers of Pandya Kingdoms were ardent follower of Buddhism.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) is incorrect regarding the Pandya
kingdom as the rulers of Pandya kingdom had
brahmanical influence from Northern Kingdom and it
enjoyed it’s patronage. Pandya kings performed Vedic
sacrifices in early centuries of Christian Era.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, New NCERT)

In the context of the economic history of the South India, who were ‘Masattuvan’?

answerOptions.rationale:
‘Masattuvan’ were designated as successful
merchants in Tamil and called Setthis and Satthavahas
in Prakrit, could become enormously rich. Masattuvan
were specialised in both inland as well as in external
trade. A wide range of goods were carried from one
place to another like salt, stone, timber, medicinal
plants were in high demand in the Roman Empire, as
textiles and medicinal plants and these all were
transported across the Arabian Sea to the Mediterranean.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The words for rice, ginger, cinnamon and several other articles in Greek language were derived from Telugu language.
2. Pariyars were agricultural labourers specialising in animal skin.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect as in ancient times, the
Tamils traded with the Greek or Hellenistic kingdom of
Egypt and Arabia on the one side, and with the Malay
archipelago and from there with China on the other. As
a result of trade, the words for rice, ginger, cinnamon
and several other articles in Greek language were
derived from Tamil language.
17. Which among the following step(s) were
undertaken by the rulers of three ancient Tamil
Kingdoms to promote and protect trade with
foreign kingdoms?
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Appointment of custom officials

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists and choose the correct code. List-I List-II (Social Classes in (Descriptions) Tamil Literature) A. Enadi 1. Ruling class B. Vellalas 2. Members of lowest class specialising in agricultural operations. C. Kadaisiyar 3. Rich peasants D. Arasar 4. Captains of army
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-4, B-2, C-3, D-1.
Enadi was a title offered to Captains of army. It was
done at a special ceremony and was indicative of
importance of warrior class in Sangam age.
Vellalas were fourth caste of Sangam age. They formed
the peasantry and were further divided in rich and poor
peasants.
Kadaisiyar were members of lowest class who carried
agricultural works. They were treated same as of slaves
in Sangam age.
Arasar were ruling class of Sangam age and had
marriage relations with fourth caste, Vellalas.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Kshatriyas and Vaishyas were treated normally and

Warrior class who fought wars were respected and given
titles.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

‘‘In a space in which an elephant could lie, one can produce enough grains to feed seven’’. This was stated in Sangam poems for which of the following kingdom?

answerOptions.rationale:
The given statement from the Sangam poems
highlight the agricultural productivity of Coromandel
coast of Tamil Nadu in the Sangam age. It was drained
by the Kaveri river and was famous for production of
rice. It formed the territories of the Chola Kingdom.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following ancient Tamil text deals with Philosophy and wise maxims?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Tirukkural deals in an
ancient Tamil text with philosophy and wise maxims. It
is an ancient Tamil text written by Thiruvalluvar. It is
one of the greatest works on ethics and morality and is
also referred as Tamil Veda.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Sangam literature.
1. The narrative works are called Kilkanakku or Eighteen Minor Works.
2. The didactic works are called Melkanakku and comprises eighteen major works consisting of eight anthologies and ten idylls.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are incorrect with
reference to Sangam literature. The Sangam literature

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Art of writing in South India, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. It was introduced in the Southern India by the Brahamana priests in the second century AD.
2. More than 75 short inscriptions in the Brahmi script have been found in the caves near Madurai.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Only statement (2) is correct with reference to
the Art of writing in South India.
More than 75 short inscriptions in the Brahmi script
have been found in natural caves, mainly in the
Madurai region. It provide the specimens of the
earliest form of Tamil mixed with Prakrit words. They
belong to the second-first centuries BC when the Jaina
and Buddhist missionaries appeared in this area.
Statement (1) is incorrect as the art of writing was
known to the Tamils before the beginning of the
Christian era, and brahmanical influence.

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about Tamil epics written during the Sangam age.
1. Silappadikaram written by a Buddhist monk deals with the love story of Kovalan and Madhavi.
2. Manimekalai written by the grain merchant of Madurai deals with the adventure of the daughter born of the union between Kovalan and Madhavi.
3. Both these epics throw light on the social and economic life of the Tamils upto the sixth century AD.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect about Tamil epics
written during the Sangam age as Silappadikaram was
written by Ilango Adigal who was a Jaina monk. Also
referred as ‘story of anklet’, it deals with love story of
Kovalan and Madhavi.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Vakataka kingdom, which among the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. They succeeded Satavahanas in Southern Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
2. They were great patron of Brahmanical religion and performed numerous Vedic sacrifices.
3. They supported the Gupta rulers in conquering Gujarat and adjoining parts of Western India from the Shaka Kshatraps.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference to
the Vakataka kingdom. The Vakataka were Brahmans
themselves. They issued land charters to brahmans, it
had been found on large number of copper-plates. They
were great patron of Brahmanical religion and
performed numerous Vedic sacrifices.
The Vakataka had matrimonial relation with Gupta
rulers. Chandragupta II married her daughter Prabhavati
Gupta to Vakataka prince. And in consequence Vakataka
helped Gupta rulers in conquering Gujarat and nearby
areas of Western India from Shaka Kshatraps.
Statement (1) is incorrect as Vakataka succeeded the
Satavahanas in areas of Northern Maharashtra and
Vidarbha.
Ikshvakus

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Ikshvaku dynasty.
1. They were descendants of the mythological Ikshvaku dynasty of Ayodhya.
2. They started the practice of land grants in the Krishna-Guntur region.
3. They constructed beautiful monuments at Nagarjunakonda and Dharanikota.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect because the Ikshvaku
dynasty (225-340 AD) was a feudatory tribe under the
patronage of Satavahana Empire. That ruled the
Krishna - Guntur region of Andhra Pradesh.
The lkshvakus constructed many monuments at
Nagarjunkoda and Dharanikota. Dharanikota (present-
Amravati) was the capital of the lkshvakus. They were
the patronage of Amravati School of Art.
Pallavas

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

The Pallavas were the feudatories of which among the following kingdoms of the ancient India?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Pallavas were the feudatories of the
Satavahanas kingdom, and began their rule in far South
after decline of Satavahanas. They started as local rulers
and gradually extended their rule Southwards to
Kanchipuram, in Tamil Nadu. They fought many battles
with rulers of Chola dynasty for supremacy over
Coromandel coast.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The rulers of Pallavas and Chalukyas were engaged in bitter struggle over the supremacy of

answerOptions.text: land lying between the Krishna and Tungabhadra.
answerOptions.rationale:
The rulers of Pallavas and Chalukyas were
engaged in bitter struggle over the supremacy of land
lying between the Krishna and Tungabhadra river. The
main interest in the political history of peninsular India
from the sixth to the eighth century centres around the
long struggle between the Pallavas of Kanchi and the
Chalukyas of Badami for supremacy.
Time to time, the Pallava princes tried to cross the
Tungabhadra river, which formed the natural historic
boundary between many kingdom of the Deccan and
the deep South.

answerOptions.text: port of Arikamendu and Uraiyur in the Eastern coastal peninsula.
the territories of Kalinga ruled by the Ganga dynasty.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Pallava king Mahendravarman I.
1. He was the contemporary of Harshavardhana and Pulakeshin II.
2. He was converted to the Vaishanavism by the Tamil saint, Appar.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to the
Pallava King Mahendravarman I (600-630 AD) as he
was a Jaina to begin with, but was later converted to
Shaivism by Appar, one of the Tamil saints.
Statement (1) is correct.
Mahendravarman I, the Pallava king, ruled at the same
time as Harsha (606-647 AD) and Pulakeshin II
(610-642 AD). So, he was a contemporary of both. Like
many of the kings of his time, he too was not just a
warrior but also a poet and a musician.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Pallava King Narasimhavarman I, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. He assumed the title of Vatapikonda after defeating Pulakeshin II of the Chalukya dynasty.
2. He also founded the Port city of Mamallapuram.
3. The seven ratha temples at Kanchipuram was built under his reign.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct with
reference to the Pallava King Narasimhavarman.
Narasimhavarman I (630-668 AD) assumed the title of
Vatapikonda, which means the conqueror of Vatapi
after defeating Pulakeshin II.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-VI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the local assembly under the Pallava rulers.
1. Sabha was the assembly of the Brahmin land owners.
2. Ur was a village assembly found in areas where the land owners were not Brahmins.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to the local assembly under the Pallava rulers.
The inscriptions of the Pallavas mention a number of
local assemblies. These included the Sabha, which was
an assembly of brahmin land owners. This assembly
functioned through sub-committees, which looked after
irrigation, agricultural operations, making roads, local
temples etc.
The Ur was a village assembly found in areas where the
landowners were not brahmins. The organisation of
merchants was called the ‘Nagarams’, these assemblies
were controlled by rich merchants and landowners.
These local assemblies survived for centuries in
South India.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the state of religion under the Pallavas.
1. The rulers of the kingdom lavishly patronised the Brahmanas and performed many vedic sacrifices.
2. The Tamil saints, Alvar popularised the worship of Shiva and Nayanar saints promoted the worship of Vishnu.
3. Under the influence of Brahmana, Sanskrit became the court language under the rulers of Pallava Kingdom.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to the state
of religion under the Pallavas because Alvars and
Nayanars both preached the cult of Bhakti but Alvars
preached Vaishnavism during the Pallava period and
Nayanars had preached Shaivism and were known as
Shaivaites.
After the establishment of the Pallava rule, the
Brahmanism was revived. The Pallava rulers had
patronised Brahmanism and performed many vedic
sacrifices. They had built temples and made land grants to
Brahmins.
Sanskrit was the court language under the Pallava rule.
Dandin wrote Avanisundari Katha. Famous Pallava King
Mahendravarman wrote Mattavilasprahasan in Sanskrit.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following monument(s) was/were built under the auspice of Pallava rulers?
1. Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram
2. Virupaksha Temple at Hampi
3. Kailashnath Temple at Kanchipuram
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The Shore Temple of Mahabalipuram or
Mamallapuram and the Kailashnath Temple at
Kanchipuram were built during the reign of the Pallava
ruler Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) and it is the oldest
structural temple of significance in South India.
These temples were constructed in 8th century AD.
Virupaksha Temple at Hampi was constructed by Lakkan
Dandesha, a chieftain under the ruler Deva Raya II of the
Vijayanagara Empire.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Mains 2005)

The capital of Kadamba Kings was

answerOptions.rationale:
The capital of Kadamba kings was Banvasi.
Kadamba kingdom was contemporary with
Pallavas. It was founded by Mayurasharman who
received education at Kanchi. He was successful in
defeating the Pallava kings with the help of forest
tribes. It was established in 345 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the ancient kingdom of Kadambas.
1. They after defeating the rulers of Pallava dynasty established an independent kingdom with its capital at Vijayanti or Banvasi.
2. They initiated the grant of tax free lands to the Brahmanas for lieu of their services.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to the
ancient kingdom of Kadambas, as land grants were
already being given by Pallavas who also patron
Brahaminism.
Ganga Dynasty

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

In the territories administered by the Chalukyas, the rural affairs were managed by village elders called

answerOptions.rationale:
In the territories administered by the Chalukyas,
the rural affairs were managed by village elders called
‘Mahajana’ under their management. The period from
300-750 AD provides good evidence of rural expansion,
organisation and better use of land.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Chalukyan ruler who ended the supremacy of the Pallavas in the South was

answerOptions.rationale:
The Chalukyan ruler who ended the supremacy of
the Pallavas in the South was Vikramaditya II (733-745
AD) who invaded Kanchi three times. In 740 AD, he
completely destroyed the Pallavas. His victory ended
the Pallava dominance in the far South even though
the Pallavas house continued for more than a century
after this.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-VI, New NCERT)

With reference to the Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. He led the victorious campaign against the Harshavardhana in the North and Mahendravarman of Pallava kingdom.
2. He started the practice of appointing feudal chief in the Southern India.
3. He sent an embassy to the Persian King, Khusrau II.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct with reference
to the Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II.
He was the greatest ruler of Chalukya Kingdom of
Badami. He defeated Harshavardhana at the bank of
Narmada river in 618 AD. He also led successful
military expedition against Mahendravarman of Pallava
kingdom. To promote trade and ensure regular supply
of good quality of horses, he also sent an embassy to
Persian king Khusrau II.
Statement (2) is incorrect as practice of appointing
Feudal Chief had already started by other kingdoms in
the past.

questions.question:
(Chap 24, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The Chalukya ruler sent an embassy of 72 merchants to China.
2. Rashtrakuta, the feudatory of Chalukyas annexed the Kingdom of Chalukyas in 757 AD.
Which of the statement(s) give above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are incorrect
because Chola Empire under the king Kulottunga I sent
an embassy of 72 merchants to China.
Rashtrakuta the feudatory of Chalukyas annexed the
kingdom of Chalukyas in 753 AD. Dantidurg, who was a
feudutory of Chalukya defeated ruler Kritivarman II in
753 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Initially, the rulers of Chola Empire were feudatories of Pallavas.
2. The founder of Chola Empire was Vijayalaya.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct.
The founder of the Chola Empire was Vijayalaya, who was
at first a feudatory of the Pallavas. He was successful
in capturing Tanjore in 850 AD.
By the end of the ninth century AD, the Cholas had
defeated both the Pallavas of Kanchi and weakened the
Pandyas, bringing the Southern Tamil country
(Tondamandala) under the control.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2020)

Which medieval Indian empire was famous for elaborated local self-government?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Chola Empire was famous for its local
self-government. Villages in Chola empire was
governed two type of assemblies
One type of village consisted of people from
different caste and the assembly which ran this type
of village was called ‘Ur’, the other type of village
was ‘Agrahara’, which were settled by Brahmins in
which most of the land was rent free.
The assembly of this agrahara type of village was a
gathering of the adultmen in Brahmana village
called Sabha or Mahasabha. These village enjoyed a
large measure of autonomy.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which Chola king started Naval Army? (CGPSC Pre 2014)

answerOptions.rationale:
Rajaraja I (985-1014 AD) was a Chola king who
started the Naval Army. He destroyed the Chera navy
at Trivandrum and attacked Quilion. He also invaded
Sri Lanka and annexed Northern part to his empire.
During his reign and his successor’s Rajendra Chola,
the Chola navy became strongest in the world.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2000)

Who among the following Chola rulers converted the Bay of Bengal into a ‘Chola lake’?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Chola ruler, Rajendra I (1014-1044 AD)
converted the Bay of Bengal into a ‘Chola lake’. He led
a naval expedition against the ruler of Sri Vijaya
Empire of Malay peninsula in the 11th century AD. In
order to remove any obstacles for trading with China,
he also conquered Kedah and a number of other places
in Malay peninsula and Sumatra.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the military campaign of Rajendra Chola in the North India.

India.
Rajendra Chola led his army across Kalinga to Bengal in
which the Chola armies crossed the Ganga. It took place
in 1022 AD and followed the same route which the great
conqueror Samudragupta had followed.
To commemorate his victories, Rajendra Chola assumed
the title of ‘Ganga konda Chola’ (or ‘the Chola conqueror

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to administration under the Chola Empire, the ‘agraharas’ were

answerOptions.text: general assembly of villages inhabited by the peasants.

answerOptions.rationale:
Gathering or assembly of adult men in the villages
inhabited by Brahmana in Chola kingdom was called
Agraharas. In these villages, Brahmanas, most of the

measure of autonomy.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to temple architecture during the Chola Empire.
1. During the reign of Chola Empire, Dravida style of temple architecture became prominent.
2. They started the practice of installing images of kings and queens in the temples.
3. The greatest specimen of Chola temple architecture is Kailashnath temple at Kanchipuram built under the reign of Rajaraja Chola.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect with reference to temple
architecture during the Chola Empire, as an early
example of the Dravida style of temple architecture is
Kailashnath temple at Kanchipuram built by Pallava
rulers.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to state of literature during the Chola Empire.
1. One of the greatest Tamil poet Naniah enjoyed that patronage of the Chola rulers.
2. Kamban is credited with compilation of Ramayana in Tamil.
3. The age of Kamban who is placed in the second half of the 11th and early part of the 12th century is regarded as a golden age in Tamil Literature.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct with reference
to state of literature during the Chola Empire.
Kamban’s Ramayana is considered as classic in Tamil
literature. Kamban is believed to have lived at the court
of a Chola king.
The age of Kamban is placed in the second half of the
11th and the early part of the 12th century AD is
regarded as a golden age in Tamil literature.
Statement (1) is incorrect as Nanniah lived at court of a
Chalukyan king and wrote Telugu version of
Mahabharata.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following cities had served as the capital of the Chola Empire?
1. Tanjore
2. Kanchipuram
3. Gangaikonda Cholapuram
4. Nagapattinam
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Tanjore, Kanchipuram and Gangaikonda
Cholapuram served as the capitals of Chola Empire.
Founder of Chola Empire Vijayalaya had his kingdom
at Tanjore which he captured in 850 A.D. After
defeating Pallavas, they also had city of Kanchipuram
under their control and set their capital there.
Rajendra Chola I led his army North from Kalinga to
Bengal and set up his capital near mouth of Kaveri
river and named the city Gangaikonda Cholapuram, the
city of Chola conqueror of Ganga ruler.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists and choose the correct code. List I List II (Cities conquered by the (Associated Kingdoms) Chola ruler) A. Madurai 1. Chera B. Anuradhapur 2. Sri Lanka C. Trivandrum 3. Later Chalukyas D. Kalyani 4. Pandya
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.
Madurai was ruled by Pandyas of Sangam Age and was
taken by Rajaraja of Chola kingdom.
Anuradhapur was ancient capital of rulers of Sri Lanka.
It was destroyed by Chola rulers who treated their king
and queens harshly.
Trivandrum was a Chera ruling area. It lies in Kerala.
Rajaraja destroyed Chera Navy and captured this city
from them.
Kalyani was capital of Later Chalukyas. Cholas
plundered this city also.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Pampa, Ponna and Ranna were regarded as three gems of

answerOptions.rationale:
Pampa, Ponna and Ranna were regarded as three
gems of Kannada poetry. They were Jain scholars, but
they also wrote on themes taken from Mahabharata and
Ramayana. Pampa was the court poet of Chalukya king
Arikesari II. He is best known for his epic
Vikramarjuna Vijaya.
Ponna was the court poet of Rashtrakuta king Krishna
III. He is best remembered for his composition
‘Shantipurana’ written in Champu style. Ranna was the
court poet of Chalukya king Tailapa II. Ajita Purana is
considered as the most important work of Panna.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists and choose the correct code. List I List II (Temples ) (Associated dynasty) A. Brihadisvara temple at 1. Pallava Tanjore B. Kailashnatha temple at 2. Hoysala Kanchipuram C. Papanatha temple at 3. Chola Pattadakal D. Hoysalesvara temple at 4. Chalukya Halbeid
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2.
Brihadisvara temple at Tanjore was built under the
patronage of Rajaraja I of the Chola dynasty.
Kailashnatha temple at Kanchipuram was built under
the patronage of Rajasimha of Pallava dynasty. It is an
example of early Dravida style of architecture in eighth
century.
Papanatha temple at Pattadakal was built during the
eighth century. It was built under the patronage of
Chalukya rulers.
Papanatha temple this temple at Pattadakal was built
during the eighth century by the rulers of Early
Chalukya dynasty.
Hoysalesvara temple at Halbeid was built under the
patronage of king Vishnuvardhana of Hoysal dynasty.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2012)

Which among these was famous for Telugu translation of Mahabharata? 
1. Kamban 2. Kuttan
3. Nannaya 4. Tikkana
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Nannaya and Tikkana
were famous for Telugu translation of Mahabharata.
Besides these two, Yerrapragada (Errana) was also
involved in Telugu translation of Mahabharata.
Together, they translated the Mahabharata from
Sanskrit into Telugu over the period of the 11th to 14th
century AD. They were patronised by Chalukyan kings.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2015)

Which among the following kingdoms was not involved in the tripartite struggle from the eighth to the tenth century AD?

answerOptions.rationale:
Cholas were not involved in the tripartite struggle
from the eighth to the tenth century AD.
Tripartite struggle was between Pala dynasty who
dominated the Eastern India, Pratiharas who were in
Western India and Rashtrakutas who dominated the
Deccan region and areas in North and South as well.

(Chap 1, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Mains 2015)

Who was the founder of Pala dynasty?

answerOptions.rationale:
Gopala was the founder of the Pala dynasty. In
750 AD, he was elected as king by the notable men of
the areas in Eastern India, to end the anarchy
prevailing there. He was succeeded in 770 AD by his
son Dharmapala who ruled till 810 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to administration under Pala dynasty.
1. The empire consisted of areas administered directly and areas ruled over by the Vassal chiefs.
2. The directly administered territories under the Pala empires were divided into bhukti (province) and visaya (districts).
3. The governor of the provinces was called samanta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to administration under Pala dynasty. In the
Pala dynasty, the empire consisted of areas
administered directly and areas ruled by Vassal chiefs.
Areas under Vassal chiefs were mostly autonomous in
character as far as internal matters were concerned and
they had a general loyalty to kings. They paid fixed
tributes and provided troops in need.
The areas ruled over by vassals were divided into
provinces which were called bhukti and mandala or
visaya, which were districts.
Statement (3) is incorrect as the Governor of the
provinces or bhukti was called uparika.

(Chap 1, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The real founder and the greatest ruler of the Pratihara dynasty was

answerOptions.rationale:
The real founder and the greatest ruler of the
Pratihara dynasty was Mihir Bhoja.
He rebuilt the empire and by about 836 AD, he had
recovered Kannauj which was made the capital of the
Pratihara empire for almost a century.
The Gurjara Pratihara dynasty was formed by
Nagabhata I in 739 AD. He was successful in defeating
Arabs who after conquering Sindh were advancing
towards Gujarat.

1. He is credited with writing the first Kannada book on poetics.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the state of religion under Rashtrakuta, which of the following statements are correct?
1. The kings of Rashtrakuta empire were great patron of Shaivism and Vaishnavism.
2. During the reign of Rashtrakutas, Kailasha temple at Ellora was built.
3. Its rulers didn’t allow Muslim traders to settle and to preach Islam in their territory.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to the state of religion under Rashtrakuta. Rashtrakuta
rulers were tolerant of all religions. They were great
patrons of Shaivism and Vaishnavism. They also
provided patronage to Jainism. The famous rock-cut
temple of Shiva at Ellora was built by one of
Rashtrakuta kings.
Statement (3) is incorrect as Rashtrakutas allowed Muslim
traders to settle and permitted Islam to be preached in
their territory.

questions.question:
(Chap 27, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2014)

With reference to cultural history of India, the term ‘Panchayatana’ refers to

answerOptions.rationale:
With reference to cultural history of India, the
term ‘Panchayatana’ refers to a style of temple
construction.
Panchayatana denotes type of temple building wherein
chief God Shiva or any other was housed in the main
building and was accompanied by four subsidiary
shrines containing other four deities- Brahma, Ganapati,
Vishnu and Shakti.

questions.question:
(Chap 25, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to materialistic Philosophy Lokayata.
1. Charvaka was the main expounder of this school of thought.
2. This school denied the existence of any divine or supernatural agency and underlined the importance of intimate contact with the world.
3. By the fifth century AD, it overshadowed the other idealist philosophies and became popular among the masses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to materialistic Philosophy Lokayata. Charvaka was the
main expounder of Lokayata Philosophy which was
focused on materialistic nature of life. Lokayata means
ideas from lives of common people.
Charvaka was against any quest for spiritual salvation
and denied the existence of any divine or supernatural
force of nature.
He accepted only reality or existence which could be
experienced by human beings.
Statement (3) is incorrect as it was overshadowed by
other idealist philosophy and it went out of masses.

questions.question:
(Chap 25, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Philosophies) (Basic tenants) A. Samkhya Brahma is reality and everything else is unreal. B. Nyaya Salvation can be attained through meditation and physical application. C. Vedanta Knowledge can be acquired through perception, inference and hearing. D. Yoga Salvation can be attained through acquisition of knowledge.
Codes A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.
Samkhya Philosophy laid emphasis on knowledge and it
can be acquired through perception, inference and
hearing. It had a typical methods of scientific inquiry to
nature.
Nyaya meant school of analysis. It developed as a
system of logic and said salvation could be achieved
through acquisition of knowledge.
According to Vedanta School of Philosophy, Brahma is
the reality and everything else is unreal, maya. The soul
(atma) is same as Brahma.
Yoga School of Philosophy emphasised on meditation
and asanas. It also prescribed pranayama which is a
breathing exercise. According to this philosophy,
through the meditation and asanas salvation could be
attained.
