questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following ancient texts composed by Bhakti saints from South India is also referred as the fifth Veda?

answerOptions.rationale:
Tirumurai is an ancient text composed by Bhakti
saints from South India and it is also referred as the
fifth veda. It was compilation of teachings of Tamil
devotees/saints of Vishnu and Shiva- Alvar and
Nayanars.
Compilation was done in eleven volumes in early part
of 12th century.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the religious changes in Post-Gupta times.
1. The monastic organisations of the Jainas, Shaivites and Vaishnavites were divided into ranked hierarchy.
2. A new sect called Tantricism emerged in the sixth century AD and it admitted both women and shudras into its rank.
3. Tantricism was exclusively related to Buddhism and emphasised on the use of magical rituals for attaining salvation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference to
the religious changes in Post-Gupta times as the
monastic organisations of the Jainas, Shaivites,
Vaishnavites, etc., came to be divided into about five
ranks. The higher rank was occupied by the acharya,
whose coronation took place in the same manner as the
coronation of the prince. The Upadhyaya and Upasaka
occupied lower positions. Spread of Tantricism
happened in about the sixth century AD.
Tantricism admitted both women and shudras into its
ranks and laid great stress on the use of magic rituals. It
was popular in Eastern India.
Statement (3) is incorrect as tantricism permeated to
Jainism, Brahminism, worshippers of Shiva and Vishnu
and Buddhism.

questions.question:
(Chap 29, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The chief export from India in ancient times,
which later came to be known as ‘wootz’ was

answerOptions.rationale:
The Indian steel was chief export from India in
ancient times and came to be called ‘wootz’ in later
times.
No other countries in the world could manufacture
such steel swords as were made by Indian craftsmen.
The Indians were great experts in the art of making
steel. This craft was developed first in India.

questions.question:
(Chap 29, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2018)

Who among the following was the first to explain that the rotation of the Earth on its own axis account for daily rising and setting of the Sun?

answerOptions.rationale:
Among the given options, Aryabhatta was the first
to explain that the rotation of the Earth on its own axis
account for daily rising and setting of the Sun.
Aryabhatta was a fomous astronomer and one of the
finest ancient Indian mathematician. He lived during
the Gupta age and composed Aryabhatiya.

questions.question:
(Chap 29, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Aryabhatta.
1. He was one of the earliest exponents of the decimal system.
2. He formulated the rule for finding the area of a triangle.
3. He discovered the causes of solar and the lunar eclipses and correctly measured the circumference of the Earth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
regarding Aryabhatta.
Aryabhatta (476-550 AD) was one of the greatest
mathematicians of ancient world. He was one of the
earliest exponents of the decimal system.
His major work, Aryabhatiya contains topics including
arithmetic, algebra, plane and spherical trigonometry.
He also formulated the rule for finding the area of a
triangle.
In the fied of Astronomy, he discovered the causes of
solar and the lunar eclipses and correctly measured the
circumference of the Earth.

questions.question:
(Chap 29, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to science of medicine practised in ancient India, which of the following statements are correct?
1. In Sushrutasamhita, Sushruta describes the method of operating cataract, stone disease and several other ailments.
2. Charakasamhita compiled by Charaka is
considered as encyclopedia of Indian medicine.
3. Charaka is considered as the father of surgery.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference to
science of medicine practised in ancient India.
In the second century AD, India produced two famous
scholars of the Ayurveda, Sushruta and Charaka.
In the Sushrutasamhita, Sushruta explains the method
of operating cataract, stone disease and many other
diseases.
Charaka’s Charakasamhita is said to be an encyclopaedia
of Indian medicine. It describes various types of fever,
leprosy, hysteria (mirgi) and tuberculosis.
Statement (3) is incorrect as Sushruta (not charak) is
considered to be the ‘father of surgery’.

questions.question:
(Chap 29, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Indian Scholars) (Contributions) A. Kanada 1. Calculation the position of planet based on the Babylonian method. Described acute angle, obtuse B. Aryabhatta 2. angle and right angle. C. Varahamihira 3. Developed the Atomic theory. D. Apastamba 4. Moon rotated around the Earth and Earth rotated around the Sun.
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2.
Kanada (6th-4th century BC) was a philosopher of
Vaisheshika School of Philosophy. He propounded the
theory of atoms.

questions.question:
(Chap 26, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Begram and Bamiyan are important Buddhist sites constructed during ancient history. They are situated in which of the following present day countries?

answerOptions.rationale:
Begram and Bamiyan are situated in present day
Afghanistan. They are situated in the North-West of
Indian subcontinent and were famous Buddhist sites in
ancient India relics. Begram was famous for ivory work,
which was similar to Indian workmanship in Kushan
times.
Bamiyan had the distinction of possessing the tallest
Buddha statue. In Afghanistan, many statues of the
Buddha and monasteries have been discovered.

questions.question:
(Chap 26, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

In which country is the ‘Angkor Wat Temple’ complex located? (CGPSC Pre 2011)

answerOptions.rationale:
The ‘Angkor Wat Temple’ complex is located in
Kampuchea (modern Cambodia). It was built by Khmer
king Suryavarman-II in the beginning of the 12th
century AD.
It is the largest group of Hindu temples built in
dravidian style of temple architecture.
The stories of the Ramayana and Mahabharata are
narrated in the relief on the walls of the temple.

questions.question:
(Chap 26, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to temple of Angkor Wat in Cambodia.
1. The stories of the Ramayana and Mahabharata are narrated in reliefs of the walls of the temple.
2. It was constructed in medieval times by the ruler of Champa who patronised Brahmanical religion.
3. It was constructed after demolishing the earlier Buddhist structure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct with reference
to temple of Angkor Wat in Cambodia. In Indo-China,
which is at present divided into Vietnam, Cambodia
and Laos, the Indians set up two powerful kingdoms in
Kamboja and Champa.
The powerful kingdom of Kamboja, identical
with modern Cambodia was founded in the sixth
century AD. Its rulers were devotees of Shiva.
It can be compared to the best artistic achievements of
the Egyptians and Greeks.
Statement (3) is incorrect as it wasn’t constructed after
demolishing any earlier Buddhist structure.

answerOptions.rationale:

Ghazni. Alaptigin laid down the foundation of the
Ghaznavid Kingdom. He was the governor under the
Samanid dynasty of Iran. Ghazni was the capital of his
new kingdom. He was succeeded by his slave and
son-in-law, Subuktagin.
Statement (2) is incorrect because Alaptigin was Turkish
in ethnicity.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Mahmud was closely associated with the renaissance of the Iranian spirit.
2. Firdausi was the poet laureate at the court of Mahmud.
3. Mahmud proclaimed descent from the Iranian legendary king Afrasiab.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct.
Mahmud of Ghazni was the third ruler of the
Ghaznavid dynasty. He ascended to throne in 998 AD
at the age of 27. He was the first Turk ruler to be
known as Sultan.
He proclaimed descent from the Iranian legendry king
Afrasiab. He was closely associated with the
renaissance of the Iranian spirit. Firdausi, the poet
laureate at the court of Mahmud, was the author of
Shahnama.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2004)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct code. Assertion
Mahmud Ghazni invaded India seventeen times. Reason (R) He wanted to establish permanent Muslim empire in India. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
answerOptions.rationale:
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Mahmud Ghazni invaded India seventeen times
during 999 AD to 1027 AD.

answerOptions.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following pairs is/are incorrectly
matched? List I List II (Expedition of Mahmud Ghaznavi) (Year)
1. Waihind 1008-09 AD
2. Kannauj 1025 AD
3. Somnath 1026 AD
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Pairs (2) and (3) are incorrectly matched because
Kannauj (in present day Uttar Pradesh) was attacked by
Mahmud Ghaznavi in the year 1018-19 AD. During this
raid, he also attacked Mathura.
Kannauj and Mathura were part of the territory ruled by
Pratihar Rajyapal. Somnath temple in Gujarat was
attacked by him in the year 1025 AD. It was under the
rule of Chalukyan ruler Bhima I. Mahmud Ghaznavi
took away booty of 20 million dinars.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which among the following statements is incorrect in the context of Al-Biruni?

answerOptions.text: He came into service of Mahmud when Mahmud Ghaznavi invaded Khwarizm.
His literary work was influenced by Indian scholar of that time.
He was against the study of Indian literature.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (d) is incorrect in the context of
Al-Biruni as he was not against the study of Indian
literature. He is considered as the founder of Indology.
He was an impartial writer on the customs and creeds
of different nations. He was well-versed in several
languages such as Syrian, Arabic, Persian, Hebrew,
Sanskrit, etc.
Al-Biruni was born in 973 AD, in Khwarizm in present
day Uzbekistan. In 1017 AD, when Sultan Mahmud
invaded Khwarizm, he took several scholars and poets
back to his capital, Ghazni, he was one of them.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Kitab-ul-Hind.
1. It was written by Al-Biruni in Arabic language.
2. It covered only religion and philosophy.
3. He adopted a distinctive structure in each chapter, beginning with a question, following this up with a description based on Sanskrit traditions.
Which of the statements given below is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to the
Kitab-ul-Hind because Kitab-ul-Hind is divided into
80 chapters on subjects such as religion and
philosophy, festivals, astronomy, alchemy, manners
and customs, social life, weights and measures,
iconography, laws and metrology.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2002)

The first Muslim who studied Puranas was

answerOptions.rationale:
The first Muslim who studied Puranas was
Al-Biruni. He was not only historian but also took keen
interest in the wide level of subjects.
Besides Puranas, he also studied Vedas, the Bhagwad
Gita, Patanjali, the Manusmriti etc. He also translated
Patanjali’s Yoga sutra into Arabic.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Battle of Tarain.
1. The first battle of Tarain was fought between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj.
2. In the first battle, Prithviraj was defeated by the Muhammad Ghori.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) is correct with reference to the
Battle of Tarain. The Battle of Tarain is considered as a
watershed moment in the history of India. Two battles
were fought at Tarain in the year 1191 and 1192,
respectively. Both the battles were fought between
Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj.
Statement (2) is incorrect because in the first battle,
(1191 AD) Prithviraj emerged as victorious and he
repulsed Muhammad Ghori.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following rulers had defeated Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj in different battles, however, Qutb-ud-Din Aibak was successful in defeating him?

answerOptions.rationale:
Bhima II was the ruler of the Chalukya (also
known as Solanki) dynasty. He ruled over present day
Gujarat. In 1178 AD, the Ghurid king Muhammad
Ghori invaded the Chalukya kingdom, but was defeated
in the Battle of Kayadara. He also defeated Prithviraj
and forced him to turn his attention towards the Punjab
and the Ganga valley. However, Qutb-ud-Din Aibak
was successful in defeating him in the year 1197 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Bakhtiyar Khalji.
1. He attacked and destroyed famous monasteries like Nalanda and Vikramshila.
2. He established Lakhnauti as his capital in North Bihar.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with reference to the
Bakhtiyar Khalji. He was one of the generals of
Muhammad Ghori. He was appointed as Governor of
Bihar and Bengal by Muhammad Ghori. He attacked
Bihar in 1197 AD and Bengal in 1202 AD.
He attacked and destroyed famous monasteries like
Nalanda and Vikramshila because of his radical Islamic
ideology.
Statement (2) is incorrect because he established
Lakhnauti as his capital in North Bengal.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2003)

How did sultan Qutb-ud-Din Aibak die?

answerOptions.text: He was treacherously stabbed to death by one of his ambitious nobles.
He was killed in a battle with Taj-al-Din Yildiz the ruler of Ghazni, who entered into a contest with him over the capture of Punjab.
He sustained injuries while besieging the fortress of Kalinjar in Bundelkhand and succumbed to them later.
He died after a fall from his horse while playing chaugan.
answerOptions.rationale:
In 1210 AD, Qutb-ud-Din Aibak died of injuries
received in a fall from his horse while playing chaugan
(Polo).
He was the slave of Muhammad Ghori and helped in
expansion of Turkish sultanate in India. After his death,
he was succeeded by his son-in-law Iltutmish, who
defeated his son Aram Shah.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The position or authority of Qutb-ud-Din Aibak was challenged by whom among the following?
1. Muizz-ud-din 2. Illtutmish
3. Yalduz 4. Sher Khan
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The position or authority of Qutb-ud-Din Aibak
was challenged by Yalduz. Qutb-ud-Din Aibak and
Yalduz were the slaves of Muiz-ud-Din or Mohammad
Ghori. Qutb-ud-Din Aibak succeeded in Delhi as
Sultan. On the other hand, the another slave of
Mohammad Ghori, Yalduz succeeded at Ghazni.
As the ruler of Ghazni, Yalduz claimed to rule over
Delhi as well. It was unacceptable for Aibak, who
discontinued its links with Ghazni.
It also enabled the Delhi Sultanate to develop on its
own independent lines, without depending on countries
outside India.

(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. Iltutmish was the son-in-law of Qutb-ud-Din

2. At the time of his accession, Qubacha, declared

3. His accession was not accepted by some of the

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
(a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct with regard to Iltutmish?
1. He established Delhi as the capital of the Slave dynasty.
2. He was successful in defeating Chalukya ruler of Gujarat.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with regard to Iltutmish.
He succeeded to throne in 1210 AD. He was an Ilbari
Turk, who was associated with the Shamsi dynasty.
After becoming Sultan, he established Delhi as the
capital of the Slave dynasty because nobles in Lahore
were against his accession. He received the title of Sultan
by Caliph of Baghdad in 1229 AD and was also known as
‘slave of a slave’.
Statement (2) is incorrect because he was not successful
in defeating Chalukya ruler of Gujarat. His expedition
against Chalukya ruler was a failure.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

What was the main reason behind the refusal of request of Jalaluddin for asylum by Iltutmish?

answerOptions.text: He had earlier defeated Iltutmish in a battle.
Iltutmish was busy in consolidation of his Sultanate.
He was being chased by Mongol ruler Genghis Khan.
answerOptions.rationale:
The main reason behind the refusal of request of
Jalaluddin for asylum by Iltutmish was that he was being
chased by Mongol ruler Genghis Khan.
Khwarizmi Empire was contemporary of Slave dynasty,
It was ruled by king Jalaluddin. He was attacked by
Mongol ruler Chengez Khan and defeated by him. Then,
he requested Iltutmish to give him refuge, which was
denied by him. In this way, Iltutmish was able to save
his Sultanate from Mongols’ invasion by denying refuge
to Jalaluddin.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding Razia Sultan.
1. She received support from the nobles.
2. Under her reign, Gujarat was subdued under Delhi Sultanate.
3. She was captured by the Altunia on the orders of rebellion of her brother.
4. She was killed in battle against her brother Muiz-ud-din Bahram, who crowned himself as a king.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (4) are incorrect regarding
Razia Sultan.
Razia Sultan was nominated as the ruler by Iltutmish
as his sons were not worthy. Turkish nobles wanted her
to be puppet in their hands but she discarded them.
She even gave up the female apparel and started
holding court with her face unveiled. This led them to
accuse her of violating feminine modesty and hence,
did not support her.
She was killed by bandits when she was on her way to
recapture Delhi. Under her reign, Gujarat was not
subdued under Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Razia Sultan.
1. Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi revolted against her.
2. Her friendship with Abyssinian Noble, Yakut Khan was one the reasons for hatred to nobles towards her.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Neither statement (1) nor (2) is incorrect with
reference to Razia Sultan. Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi was
the wazir of Razia Sultan. He had opposed her
elevation to the throne. Thus, he backed and
supported a rebellion of nobles against her. But, he
was defeated and forced to flee.
Nobles also hated her because she gave importance
and preference to Abyssinian Noble, Yakut Khan.
She appointed him to an office of the Amir-i-Akhur
(master of the horse). Yakut was later killed by
rebellion.

questions.question:
(Chap-6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The real name of Balban was the Ulugh Khan.
2. He held the position of Naib or deputy to Nasiruddin Mahmud, a younger son of Iltutmish.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct. 13.
The real name of Balban was Ulugh Khan. He was
Turkish chief, known in history by his later title of
Balban. He gradually arrogated all power to himself,
and finally ascended the throne in 1265 AD.
During the earlier period, Balban held the position of
Naib or deputy to Nasiruddin Mahmud, a younger son
of Iltutmish. He had helped him in securing the
throne in 1246 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following policies or initiatives was/were not taken by Balban?

answerOptions.text: He introduced practice of Sijada and Paibos.
He started celebration of Persian festival Nauroz.
He allowed women’s recruitment in army.
answerOptions.rationale:
Balban did not allow women’s recruitment in
army.
Statements (a), (b) and (c) are the policies or initiatives
taken by Balban. During his reign from 1275 to 1286
AD, Balban had taken many initiatives. He introduced
the practice of Sijada and Paibos, which were a form of
salutation to the king.
He also started celebration of Persian festival Nauroz in
the court for the first time. He launched many campaign
against Mongols as they wanted to bring Delhi under
their control.

(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

clearly put forward the view that the state should
be based on the willing support of the governed.
2. He also tried to gain the goodwill of the nobility by
following policy of tolerance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
(a) Only 1 (b) Only 2
(c) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2

reference to Jalaluddin Khalji. He ascended the throne

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2011)

Who was the ruler of Devagiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion?

answerOptions.rationale:
Ramchandra Dev was the ruler of Devagiri at
the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion. During the
invasion, Ramchandra Dev, the ruler of Devagiri,
promised to pay an yearly tribute to Delhi, but he
failed to pay.
Therefore, in 1306-07 AD, he sent an army in the
leadership of his slave, Malik Kafur.
Later Rai Ramchandra Dev surrendered to Kafur and
was honourably treated and carried to Delhi, where he
was restored to his dominions with the title of Rai
Rayan.

questions.question:
(Chap-7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Alauddin Khalji constructed a new garrison town named Siri for his soldiers. What was the main reason behind the establishment of this garrison?

answerOptions.text: To fight with the Mongol invaders
answerOptions.rationale:
Alauddin Khalji constructed a new garrison town
named Siri (1297-1307 AD) for his soldiers. The main
reason behind the establishment of this garrison was to
fight with the Mongol invaders.
During Alauddin reign, Mongols invaded frequently
and posed a great threat to the Sultanate.

(Chap-7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. Alauddin came to the throne by treacherously
murdering his uncle, Jalaluddin Khalji.
2. His slave, Malik Kafur was killed by the palace
guards.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the expansion of Delhi Sultanate.
1. Ratan Singh was the ruler of Ranthambore.
2. He defeated Alauddin Khalji’s army which was led by Malik Kafur.
3. It is believed that Alauddin Khalji marched against Chittor for Padmini, wife of Ratan Singh.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are incorrect with reference
to the expansion of Delhi Sultanate as Ratan Singh was
the rulers of Mewar Kingdom not Ranthambore. His
capital was Chittor. In the battle against Alauddin
Khalji in 1303 AD, he was defeated and Killed.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statement is correct with regard to the campaigns of Malik Kafur?

answerOptions.text: Malik Kafur led campaign against Warangal in year 1309.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) is correct with regard to the
campaigns of Malik Kafur. Malik Kafur led military
campaign against Warangal in the 1309 AD on the
order of Alauddin Khalji. Warangal was ruled by
Kakatiya kingdom who was defeated very badly by
Malik Kafur.

answerOptions.text: In the same year, he also defeated ruler of Dwar Samudra.
After his successful campaign in South India, he was appointed as Wazir.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

What was the name of Jain saint with whom Muhammad bin Tughlaq held discussions?

answerOptions.rationale:
Muhammad bin Tughlaq held discussions with the
Jain saint Jinaprabha Suri. Tughlaq was a learned
person and he invited Jain Saint Jinaprabha Suri to
discuss on various issues related with the religious
affairs and philosophy.
He was having secular attitude towards Hinduism and
other religions. He was the first Sultan of Delhi who
participated in public celebration of Holi.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Arrange the following programmes of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in their chronological orders.
1. Transfer of capital
2. Increase in taxation in doab
3. Promulgation of token currency
4. Khurasan expedition
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct chronology of Muhammad bin
Tughlaq’s initiatives is as follows; Increase in Taxation in
Doab, Transfer of Capital, Promulgation of Token
currency, Khurasan Expedition.
After ascending the throne in 1325 AD, his first major
initiative was to increase the taxation in Doab region of
North India in (1326 AD). His next main initiative was to
transfer capital from Delhi to Deogir in 1327 AD.
He then promulgated Token currency in 1329 AD. He
launched Khurasan expedition in 1329 AD to occupy
Khurasan and Iraq.

questions.question:
(Chap-8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Sultans of which dynasty ruled the country for the longest period? (UP Lower Sub Pre 2008)

answerOptions.rationale:
In the given options, Tughlaq dynasty (1320-1412
AD) ruled the country for the longest period.
The Sultans of Slave dynasty ruled from 1206-1290 AD.
The Sultans of Lodi dynasty ruled from 1451 to 1526
AD. The Sultans of Khalji dynasty ruled from 1290
to 1320 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Timur Lang.
1. He invaded India during the reign of Nasiruddin Tughlaq.
2. After defeating Delhi Sultan, he established Timurid dynasty which ruled for short period of time.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is incorrect with reference to Timur
Lang. He was from Turk-Mongol ethnicity. He was the
ruler and founder of the Timurid Empire. His Empire
was spread in the region of Central and West Asia. He
did not established Timurid dynasty in India.
Sayyid and Lodi Dynasty

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the Afghan rulers to the throne of Delhi?

answerOptions.text: Sikandar Shah, Ibrahim Lodi, Bahlul Khan Lodi
Sikandar Shah, Bahlul Khan Lodi, Ibrahim Lodi
Bahlul Khan Lodi, Sikandar Shah, Ibrahim Lodi
answerOptions.rationale:
The correct chronological order of the Afghan
rulers to the throne of Delhi is as follows
Bahlul Khan Lodi, Sikandar Shah, Ibrahim Lodi.
Bahlul Lodi (1451-1489 AD) was the founder of Lodi
dynasty in India.
Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517 AD) was son of Bahlul Lodi.
He became ruler of the Lodi dynasty after the death of
his father in 1489.
Ibrahim Lodi (1517-1526 AD) was the last Sultan of
Delhi Sultanate. He became Sultan in 1517 after the
death of his father Sikandar Lodi.
Central Administration

answerOptions.text: Bahlul Khan Lodi, Ibrahim Lodi, Sikandar Shah Lodi

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

What was/were the main reason(s) behind the introduction of market and other reforms by the Alauddin Khalji? 
1. To collect revenue for raising large army in order to check Mongol invasion.
2. To implement the principle of Sharia law over the non-Muslim population.
3. To ensure supply of cheap food grain to armed forces and common people.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Reasons mentioned in statements (1) and (3) were
responsible for the introduction of market and other
reforms by Alauddin Khalji. He reigned from 1296 to
1316 AD. He introduced many reforms during his
reign.
One among them was market reform. The main
objectives behind the market reform were to collect
revenue to raise large army in order to check Mongol
invasion and ensure supply of cheap food grain to armed
forces and common people.
Statement (2) is incorrect because reforms did not aim at
implementing the principle of Sharia law over the
non-Muslim population.

questions.question:
(Chap-8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2019)

Consider the following statements. 
1. In the revenue administration of Delhi Sultanate, the in-charge of revenue collection was known as Amil.
2. The Iqta system of Sultans of Delhi was an ancient indigenous institution.
3. The office of Mir Bakshi came into existence during the reign of Khalji Sultans of Delhi.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are not correct because the
Iqta system was mainly introduced by Turkis
conqueror. The holders of these offices were called
Walis or Muqtis. It was developed by Iltutmish. Thus,
it was not an ancient indigenous institution. The office
of Mir Bakshi came into existence during the reign of
Mughals. It used to head the military department.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Officer) (Assign Duty) A. Qazi 1. Supervised the accounts B. Wazir 2. Pay-master C. Mushrif 3. Chief Judge D. Bakshi 4. Supervised the work of all other officers
Codes A B C D A B C D

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Ariz-i-mamalik was Commander-in- Chief of Army.
2. The head of military department was known as Ariz-i-mamalik.
3. Ariz-i-mamalik’s responsibility included recruitment, equip and pay the army.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct. The head of
military department was known as Ariz-i-mamalik. His
responsibility included recruitment and ensuring
provisions of equipment and salary to the army.
Statement (1) is incorrect because Sultan used to be
Commander-in-Chief of Army. All other officers were
under him.
41. Consider the following statements.
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. Of all the Delhi rulers, Alauddin Khalji had the
largest standing army.
2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq paid great attention to
revenue department.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are
correct?
(a) Only 1 (b) Only 2
(c) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2
Ans. (c)

Exp. Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct.
Of all the Delhi rulers, Alauddin Khalji had the largest
standing army. The strength of his army is placed at
3,00,000 by Barani which appears to be an exaggeration.
He was also the first Sultan to pay his soldiers fully
in cash.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq paid close attention to
revenue department. Hence, he used to give more
attention to Wazir (the head of revenue department).
His Wazir Khwaja Jahan, was widely respected, and
was left in charge of capital when Muhammad bin
Tughlaq went out to deal with the rebellions.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following reform(s) was/were introduced by the Alauddin Khalji?
1. Regular muster of the armed forces
2. Branding (dagh) of the horses
3. Descriptive role of each soldier was maintained
4. Paid salaries in cash
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the reforms given in the question were
introduced by Alauddin Khalji. Alauddin Khalji
introduced many reforms in military administration to
cherish his dream of becoming Sikandar-i-Sani (Second
Alexander the Great). For this, he implemented regular
muster of the armed forces, branding (dagh) of the
horses, descriptive role of each soldier was maintained
and they were paid salaries in cash. These steps
enhanced efficiency of the army.

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:

regarding the administration under Delhi Sultanate.

kingdoms of the medieval period. Generally, the
amount of land revenue was fixed at one-third of the
total produce. However, it kept on changing under
different rulers.
Muqaddam was the hereditary headman of the villages.
They were responsible for collecting tax. They were
like zamindars. During the reign of Alauddin Khalji,
their power was curbed.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to Harihara and Bukka.
1. They were imprisoned by Muhammad bin Tughlaq and later converted to Islam by him.
2. Saint Vidyasagar inspired them to lay the foundation of Vijayanagara Empire.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with reference to Harihara
and Bukka. They were the Ministers in the Kingdom of
Kampili (modern Karnataka).
The Kampili Kingdom was attacked by Muhammad bin
Tughlaq for giving refuge to a Muslim rebel. In this
course of action, they were imprisoned and converted
to Islam by him.
Statement (2) is not correct because after a short time,
Harihara and Bukka forsook their new master and their
new faith. At the instance of their Guru Vidyaranya,
they were re-admitted to Hinduism and laid the
foundation of Vijayanagara Kingdom.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Harihara and Bukka merged Hoysala Kingdom with their empire.
2. Bukka succeeded Harihara in the year 1356 AD.
3. Under Harihara and Bukka, Vijayanagara empire was kind of cooperative society.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct.
Harihara and Bukka merged Hoysala Kingdom with
their empire. This merger was held when Hoysala ruler
was badly defeated by the Sultan of Madurai. By the
year 1346 AD, whole territory of Hoysala Kingdom
passed into the hands of Vijayanagara rulers.
Harihara was the first ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire.
He was succeeded by Bukka in the year 1356 AD who
ruled till 1377 AD. During this period, the boundaries
of empire were extended. The Sultan of Madurai and
his territory was amalgamated in the Vijayanagara
Empire.
Under Harihara and Bukka, Vijayanagara Empire was
kind of cooperative society. It means that the central
authority was weak and ruler coordinated with other
feudal chief in order to run the administration. Under
the reign of latter ruler, the cooperative society was
replaced with strong central authority.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Both the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagara Kingdom fought for the control over the Konkan region. Why Konkan region was important?
1. Being fertile, it was one of the major source of revenue for King.
2. Strategic port Goa was located in this region.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagara
Kingdom fought for the control over the Konkan region
because of its fertile land and location of Goa (strategic
port) in this region. Konkan region extends from Gulf of
Cambay in North towards the South all along the
Western seaside areas of Maharashtra and Goa and
ends in Karnataka.

questions.question:

Parmeshwara and Maharajadhiraja.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Who among the following rulers married his daughter to the Bahmani Sultan Firuz Shah?

answerOptions.rationale:
Deva Raya I married his daughter to the Bahmani

fierce battle. He also paid 10 lakhs of huns, pearls and

Deva Raya I reigned from 1404 to 1422 AD.

questions.question:

Works mentioned in statements (1) and (2) were

reign.
Statement (3) is incorrect because Deva Raya II

Deva Raya I emphasised on the modernisation of the
army.

questions.question:

Consider the following statements.

Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding Deva Raya II. Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya
II received tribute from king of Sri Lanka. Nuniz, a
Portuguese writer of 16th century tells that the Kings of
Quilon, Sri Lanka, Pulicat, Pegu and Tenasserim
(Burma and Malaya) also paid tribute to Deva Raya II.
Deva Raya II (1425 to 1446 AD) was a great elephant
hunter. Hence, he is popularly known as ‘Gajabetekara’.

Ushaparinayam and Jambavati Kalayana in Sanskrit and
Amuktamalyada in Telugu. Foreign travellers Paes and

great justice and equity prevailing in his empire.

adventurous policy to play off one Sultan against
another when Sultans understood his policy, they
joined hand together and defeated him. He was killed

(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2020)

Which famous war took place in 1565 AD?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Battle of Talikota took place in 1565 AD. It
was fought between Vijayanagara and combined forces
of Bijapur, Ahmednagar and Golconda. It is also known
as the Battle of Rakshashi-Tangadi. It was held on the
banks of river Krishna.

and the power of Vijayanagara Empire declined after
this battle.

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I (Traveller) List II (King) A. Abdur Razzaq 1. Deva Raya-I B. Nuniz 2. Deva Raya-II C. Nicolo-de-Conti 3. Krishnadeva Raya D. Barbosa 4. Achyuta Raya

Codes

answerOptions.rationale:

Vijayanagara Empire from earliest to latest is- Sangama
(1336-1485), Saluva (1485-1505) and Tuluva
(1491-1570). Hence, option (b) is the correct. Sangama
dynasty was established by the Harihara and Bukka
year in 1336 AD. Saluva dynasty was established by the

remained in power since 1570.

Empire in the South India. He belonged to Afghan
ethnicity. He reigned from 1347 to 1358 AD. Towards
the end of his reign, the kingdom stretched from the
Wainganga river to Krishna and East to West from
Bhongir to Daulatabad.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statement is incorrect in the context of Alauddin Hasan and Bahmani Kingdom?

answerOptions.text: He was also known as Hasan Gangu.
He traced his origin from mythological hero of Iran Bahman Shah.
The name of Bahmani Kingdom derived its name from Bahman Shah.
Alauddin Hasan was defeated by Deva Raya II.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Firuz Shah Bahmani,
which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. He appointed Hindus on a large scale in administration.
2. He built an observatory near Daulatabad.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the given statements (1) and (2) are correct.
Firuz Shah Bahmani reigned from 1397 to 1422 AD.
He adopted the title of Taj-ud-din Firuz Shah.
He appointed Hindus on a large scale in administration.
He built an observatory near Daulatabad. He defeated
rulers of Vijayanagara in 1389 AD and in 1408 AD.
Later, he was defeated by Deva Raya I in 1419 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following Bahmani rulers transferred his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?

answerOptions.rationale:
Ahmad Shah I transferred his capital from
Gulbarga to Bidar in 1429 AD. Bidar served as the
capital from Bahmani Kingdom till 1538 AD. Bidar was
selected as a seat of capital because of its central
location and also it was surrounded by the large tract of
fertile land.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Who among the following Prime Minister of Bahmani rulers established famous Madrasa at Bidar?

answerOptions.rationale:
Prime Minister Mahmud Gawan of Bahmani ruler
established famous Madrasa at Bidar.
The name of Madrasa was Mahmud Gawan Madrasa. It
had a large library which consisted of 3,000 manuscript.
He himself was well versed in Islamic theology, Persian
and Mathematics.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which one among the following was not a reform measure carried out by Mahmud Gawan of Bahmani Kingdom?

answerOptions.text: The Kingdom was divided into eight provinces or Tarafs.
Nobles were paid salaries and were asked to maintain contingents of horses.
A tract of land, Khalisa was set apart for the expenses of the Tarafdar.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (c) was not a reform measure carried
out by Mahmud Gawan of Bahmani Kingdom because
Khalisa land was set apart for the expenses of the Sultan
(not Tarafdar).
All the other given statements are correct.
Mahmud Gawan introduced large number of reforms in
the system to make it more efficient and corruption free.
It includes division of kingdom into eight provinces or
Tarafs, Nobles were paid salaries and were asked to
maintain contingents of horses and lands were measured
and land taxes were fixed on that basis.

answerOptions.text: Lands were measured and land taxes were fixed on that basis.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following was not one of the states formed after the disintegration of Bahmani Kingdom?
1. Ahmednagar 2. Bijapur
3. Berar 4. Warangal
5. Golconda
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Warangal was not among the states which were
formed after the disintegration of Bahmani Kingdom.
After the death of Mahmud Gawan, Bahmani Kingdom
started declining and ultimately it was disintegrated
into following five kingdoms :
Kingdom Dynasty
Ahmednagar Nizam Shahi dynasty
Bijapur Adil Shahi dynasty
Golconda Qutb Shahi dynasty
Bidar Barid Shahi dynasty
Berar Imad Shahi dynasty

questions.question:
(Chap
10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the place (s) was/were adorned as the capital by Bengal rulers?
1. Gaur 2. Murshidabad
3. Pandua
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Gaur and Pandua were adorned as the capital by
Bengal rulers. Gaur (also known as Gauda and
Lakhnauti) was the earliest capital of Bengal Kingdom.
Pandua was established as the capital by the Ilyas Khan
when he laid the foundation of Ilyas Shah dynasty. In
1450 AD, Sultan Mahmud Shah of Bengal announced
the transfer of Bengal’s capital from Pandua to Gaur.
The transfer was completed by 1453 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect in the context of Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah of Bengal Province?

answerOptions.text: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah was known for his love of justice.
Chinese emperor sent him envoy and requested him to send Buddhist monks to China.

answerOptions.rationale:
None of the statements are incorrect in the
context of the Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah of Bengal
Province. He reigned from 1389 to 1409 AD. He was
known for his love of justice.
Chinese emperor sent him envoy and requested him to
send Buddhist monks to China. He had cordial relation
with Chinese emperor. He promoted Persian literature.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The two important warring Kingdoms in North Bengal and Assam included
1. Kamata 2. Ahom
3. Sharqi 4. Malwa
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The two important warring Kingdoms in North
Bengal and Assam included Kamata and Ahom,
respectively.
Kamata Kingdom came into existence in the year 1257
AD. The last rulers of Kamata Kingdom were displaced
in 1498 AD by Alauddin Husain Shah of Bengal. The
Ahom Kingdom was established in 1228 AD by
Sukaphaa.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. During the period of Vijayanagara Empire Gajapati dynasty ruled over Orissa.
2. The capital of Gajapati Dynasty was Puri.
3. Kapilendra Deva was the founder of Gajapati Dynasty.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct. During the
period of Vijayanagara empire Gajapati dynasty ruled
over Orissa. It ruled from 1434-1541 AD. The reign of
Vijayanagara Empire was 1336-1646 AD. Thus, it was
the contemporary of Vijayanagara Empire.
Kapilendra Deva was the founder of Gajapati Dynasty.
He founded this dynasty in 1434 AD.
Statement (2) is incorrect as Cuttack was the capital of
Gajapati kingdom of Orissa.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

With reference to the Gujarat ruler Ahmad Shah I, which of the following statements is/are incorrect?
1. Ahmad Shah I is known as real founder of Kingdom of Gujarat.
2. He attacked Sidhpur, the famous Hindu temple.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Neither statement (1) nor (2) is incorrect with
reference to the Gujarat ruler Ahmad Shah I. He is
known as real founder of Kingdom of Gujarat. He was
the grandson of Zafar Khan (founder of Gujarat
Kingdom). He attacked Sidhpur, the famous Hindu
temple in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Identify the King on the basis of given description.
1. He shifted the capital from Patan to new city of Ahmedabad.
2. He also imposed a Jizyah on Hindus in Gujarat for the first time.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Ahmad Shah I of Gujarat shifted the capital from
Patan to new city of Ahmedabad. The city of
Ahmedabad was founded by him in the year 1413 AD.
He also imposed a Jizyah on Hindus in Gujarat for the
first time. He also appointed Malik Chand and Moti
Chand as ministers.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Hoshang Shah.
1. He adopted policy of religious intolerance towards Hindus.
2. He was defeated and imprisoned by Zafar Khan.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect with reference to the
Hoshang Shah because he was ruler of Malwa who
adopted policy of religious tolerance towards Hindus
and people of other religion. This is mentioned in the
inscription of the Lalitpur temple. Hoshang Shah
reigned from 1406 to 1435 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Rana Kumbha.
1. Rana Kumbha belonged to Mewar.
2. He is known for constructing Kirti Stambha.
3. He was murdered by his son Uda.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct with
reference to Rana Kumbha. He belonged to Mewar. He
is known for constructing Kirti Stambha at Chittor after

He was murdered by his son Uda in the greed of throne.
Uda was removed by Maharana Raimal (another son of
Rana Kumbha).
56. Rana Sanga defeated Sultan Ibrahim Lodi in,

(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Ans. (a)

Exp. Rana Sanga of Mewar defeated Sultan Ibrahim

Delhi Sultanate. Sultan was defeated very easily and in

by a sword cut and an arrow also hit him in the leg
which made him lame for rest of the life.

known as Zafar. He proclaimed himself an independent

Which one of the following places was known as ‘Shiraz of East’ during the regime of Sharqi rulers?

answerOptions.rationale:
Jaunpur was known as the ‘Shiraz of East’ during

questions.question:

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which among the following Ruler abolished Jizya first time? (UK UDA Mains 2006)

answerOptions.rationale:
Zain-ul-Abidin, a Kashmiri ruler abolished Jizya
first time. He was a learned and tolerant ruler. He is
still called Badshah (the Great Sultan) by the
Kashmiris. He also unified the Kashmiri Kingdom. He
was also a great builder and fostered many crafts in
Kashmir, such as stone cutting, bottle making, gold
bearing etc.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement is correct in the context of Babur?

answerOptions.text: He succeeded the throne of Ferghana, when he was only 11 years old.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is correct in context of Babur. Umar
Shaikh Mirza was the ruler of Ferghana and father of
Babur. Due to sudden death of his father, Babur
succeeded the throne at the age of 11.
Statements (b), (c) and (d) are incorrect. He defeated
Sultan Ibrahim Lodi of Delhi at Panipat in 1526 AD
and founded Mughal Empire in India. He did not
capture Jaipur in 1526 AD.
He was forced to leave Ferghana due to frequent
invasion of Turk group. The Uzbeks under the
leadership of the Shaibani Khan captured Ferghana.
He ruled in India for about four years (1526 AD -
1530 AD).

answerOptions.text: In 1526, he defeated the Sultan of Delhi, Sikandar Lodi at Panipat and captured Delhi and Jaipur.
He was forced to leave Ferghana due to the invasion of Arab group, the Uzbeks.
He ruled over India for 10 years and consolidated his Empire in India.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Who among the following defeated Babur in the Battle of Sar-e-pul? (UP Lower pre 2015)

answerOptions.rationale:
Shaibani Khan defeated Babur in the Battle of
Sar-e-pul. Shaibani Khan also known as Shahi Beg
Khan, was an Uzbek leader. He was the descendant of
Shaiban, the fifth son of Jochi (Genghis Khan’s
eldest son).

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following pairs regarding the military campaigns of Babur. Year Campaigns
1. 1524 AD Captured Lahore
2. 1527 AD Defeated the Rajputs at Chanderi
3. 1528 AD Defeated Rana Sanga, Rajput rulers and allies at Khanwa.
Which of the above pairs is/are incorrectly
matched?

answerOptions.rationale:
Pairs (2) and (3) are incorrectly matched as Babur
defeated the Rajput forces led by Rana Sanga at
Khanwa in 1527 AD (not 1528 AD). In the next year
(1528 AD), the Battle of Chanderi was fought between
the Rajput ruler Medini Rai and the Babur. In this
battle, Babur emerged victorious.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-VI, NCERT)

The Empire of Babur included the areas of (UKPSC Pre 2003)
1. Kabul 2. Punjab
3. modern Uttar Pradesh 4. modern Rajasthan
Which of the option given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Mughal Empire during the reign of Babur
included modern day territories of Kabul, Punjab, and
Delhi and Gangetic plain of Uttar Pradesh. Except
Kabul, these territories were annexed by Babur after
defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the third battle of Panipat
(1526 AD). In the subsequent battles (at Khanwa and
Chanderi) he was able to consolidate his control over
parts of Eastern Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.
While territories encompassing modern Rajasthan
came under full control of the Mughals during the reign
of Jahangir in 1615 AD.
8. Consider the following statements.
(Chap 6, Class-VII, Old NCERT)
1. Babur was a poet and writer and his mother
tongue was Persian.
2. He was always keen to make gardens in all the
places where he lived.
3. He made polo game popular amongst Indian
nobles.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are
correct?
(a) Only 1 (b) 1 and 2
(c) 2 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3
Ans. (c)

Exp.
Statements (2) and (3) are correct.
Apart from military conquest, Babur is also known for
his other talent and interests. He was always keen to
make gardens in all the places, where he lived such as in
Kabul where he created many gardens. He was also
interested in Polo game, due to him it became popular
amongst Indian nobles.
Statement (1) is incorrect because Babur was a excellent
poet and writer and his mother tongue was Turkish. His
memoir Tujuk-e-Babri was written by him in Turkish
language.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

From the following names, identify the one who was not the brother of Humayun.
1. Kamran 2. Usman
3. Askari 4. Hindal
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Usman was not the brother of Humayun. Babur
had four sons namely Humayun, Kamran, Askari and
Hindal. Humayun was eldest among them. He
succeeded the throne after his death till 1530 AD. He
reigned from 1530 to 1540 AD and again from 1555 to
1556 AD. Kabul and Qandhar were under the charge of
Humayun’s younger brother, Kamran.

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:

Humayun marched against him but he was defeated by

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Humayun during his short reign carried out many military expeditions. In this context, which of the following was/were captured by him?
1. Gujarat
2. Golconda
3. Malwa
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Humayun launched many military expeditions to
expand the territory of his Empire.
He marched against the Gujarat, which was ruled by
Bahadur Shah and defeated him. He was also able to
defeat ruler of Malwa. He did not launch any military
expedition to capture Golconda.
13. Which of the following is the correct chronology
of battles, fought by Humayun?
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Chausa, Kannauj, Sirhind
(b) Kannauj, Chausa, Sirhind
(c) Sirhind, Chausa, Kannauj
(d) Chausa, Kannauj, Sirhind
Ans. (d)

Exp. The correct chronology of battles given in the
question is as follows ; Chausa, Kannauj and Sirhind.
Battle of Chausa was fought in the year 1539 AD
between Sher Khan (Sher Shah Suri) and Humayun at
place called Chausa in Bihar. Humanyun was defeated
very badly.
Battle of Kannauj was fought in the year 1540 AD.
Humayun again launched military expedition against
Sher Khan to take his revenge. A battle was fought at
Kannauj (Uttar Pradesh). Again, Humayun was
defeated. This battle marked the end of Mughal rule in
India. It was replaced by the Suri dynasty.
Battle of Sirhind was fought in 1555 AD. In this battle
Sikandar Shah Suri (the ten ruler of Sur Dynasty) was
defeated and Mughal dynasty was restorted .

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

When Humayun was engaged in establishing law and order in Gaur (Capital of Bengal), who among the following declared himself as the ruler of Agra?

answerOptions.rationale:
When Humayun was engaged in establishing Law
and Order in Gaur (Capital of Bengal), his brother
Hindal declared himself as the ruler of Agra. This step
was taken by Hindal after being provocated by the
nobles. Later, he pleged allegience to Humayun. He
died in 1551 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

What was/were the main reason(s) behind the establishment of a new city, of Delhi by Humayun, which he named Dinpanah?
1. It can serve as a second capital.
2. Agra was under constant threat due to rising power of the Bahadur Shah.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the given statements (1) and (2) were reasons
behind establishing Delhi. Humayun is credited for the
establishment of a new city of Delhi, named Dinpanah.
The reason for its establishment is to create another
seat of capital, as Agra was under constant threat due to
rising power of the Bahadur Shah and Delhi will also
serve as second capital.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct
with reference to Sher Shah?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is correct with reference to Sher
Shah. In 1540 AD, Suri dynasty was established by the
Sher Shah. His real name was Farid.
Statement (b) is incorrect because he was the son of
Hasan Khan, who was the small Jagirdar at Sasaram
(Bihar). He received the title Sher Khan by Bahar Khan
Lahori (Governor of Bihar).

answerOptions.text: He was the son of nobleman, who had a small estate under the rulers of Jaunpur.

questions.question:
(Chap 12, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

The Battle of Sammel in 1544 AD was fought between, which of the entities?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Battle of Sammel was fought between
Sher Khan ( Sher Shah Suri) and Maldeo Rathore in
1544 AD. In this battle the Rajput forces under their
commander Jaita and Kumpa fought against the Afghan
forces of Sher Shah Suri.
Ultimately, Sher Shah emerged victorious, but several
of his generals lost their lives and his army suffered
heavy losses.
Commenting on the bravery of the Rajput forces, Sher
Shah after this battle exclaimed that, “for a handful of
millet, I almost lost the Empire of Hindustan”.

questions.question:
(Chap 14, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Chand Bibi ruled over the Ahmednagar as a regent.
2. She accepted Mughal suzerainty in the year 1596 AD.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct.

and defeated her. She accepted the Mughal suzerainty
in the year 1596 AD. She also ceded Berar to Mughals
in return of their recognition of the claim of Bahadur as
a ruler of Ahmednagar. She also acted as a regent of
Bijapur.

questions.question:

questions.question:
(Chap 18, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. In the war of succession, Aurangzeb had defeated Shuja at Khajwah near Allahabad (now Prayagraj).
2. The battle of Deorai near Ajmer was the last major battle that Dara fought against Aurangzeb.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct.
Aurangzeb had defeated Shuja at Khajwah near
Allahabad (now Prayagraj) in the war of succession, in
December 1658 AD. Shuja was hounded out of India
into Arakan (April 1660 AD). Soon, he and his family
was executed by Arakanese on a charge of fomenting
rebellion.
The battle of Deorai near Ajmer (March 1659 AD) was
the last major battle that Dara fought against Aurangzeb.
In this battle, Dara Shikoh was defeated.

Consider the following pairs. Soil Type Description

2. Chachar Fallow for 3-4 years
3. Banjar Fallow for longer period of time
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?

answerOptions.rationale:
Pairs (2) and (3) are correctly matched. Under the
reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar, land was divided into
different categories on the basis of their productivity.
The division is as follows
Polaj – It was land cultivated every year.
Parati – It was land cultivated once in 2 year
Chachar – It was land allowed to be fallow for 3-4 years.
Banjar – It was worst kind of land and was left fallow for
longer period of time.
