A common feature to all the Bhakti saints was that
they composed of their verses in the languages
(generally vernacular language) understood by their
followers. Bhakti saints belonged from different region
and their time period was also different.
They also encouraged universal brotherhood and
denied caste system. They also emphasised on the
concept of the self-surrender to God without being
dependent over the mediatory.

answerOptions.text: rejected the authority of the priestly class.
encouraged women to go to the temples.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the Bhakti saint Chaitanya?
1. He popularised the Krishna Cult in Bengal.
2. He believes that through love and devotion, song and dance, a devotee can feel the presence of God.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding the Bhakti saint Chaitanya.
Bhakti saint Chaitanya popularised the Krishna Cult in
Bengal. He believes that through love and devotion,
song and dance, a devotee can feel the presence of God.
His system of songs and dance by several people in a
group is known as sankirtan/kirtan system. He accepted
disciples from all classes and castes.
One of the most important things about him was that he
did not rejected the scriptures and idol worship.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Kabir.
1. His collection of verses is called sakhis and pads.
2. His verses are preserved in the Guru Granth Sahib.
3. He belonged to community of fishermen.
4. Kabir believed in a formless Supreme God.
Which of the statement(s) given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct regarding
Kabir. He was one of the most famous disciples of
Ramananda. His collection of verses is called sakhis and
pads. His verses are preserved in the Guru Granth
Sahib. He was a popular Nirguna saint (believed in a
formless Supreme God).
Statement (3) is incorrect as Kabir was brought up in a
family of Muslim Julahas or Weavers settled in or near
the city of Varanasi (Banaras).

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which one of the following statements about the teachings of Kabir is incorrect?

answerOptions.text: He was not against pilgrimage and idol worship.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is incorrect regarding the teachings
of Kabir. Kabir was a renowned Nirguna saint
therefore, he was against the pilgrimage and idol
worship.

answerOptions.text: He emphasised on one God and the spread of devotionalism.
He did not consider it necessary to abandon the normal life of a householder.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is/are correct
with reference to the Tulsidas?
1. He conceived of God in the form of Krishna.
2. His composition the Ramcharitmanas was written in Braj language.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements are incorrect regarding
Tulsidas. Tulsidas was born in 1511 in a Brahmana
family in Uttar Pradesh. He was a Saguna saint.
He conceived of God in the form of Rama. His
composition the Ramcharitmanas was written in Awadhi
language. The other important literary of his includes
Gitawali, Vinaya Patrika etc.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Surdas was one of the important Bhakti saints. His composition included
1. Bijak
2. Surasaravali
3. Sahitya Lahiri
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Surdas was one of the important Bhakti saints of
Krishna or Vaishnava Cult. His composition include
Surasaravali, Sur Sagar and Sahitya Lahiri. He was born
in 1478 AD in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. He was disciple of
Vallabhacharya. He was a blind. He was contemporary
to the Mughal emperor Akbar. Bijak was not his
composition as it was compiled by Kabir.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Who among the following was not contemporary of Surdas?

answerOptions.rationale:
Namdev was not contemporary of the Surdas. The
time period of Surdas was from 1478 to 1573 AD.
Namdeva was Bhakti saint from Maharashtra. His time
period was from 1270 to 1350 AD. He was tailor by
profession who was also involved in social evils like
banditry. He laid the foundation of new sect named
Varakari sect.
Mirabai, Shankaradeva and Dadu Dayal were
contemporary of Surdas. Dadu Dayal was Nirguna
saint. He was born in a Muslim family but brought up
by a Hindu Family. He was from Gujarat.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements regarding Shankaradeva.
1. He was responsible for the introduction of Bhakti Movement in Assam.
2. He composed poems and plays in Bengali.
3. He began the practice of setting up namghars.
Which of the statement(s) given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct regarding
Shankaradeva. Shankaradeva was responsible for the
introduction of Bhakti Movement in Assam. He was the
follower of Vaishnavism. He was the leading proponent
of spreading the ideas of Bhagavad Gita. He began the
practice of setting up namghars or satra, type of
monasteries. Ekasarana Dharma was founded by him.
Statement (2) is incorrect because he composed poems
and plays in Assamese language.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statements is incorrect in the context of Mirabai?

answerOptions.text: She was a Rajput princess married into the royal family of Mewar.
She was a disciple of Saint Dadu.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect in the context of Mirabai
as she was a disciple of Saint Raidas who was a leather
worker. Mirabai (15th-16th centuries AD) was a
renowned Saguna saint from Rajasthan. She was born
in a princely Rajput family and married to Bhoj Raja,
who was the son of Rana Sanga of Mewar. She was a
devotee of Lord Krishna. Bhajan written by her for
Lord Krishna are known as Padavali.

answerOptions.text: She was a devotee of Lord Krishna.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Jnaneshvara.
1. He preached bhakti in Maharashtra.
2. He wrote a commentary on Bhagavad Gita in Marathi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to Jnaneshvara. He was a Bhakti saint from
Maharashtra. His time period was from 1275 to 1296
AD. He wrote a commentary of Bhagavad Gita called
Jnaneswari. His other important work includes
Changdev Prasasti and Amrit Anubhava. He was
associated with the Krishnamargi sect.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Bhakti saint Vallabha was a renowned follower of Vedantist philosophy.
2. He was a Tailang Brahmana.
3. He was not contemporary of the saint Jnaneshvara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct as
Vallabhacharya was an important Bhakti saint who
followed Vedantist philosophy. He was born in Banaras
in a Telugu Tailang Brahmana family. His time period
was from (1479-1531 AD). He propounded the
philosophy of Shuddhadvaita. He founded Pustimarga.
He also founded Rudra Sampradaya.
Statement (3) is incorrect because he was contemporary
of the saint Jnaneshvara.
28. Which of the following Bhakti saints is not
matched correctly with the modern state to,
which he belonged?
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Shankaradeva – Assam (b) Kabir – Uttar Pradesh
(c) Narsi Mehta – Gujarat (d) Tukaram – Bengal
Ans. (d)

Exp. Pair (d) is not correctly matched as Tukaram was
Bhakti saint from Maharashtra (not Bengal). He was
born in 1608 at Pune. He was a Nirguna saint. He was a
devotee of Vithoba or Vitthala, incarnation of Lord
Vishnu. He laid emphasis on community-based worship
with spiritual songs called Kirtans. He wrote abhangas
in Marathi language.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2001)

Match the following lists and choose the correct code. , List I List II (Bhakti Saints) (Profession) A. Namdev 1. Barber B. Kabir 2. Weaver C. Ravidas/Raidas 3. Tailor D. Sena 4. Cobbler
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-3, B-2, C-4, D-1.
Namdev was a tailor by profession.
Namdev (1270-1350 AD) was a Bhakti Saint from
Maharashtra. He was devotee of Lord Vitthal of
Pandher Pura.
Kabir was a weaver by profession. Kabir (1398-
1518 AD) was a renowned Nirguna Saint. He was
against Pilgrimage and Idol worship.
Ravidas or Raidas was a cobbler by profession. He was
born in 1450 at Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh).
Sena was a barber by profession. He worshipped
Vithoba or Vitthala, incarnation of Lord Vishnu.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Guru Nanak
1. He was born at Talwandi, which is located in Punjab province of Pakistan.
2. The sacred space created by Baba Guru Nanak for community kitchen is known as dharmsala.
3. Guru Angad compiled the teaching of Baba Guru Nanak.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct with reference
to Guru Nanak. He was the founder of the Sikh
religion. He was born in 1469 AD at Talwandi, which is
now located in Punjab province of Pakistan. He was a
Nirguna saint. Guru Angad (Second Sikh Guru)
compiled the teaching of Baba Guru Nanak.
Statement (2) is incorrect because the sacred space
created by Baba Guru Nanak for community kitchen is
known as Langar.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the teachings and principles of Guru Nanak .
1. He wanted to establish a new religion by denouncing Hinduism.
2. He advocated a middle path in which spiritual life could be combined with the duties of the householder.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct with reference to the
teachings and principles of Guru Nanak. He was the
first Guru of Sikh. He advocated a middle path in
which spiritual life could be combined with the duties
of the householder. He preached about the unity of
God. He criticised idol-worship, pilgrimages and other
tradition and rituals.
Statement (1) is incorrect because he did not want to
establish a new religion by denouncing Hinduism.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

In the sacred text of the Sikh, Guru Granth Sahib the verses of, which among the following saints was/were included?
1. Shaikh Farid 2. Saint Kabir
3. Namdev 4. Guru Teg Bahadur
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
In the sacred text of the sikh, Guru Granth Sahib
the verses of Shaikh Farid, Saint Kabir, Namdev and
Guru Teg Bahadur. The Adi Granth, its first rendition,
was compiled by the fifth guru, Guru Arjan (1564–1606
AD). The Guru Granth Sahib is written in the
Gurumukhi script. Besides the teaching of these saints
and Gurus, the teachings of Ramananda and five more
Sikh Gurus namely, Guru Nanak, Guru Angad, Guru
Aman Das, Guru Ram Das, Guru Arjan have also been
included.
Sufi Movement

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Sufism.
1. Most Sufi silsilas were named after a founding figure.
2. The Qadiri order was named after Shaikh Nasriuddin Wahab Jilani.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct with reference to the
Sufism. It was the liberal movement in the Islam. It
rejected rituals, orthodoxy and unscientific traditions.
Most Sufi lineages were named after a founding figure.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following statement is incorrect
with reference to the Abu’l Hasan al Hujwiri?

answerOptions.text: He settled in Lahore and wrote a book in Persian called the Kashful-Mahjub.
He was forced to cross the Indus as a captive of the invading Arab army.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (b) is incorrect regarding Abu’l
Hasan al Hujwiri as in 1039 AD, he was forced to
cross the Indus as a captive of the invading Turkish
army.
Abu’l Hasan al Hujwiri was a native of Hujwir near
Ghazni in Afghanistan. He is revered as Data Ganj
Bakhsh or ‘Giver who bestows treasures’. He settled in
Lahore and wrote a book in Persian called the
Kashful-Mahjub.

answerOptions.text: He is revered as Data Ganj Bakhsh or ‘Giver who bestows treasures’.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about Sufism.
1. The most influential group of sufis in India was the Suhrawardi.
2. Sufis were organised in 15 silsilas.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are incorrect
regarding sufism. The Sufi movement in India emerged
in the 11th century AD. Abu’l Hasan al Hujwiri laid the
foundation of Sufism in India.
Over the course of period, Sufism was organised into 12
silsilas. The most influential group of sufis in India was
the Chisti not Suhrawardi. Silsilas were organised on
the basis of spiritual genealogy of Sufi teachers. They
followed a distinct method of instruction and way of
devotion to God.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-VII, Old NCERT)

Arrange the following Sufi saints in their chronological order.
1. Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi
2. Farid-ud-din Ganj-i-Shakar
3. Bakhtiyar Kaki
4. Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct chronological order of Sufi saints is
Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, Bakhtiyar Kaki,
Farid-ud-din Ganj-i-Shakar, Nasiruddin
Chiragh-i-Delhi.
Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti introduced the Chishti Silsila
in India around 1192 AD.
Bakhtiyar Kaki was disciple and spiritual successor of
Moinuddin Chishti. His base was in Delhi.
Farid-ud-din Ganj-i-Shakar was the disciple of
Bakhtiyar Kaki. He was popularly known as Baba Farid
or Shaikh Farid by people of all religions.
Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi was disciple and
spiritual successor of Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya
(1274-1337) AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Shaikh Nizamuddin’s hospice was on the bank of the river Yamuna in Ghiyaspur (Delhi).
2. He adopted the yogic breathing exercise and because of which he gained the name Sidh.
3. He belonged to Sufi silsila, which believed in an austere and a simple life.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct.
Nizamuddin Auliya was one of the important Sufi saints
of India. He was born in 1238 AD and died in 1325 AD.
His hospice was on the banks of the river Yamuna in
Ghiyaspur (Delhi).
He adopted the yogic breathing exercise and because of
which he gained the name Sidh. He believed in an
austere and a simple life. He was also popularly known
as Mahbub-e-Ilahi (Beloved of God).

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following pair is incorrectly
matched? Sufi Saint Dargahs

answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (c) is incorrectly matched because the Dargah
of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya is located in Delhi not
Lahore.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Shaikh Salim Chishti.
1. The dargah of Shaikh Salim Chishti is located in Ajmer.
2. He was a direct descendant of Baba Farid.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is incorrect with reference to
Shaikh Salim Chishti because his dargah is located in
Fatehpur Sikri, Agra Uttar Pradesh not in Ajmer. He
was highly revered by Mughal emperor Akbar. He
named his first son Salim (later emperor Jahangir) in
honour of Chishti.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2012)

With reference to the religious history of Medieval India, the Sufi mystics were known to pursue,
which of the following practices? 
1. Meditation and control of breath.
2. Severe ascetic exercise in lonely place.
3. Recitation of holy songs to arouse a state of ecstasy in their audience.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given practices were pursued by Sufi
mystics. Sufis had risen in Islam at a very early state.
These Sufi Saints helped to spread peace and harmony
in Medieval India. These Sufis turned to asceticism and
mysticism in protest against growing materialism of the
caliphate as a religious and political institution.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct code. Assertion
Many Sanskrit works on music were translated into Persian during the medieval period. Reason (R) The early Chisti Sufis were fond of musical assemblies called sama. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
answerOptions.rationale:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true,
but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of
Assertion (A).
Sufism did not only influence religious and social sphere
but was also influenced cultural sphere.
Many Sanskrit works on music were translated into
Persian during the medieval period. Rulers of Delhi
sultanate and Mughal Emperor promoted the
translation work. The early Chisti Sufis were fond of
musical assemblies called sama. It is considered as a
form of worship in Sufism.
It often includes singing, playing instruments, dancing,
recitation of poetry and prayers, wearing symbolic attire
and other rituals.

answerOptions.text: A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

In the context of the Sufism, the term ziyarat denotes

answerOptions.text: Organising musical show in the evening.
Pilgrimage to the tombs of Sufi saint.
answerOptions.rationale:
In Sufism, the term ziyarat denotes pilgrimage to
the tombs of Sufi saint. It is even popular at the present
time.
People visit the tomb of Sufi saints to get their
blessings. Fairs are also organised on the tombs of Sufi
saints.

questions.question:
(Chap 11, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Match the following lists and choose the correct code. List I List II (Sufi Terminology) (Meaning) A. Pir 1. Successor of the Sufi saint B. Murid 2. Sufi Teacher C. Wali 3. Place where Sufi saints live D. Khanquah 4. Disciple
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.
Pir refers to Sufi teacher. In Sufism, the tradition of Pir
and Murid has played a very significant role. They
provided guidance to their disciples.
Murid refers to disciple. Amir Khusrau was the famous
murid of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya.
Wali refers to successor of the Sufi saint. When a Sufi
saint died then he was succeeded by Wali.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Which of the following pair is incorrectly
matched?

answerOptions.text: Shari’a – the law governing the Muslim community

answerOptions.rationale:
Pair (c) is incorrectly matched because
Khojaki is not a Silsila of Sufism. It is a form of a
manuscript.
It was derived from the local landa script (Clipped
mercantile script) used by the linguistically
diverse community of Khojahs in the Punjab, Sind and
Gujarat.
Ulama are scholars of Islamic studies. As preservers of
this tradition, they perform various religious, judicial
and teaching functions.
The shari’a is the law governing the Muslim community.
It is based on the Quran and the Hadis.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following reason is the most prominent for the decline of Mughal Empire after the death of Aurangzeb?

answerOptions.rationale:
The decline of Mughal Empire started after the
death of Aurangzeb. The main reason behind the
decline of Mughal Empire was that the successors of
Aurangzeb were inefficient and incapable. They were
unable to keep a check on the mansabdars and the
subedars. There were many other factors which also
contributed in the decline of Mughal Empire such as
emergence of regional powers, problem of jagirs,
foreign invasions etc.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the decline of Mughal Empire.
1. Internal conflict among the nobles was responsible for the decline in the power of central authority.
2. Subedars of the subas started to behave in the independent way.
3. Marathas started to attack the North-Western boundaries of empire.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following institutions was the most important during the period of Mughals?

answerOptions.rationale:
Umra was the most important institution during
the period of Mughals. It constituted of important
nobles. Their influence over administration increased
after the death of Aurangzeb. They actively participated
in the court politics. Even many of them acted as
de-facto ruler.
11. In the context of roles of nobles in the decline of
Mughal Empire, which of the following statements
is incorrect?
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) Nobles contributed in the decline of Mughal rule.
(b) They were divided on the basis of ethnicity.
(c) Development of nationalist attitude among the
nobles.
(d) None of the above
Ans. (c)

Exp. Statement (c) is incorrect in the context of roles of
nobles in the decline of Mughal Empire as nationalist
attitude never developed among the Mughal nobles.
They were always interested in consolidating their own
power.
In the Mughal administration, the nobles were placed at
the second in hierarchy after the King. They played key
role in the policy formulation and running of the

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements about the role of administration in the decline of Mughal Empire.
1. Mughal administration was centralised in nature.
2. Under incapable ruler, central administration got weakened.
3. Wazirs were able to control the centralised administration.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct about the role of
administration in the decline of Mughal Empire.
Mughal administration was also responsible for the
decline of Empire up to a large extent. The
administration was centralised in nature.
But after the death of Aurangzeb, incapable rulers were
not able to control it and it got weakened. Mughal
administration was highly centralised and needed a
competent monarch to run it. In the absence of such
monarchs, Wazirs tried to fill the gap, but they failed.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Aurangzeb was unsuccessful in solving the problems of Maratha.
2. He gave mansab to many Maratha Sardars.
3. He was successful in creating an alliance with Deccan Kingdoms against the Marathas.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct as Aurangzeb
was quite successful in defeating and capturing Deccan
Kingdoms but he was not able to completely ruin the
Maratha power. During the period of Aurangzeb,
Marathas signed treaties with him. As a result of which,
he gave mansab to many Maratha Sardars.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

On the advice of whom of the following, Aurangzeb agreed to do formal agreement with Bijapur and Golconda?

answerOptions.rationale:
Aurangzeb agreed to do formal agreement with
Bijapur and Golconda on the advice of his son Shah
Alam. He succeeded to the throne in 1707 AD at the
old age of sixty three, and became the seventh Mughal
Emperor. He ruled for five years.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statement is incorrect in the context of role of Rajput rulers in the decline of Mughal Empire?

answerOptions.text: Differences grew between Marwar rulers and Mughal kings.
In the Deccan war, Rathore Rajput of Marwar supported Aurangzeb.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement(c) is incorrect in the context of role of
Rajput rulers in the decline of Mughal Empire as in the
Deccan war, Rathore Rajput of Marwar did not
supported Aurangzeb.
From the period of Akbar, Rajput had played key role
in the consolidation and expansion of Mughal Empire.
It was possible due to good relation between the Rajput
Nobles and Mughal Kings.
During the period of Aurangzeb, this bond was
disturbed. Differences grew between Marwar ruler and
Mughal kings as Aurangzeb had destroyed Mewar.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the role of Aurangzeb in the decline of Mughal Empire.
1. Aurangzeb was bounded by the complex situations.
2. The situations were created by him only.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to the role of Aurangzeb in the decline of
Mughal Empire.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the religious policy/policies related to Aurangzeb, led to the disintegration of Mughal empire in long term?

answerOptions.text: He tried to remain within the framework of the Islamic law.
His failure to respect the susceptibilities of his non-Muslims subjects.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the policies mentioned in the question led to
the disintegration of Mughal Empire in long term.
Aurangzeb was an orthodox in his outlook. He tried to
remain within the framework of the Islamic law.
He failed to respect the susceptibilities of his
non-Muslim subjects on many occasions.
He was the religious bigot who ordered destruction of
temples and re-imposed Jizyah on her Hindu subjects.
These policies of Aurangzeb alienated segments of the
Hindus and strengthened the hands of those section
which were opposed to the Mughal empire. This
ultimately resulted in the disintegration of Mughal
empire.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements.
1. In 1703, Aurangzeb opened negotiations with the Marathas.
2. Aurangzeb tried to capture Maratha states till his last breath.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the given statements (1) and (2) are correct.
In 1703, Aurangzeb opened negotiations with the
Marathas. He released Sahu, the son of Sambhaji. He
was given the title of raja and the Mansab of 7000.
Aurangzeb till his last breath in 1706 AD tried to
capture and annex Maratha states. However, he was not
successful and died in Aurangabad.

questions.question:
(Chap 10 Class-VII, New NCERT)  (UPPSC Mains 2008)

Who among the following was the first Nawab of Oudh?

answerOptions.rationale:
Saadat Khan was the first Nawab of Oudh. Burhan
ul Mulk Saadat Khan was appointed Subedar of Awadh

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 1999)

Who was the commander who sent by Sultan of Bijapur for repression of Shivaji in 1659 AD?

answerOptions.rationale:
The ruler of Bijapur (Adil Shah) sent a large
contingent under Afzhal Khan to repress Shivaji.
Afzhal Khan sent on invitation to Shivaji for a personal
interview, promising to get him pardoned from the
Bijapuri court. Shivaji went prepared considering
invitation a trap and murdered the Afzal Khan in
1659 AD. Shivaji order his leaderless army to capture

special objective of crushing Shivaji. When Shivaji
started re-occupying his territories of Deccan, Shaista
Khan was transferred from Bengal to Deccan.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Treaty of Purandar.

3. A mansab of 5000 was granted to his son Sambhaji.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
with reference to the Treaty of Purandar. After the
plundering of Surat by Shivaji in 1664 AD, Jai Singh of
Amber was sent by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb to
defeat Shivaji.
Jai Singh sieged the Purandar Fort, which led to sign of
Treaty of Purandar between Jai Singh and Shivaji in the
year 1665 AD. As per the Treaty, Shivaji gave 23 forts
out of 35 to Mughals. His son Sambhaji was granted a
mansab of 5000.
6. Which among the following statement(s) about
Shivaji is/are incorrect?
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
(a) On the assurance of Jai Singh, he visited Agra.
(b) With an intent to attain ‘Hindavi Swarajya’ Shivaji
met Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
(c) He did not pay much attention on the development
of trade.
(d) All of the above
Ans. (b)

Exp.
Statement (b) is incorrect about Shivaji because
Shivaji did not meet Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb with
intent to attain ‘Hindavi Swarajya’.
He visited Agra to meet the Emperor but due to
disrespect, he walked away from imperial court. On this
attitude, he was imprisoned by the Emperor. However,
he was successful in escaping.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

In which city was Shivaji captive, when he escaped from the custody of Mughals? (MPPSC Pre 2005)

answerOptions.rationale:
Shivaji was captive in Agra, when he escaped from
the custody of Mughals. Shivaji was invited by Jai Singh
to visit the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb at Agra. But the
visit proved to be a disaster as he felt insulted, when he
was kept in category of Mansabdars of 5000. He walked
off angrily and refused the royal service. As a result, he
was imprisoned by the emperor. But he escaped from
the detention in 1666 AD.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statement is correct in the context of the Shahuji?

answerOptions.text: Shahuji was given the title of Raja and the mansab of 7000.
answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (a) is correct in the context of the
Shahuji. Shahuji was the son of Sambhaji. He was
captured by Mughal forces from Satara along with his
mother. Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb wanted peace
with Marathas, therefore, he gave title of Raja and the
mansab of 7000 to Shahuji. However, Aurangzeb died
in 1707 AD.
Statement (b) is incorrect because he was released by
the Zulfiqar Khan (not Aurangzeb). Then, Shahu
reigned till 1749 AD.
11. Arrange the following Maratha rulers in the
correct chronological order.
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)
1. Shahu 2. Raja Ram 3. Sambhaji
Codes
(a) 3, 1, 2 (b) 3, 2, 1 (c) 2, 3, 1 (d) 1, 2, 3
Ans. (b)

Exp. The correct chronological order of Maratha rulers
is :
Sambhaji (1681-89 AD), Raja Ram (1689-1707 AD) and
Shahu (1707-1749 AD).
Raja Ram was the successor of Sambhaji. He reigned
from 1689 to 1707 AD. He ruled on the behalf of Shahu.
His headquarters was Jinji. He was frequently attacked
by Mughal forces, as a result of which he ran from one
place to another. He died in 1707 AD, which led to war
of succession between Tarabai (regent of her son Shivaji
II), widow of Raja Ram and Shahu. Ultimately, Shahu
emerged as victorious.

answerOptions.text: He was released by the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.

To organise religious ceremonies and to be the census of public morals.

Paga in Maratha administration was

Paga in Maratha administration was state

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the administration of Marathas.
1. Havaldars were supervised by the Sihahars.
2. Saranjam was not associated with the military administration of Marathas.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are incorrect with reference
to the administration of Marathas because Sihahars
were supervised by the Havaldars. They were part of
the auxiliary force of Maratha King.
Saranjam was associated with the military administration
of Marathas. Many Military chief were given Saranjam
(revenue grants). It was also known as Saranjami system.

questions.question:
(Chap 19, Class-XI, Old NCERT)

In the context of the revenue administration of Maratha, what was Chauth?

answerOptions.text: Irrigation tax levied by Raja Ram.
A levy on the neighbouring territories by Shivaji which was one-fourth of land revenue in lieu of protection against Maratha invasion.
answerOptions.rationale:
In the context of the revenue administration of
Maratha, Chauth was a levy on the neighbouring
territories by Shivaji, which was one-fourth of land
revenue in lieu of protection against Maratha invasion.
Sardeshmukhi was an additional levy of 10% demanded
from the areas outside from the Kingdom. Both of
these taxes were main source of income for Maratha
Kingdom.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Who among the following later Mughal rulers ruled for longest period?

answerOptions.rationale:
The later Mughal ruler Muhammad Shah ruled for
the longest period. He was the Mughal Emperor of
India from 1719 to 1748 AD. He was fond of a luxurious
life like music, dance, alcohol, women and animal
fights. For these reasons, he was given the title of
Rangeela.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements in the context of Nadir Shah’s invasion in India.

2. He assumed the title of Hindustan-e-ala after defeating Mughal emperor.
3. He carried away the famous Koh-i-Noor diamond and jewel-studded Peacock throne of Shah Jahan.
4. He compelled Muhammad Shah to cede him all the provinces of the Mughal Empire East of the Indus river.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct regarding Nadir
Shah’s invasion in India.
The Battle of Karnal (1739 AD) was fought between
Nadir Shah and Mughal Emperor, Muhammad Shah.
The Mughal Emperor was defeated and imprisoned.
Among Nadir Shah’s booty included the famous Peacock
throne, the Koh-i-Noor and the Darya-ye-Noor diamonds.
Statements (2) and (4) are incorrect because after the
battle, Muhammad Shah was retained the emperor of
the Mughal Empire. All Mughal land West of the Indus
were ceded to Nadir Shah. Nadir Shah didnot assumed
any title after defeating Mugals.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

With the gradual weakening and decline of the Mughal Empire, which regional forces asserted themselves?

answerOptions.rationale:
With the gradual weakening and decline of the
Mughal Empire, local and regional political and
economic forces from the region of Bengal, Maratha
and Mysore asserted themselves.
The weakening of the central authority and subsequent
turbulences in the provinces led to the rise of a large
number of independent and semi-independent powers
such as the Bengal, Awadh, Hyderabad, Mysore and
Maratha Kingdoms.
Rise of Provincial States

questions.question:

Given below description is related to which of the following rulers? He made an effort to build modern navy after 1796 AD. He used to say “better to live a day as a lion than a lifetime as a sheep”. He sent emissaries to France, Turkey, Iran and Pegu (Myanmar) to develop foreign trade.

answerOptions.rationale:
The given description is related to Tipu Sultan.
Tipu Sultan was Hyder Ali’s son and a great warrior.
He was also known as the Tiger of Mysore. He was a
well-educated man fluent in Arabic, Persian, Kanarese
and Urdu. He introduced a number of administrative
innovations during his rule. In order to boost foreign
trade and develop bilateral relation with foreign
countries, he sent emissaries to France, Turkey, Iran
and Pegu (Myanmar).

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class XII, Old NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2001)

Who among the following Indian rulers established embassies in foreign countries on modern lines?

answerOptions.rationale:
The ruler of Mysore kingdom, Tipu Sultan
established embassies in foreign countries on modern
lines. He ruled Mysore from 1782 to 1799 AD and was
one of the first Indian rulers to understand the threat
posed by foreign trading companies. During his tenure,
he sent embassies to France, Turkey, Iran and Pegu
(Myanmar) to develop foreign trade.

The great ruler Ranjit Singh belonged to which of the following misl?

After the death of Aurangzeb, civil war broke between, which of the following Maratha rulers?

answerOptions.rationale:
After the death of Aurangzeb, a civil war broke out
between Shahu at Satara and his aunt Tara Bai at
Kolhapur, for gaining control over Maratha empire. She
had carried out anti-Mughal struggle since 1700 AD in
the name of her son Shivaji II after the death of her
husband Raja Ram. Shahu was released from captivity

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct with reference to evolution and consolidation of Peshwaship?
1. The period of Peshwa domination started from the time of Shahu.
2. Baji Rao I made the Peshwa the functional head of the Maratha Empire.
3. Under Peshwa rule, Maratha Empire was extended to North India.
4. Balaji Baji Rao was also known as Nana Saheb.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct regarding
evolution and consolidation of Peshwaship. Peshwas
were the hereditary ruler who acted as a Prime Minister
to the king of the Maratha Empire. During the reign of
Shahu, Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath became most
powerful. It started the period of Peshwa domination.
His son, Baji Rao I made the Peshwa the functional head
of the Maratha Empire. During the reign of Baji Rao I
and his successor Balaji Baji Rao (also known as Nana
Saheb), the Maratha Empire extended to North India.

Empire.
Bhonsle The kingdom of Nagpur came under the rule

century AD. The city of Nagpur was the capital of the
state.

successful in capturing the fort of Singhgarh, Raigarh

of the important settlements of Portuguese on Western
coast of India.

Lally. After this defeat, French forces, within a year,
they had lost all their possessions in India. The war
ended in 1763 AD with the Signing of the treaty
of Paris.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Subsidiary Alliance.
1. The first ruler to accept the Subsidiary Alliance was the Nizam of Hyderabad.
2. Under this policy, Indian rulers were forced to have a British official called the resident at his court.
3. Under this policy, Indian rulers made to keep a large British force within their territory and pay for its maintenance.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
with reference to the Subsidiary Alliance. Lord
Wellesley in the year 1798 introduced, the Subsidiary
Alliance, which was a new intervention policy to expand
the British territory in India. The first ruler in India who
accepted the Subsidiary Alliance was the Nizam of
Hyderabad, Asaf Jah II.
Under the Subsidiary Alliance, Indian princely states
were forced to keep British resident at their court. The
Indian ruler would not employ any other European at
their court.
An Indian ruler entering into a Subsidiary Alliance with
the British, had to accept British forces in his territory
and also agreed to pay for their maintenance. In return,
the East India Company, undertook to protect the ltate
from external dangers and internal disorders. Nizam of
Hyderabad was the first to accept the Subsidiary Alliance.

questions.question:

What were the main negative consequences of the Subsidiary Alliance Policy of the British?
1. Indian rulers lost all vestiges of sovereignty in case of external matters.
2. British Resident interfered in day-to-day administration of the state.
3. British provided training to the soldiers of the state, which signed a Subsidiary Alliance.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) were the negative
consequences of the Subsidiary Alliance Policy of the
British. Indian rulers had give up their Independence and
had to accept the suzerainty of the English East India
Company.

questions.question:
(Chap 2, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements in the context of the Governor-General Lord Wellesley?
1. During his reign, British army attacked and defeated Tipu Sultan in 1799 AD.
2. In 1801 AD, Lord Wellesley forced a new treaty upon the puppet Nawab of Carnatic compelling him to cede his kingdom to the Company in return for a pension.
3. Arthur Wellesley defeated the combined armies of Sindhia and Bhonsle in 1803 AD.
4. In 1808 AD, Wellesley was recalled from India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct in the
context of the Governor-General Lord Wellesley.
Lord Wellesley was the Governor-General of Bengal
from 1798 to 1805 AD. During his tenure, the fourth
and last Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1799 AD. In
this battle, Tipu Sultan was killed. The second
Anglo-Maratha war was also fought during his tenure in
which Bhonsle, Sindhia and Holkar were defeated.
He also forced a new treaty upon, Nawab of Carnatic
compelling him to cede his kingdom to the Company in
return for a pension.
Statement (4) is incorrect as Wellesley was recalled from
India in 1805 and once again Lord Cornwallis was sent
to India.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. The conquest of Sindh occurred as a result of growing Anglo-Russian rivalry in Europe and Asia.
2. Sindh was annexed by British in 1837 AD.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (1) is correct. The conquest of Sindh
occurred as a result of growing Anglo-Russian rivalry in
Europe and Asia. There was constant fear by the British
that Russia might attack India through Afghanistan or
Persia. To counter Russia, the British Government
decided to increase its control over Afghanistan and
Persia. Therefore, they decided to conquer Sindh.
Statement (2) is incorrect as Sindh was annexed by
British in 1843 AD.

questions.question:

Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (2) is correct because the strong relation
between Awadh and Britishers strengthened the British
rule in Bengal.
Awadh was envisioned as the buffer state against armies
of Marathas. However, with the subsequent defeat of
Marathas and consolidation of its territories in rest of
India, Britishers, ultimately annexed the Awadh
kingdom in 1856 AD.
Statement (1) is incorrect because the Nawab of Awadh
was supported by the British East India Company in war
under the Governor-General of Bengal, Warren
Hastings. In this war, the Rohillas were defeated.

answerOptions.rationale:

answerOptions.rationale:

provinces were established in 1836, through merging

conquered provinces.
Statement (1) is incorrect because British territories
were broadly divided into administrative units called
Presidencies. There were three such presidencies –
Bengal, Madras and Bombay. Each Presidency was
under the charge of the Governor.

questions.question:

Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct
because to ensure good administration, Lord
Cornwallis created a permanent police force in India.
Each district were divided into number of thanas, each
of which was headed by a daroga. The hereditary village
policemen became chowkidar. The cities were placed
under the kotwals.

questions.question:

The Permanent Settlement was introduced by (UKPSC Pre 2002)

answerOptions.rationale:
The Permanent Settlement of Bengal was
introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793. It was an
agreement between the Company and the zamindars to
fix the land revenue. Under this system, zamindars
were recognised as the owner of land.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-VIII, New NCERT)

Which of the following features of the Permanent Settlement of 1793 is/are correct?
1. The Permanent Settlement vested land ownership rights in the peasants.
2. The Permanent Settlement vested land ownership rights in the zamindars.
3. The zamindars had to pay a fixed amount of rent by a particular date.
4. The zamindars benefitted hugely from the Permanent Settlement while the peasants suffered.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (2) and (3) are correct regarding
features of Permanent Settlement of 1793 because
zamindars were given hereditary rights of succession of
the lands under them. The amount to be paid by the
landlords was fixed and they were made liable to pay
rent by a particular date.
Statements (1) and (4) are incorrect as the revenue rates
were so high that many zamindars became defaulters.
Thus, zamindars did not get benefit from the system.
The Permanent Settlement of 1793 enacted by Lord
Cornwallis recognised landlords or zamindars as the
owners of the land.

questions.question:

Who devised the ‘Mahalwari Settlement’, which came into effect in 1822?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Mahalwari settlement was devised by Holt
Mackenzie in 1822 and it was reviewed under Lord
William Bentick in 1833.
In this system, the land revenue was collected by the
village headmen and it was not fixed. The peasants were
the owner of the land and every peasant had to give his
share of the revenue.

questions.question:

The demand of revenue was permanently fixed.

system because in the Mahalwari system, the revenue
was to be revised periodically.
The Mahalwari system is one of the three major land
revenue systems introduced by the British in India.
In this system, the land was divided into Mahals. Each
Mahal comprised one or more villages.
Ownership rights were vested with the peasants and the
Villages Committee was responsible for collection of the
taxes.

(Chap 4, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

answerOptions.text: The steel frame of the British administration was its Civil Services.
Lord Cornwallis was the real founder of the British Civil Services in India.
Indians were given equal opportunities in the Civil Services.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (b) are correct regarding
evolution of Civil Services in India. Lord Cornwallis
was the real founder of Civil Services in India and
hence he is called the ‘Father of Indian Civil Services.’

administration.

given equal opportunities in the civil services. The exam
was conducted only in London and age limit was set
between 18 years and 23 years. The syllabus was
moulded in favour of British residents which made it
difficult for Indians to succeed.

questions.question:

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:

discrimination between the Indians and Britishers.

questions.question:

downward filtration was related to education.
It was propounded by Lord Macaulay who believed that
the main purpose to the company was to educate elite

responsible for percolation of modern and English
education to the masses.
The main reason behind this move was the need for
educated Indians in minor administrative posts.

questions.question:

politician of 19th century.

civilised. No branch of Eastern knowledge, according
to him, could be compared to what England had
produced.

How villages were influenced by the economic policies of the British Government?
1. The villages lost their self-sufficiency.
2. The village panchayats lost their authority.

answerOptions.rationale:
Both (1) and (2) are correct regarding economic
policies of the British Government.
High tarrifs on export of Indian goods and relatively free
imports of machine made British goods crippled the
Indian handicraft sector. Added to it, the high land
revenue demand increased poverty in India. Due to this
reason the Indian villages lost their self-sufficiency.

questions.question:

British promoted indigo cultivation in India.
What was/were the main reason(s) that raised the demand of the Indian Indigo?
1. Indigo produced a rich blue colour.
2. Expansion of cotton industries in England.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding, promotion of Indigo cultivation in India by
British. The 17th and 18th century saw large scale
industrialisation in England. It enabled opening of
large number of textile mills in England driven by
machine. Gradually, it became one of the biggest
manufacturer of cotton textile. These industries in
England were dependent on Indian Indigo as dye, as it
was of better quality and produced a rich blue colour,
whereas dye from wood (grown in Europe) was pale
and dull.

questions.question:
(Chap 3, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

The cause of decline of textile industries in 18th century in Bengal was

answerOptions.text: high tariff rates on exports to Britain.
answerOptions.rationale:
The cause of decline of textile industries in 18th
century in Bengal was high tariff rates on exports to
Britain. Before the consolidation of British power in
India, the Indian cotton products were in high demand
in European markets.
However, Britishers after conquest of India increased
the tarrif rates on export to Britian, it made Indian
textile products costlier in Britian, thus discouraging its
consumption. At the same time, imports of machine-
made cheap British textile products flooded the Indian
market. Thus, Indian textile industry lost its domestic
market resulting into its decline.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VIII, New NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2018)

After the Santhal uprising subsided, what was/ were the measures taken by Colonial Government? 
1. The territories called ‘Santhal Parganas’ were created.
2. It became illegal for a Santhal to transfer land to a non-Santhal.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding measures taken by Colonial Government
after Santhal uprising. The Santhal rebellion occurred
in Chhota Nagpur region of Bihar (modern Jharkhand)
in 1855-56. After the suppression of the revolt, the
British Government accepted the demand of a separate
Santhal Pargana. Besides creating a separate district, a
Santhal Pargana Tenancy Act was also passed by the
British Government. Under this Act, it became illegal
for a Santhal to transfer land to a non-Santhal.

questions.question:
(Chap 4, Class-VIII, New NCERT)  (IAS Pre 2011)

Which amongst the following provided a common factor for tribal insurrection in India in the 19th century?

answerOptions.text: Introduction of a new system of land revenue and taxation of tribal products.
Influence of foreign religious missionaries in tribal areas.
Rise of a large number of moneylenders, traders and revenue farmers as middleman in tribal areas.
The complete disruption of the old agrarian order of the tribal communities.
answerOptions.rationale:
The main reason behind tribal insurrection in
India in the 19th century was complete disruption of
the old agrarian order of tribal communities. The tribals
living in Central India such as Bhils, Gonds, Santhals
and Mundas were deprived of forest rights of collecting
fuel and fodder from the forest under the laws enacted
by the British colonial authorities. It completely
disrupted their old agrarian order.

The immediate cause of the Deccan Riots of 1875 was

answerOptions.text: high interest rates charged by Mahajans.
answerOptions.rationale:

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct.
Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in
Bombay in 1875. It supported four Varna system but
also believed that it should be based on merit not birth.
It believed that Hindu religion gives everyone an equal
place in the spiritual and social life. In this way, it
repudiated the authority of the caste system.
Statement (3) is incorrect because Dayananda
Saraswati’s real name was Mool Shankar.

(b) He launched Shuddhi Movement.
(c) Arya Samajists opposed child marriage and
encouraged remarriage of women.
(d) None of the above
Ans. (a)

Exp.
Statement (a) is incorrect regarding Dayananda
Saraswati and Arya Samaj because it believed that
Vedas were infallible.
Dayananda Saraswati looked upon the Vedas as ‘India’s
Rock of Ages’. He believed that the Hindu religion
and the Vedas on which it was based were eternal,
unalterable, infallible and divine. Therefore, he gave
the slogan ‘Go Back to the Vedas’ and ‘the Vedas are
the Source of All Knowledge’.
According to him, the later Hindu scriptures such as
Puranas were responsible for the evil practice of idol
worship and other superstitious beliefs in the Hindu
religion.

Buddha, he urged people of India to work for their own
salvation and reject orthodox religious practices.

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XII, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2015)

Who was known by the nickname ‘Lokahitvadi’?

answerOptions.rationale:
The famous social and religious reformer in
Western India, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, was popularly
known as ‘Lokahitvadi’. He made powerful rationalist
attacks on Hindu Orthodoxy, and preached the
religious and social equality. He condemned the caste
system and worked for the upliftment of the women.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VIII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements in the context of the Paramhansa Mandali.
1. It was founded in 1840.
2. Its main objective is to abolish caste system.
3. Its headquarters was in Calcutta.
4. The member of this group believed in violent means.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (3) and (4) are incorrect in the
context of the Paramhansa Mandali.
Paramhansa Mandali was founded by Dadoba
Pandurang and Balshastri Jambhekar of Maharashtra in
1849. The principles of the Samaj denied polytheism of
popular Hinduism, the caste system and the
Brahmanical monopoly of knowledge. Its headquarter
was in Bombay.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Who formed the ‘Satya Shodhak Samaj’? (CGPSC Pre 2018)

answerOptions.rationale:
Jyotirao Phule founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj
on 24th September, 1873. Through this Society, he
opposed caste system, idolatry and denounced the need
for priests. He also promoted respect for all religions
but shunned the rituals associated with them.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements is correct regarding Kandukuri Veerasalingam?

answerOptions.text: He started Telugu journal to promote social reform.
He promoted girls education and widow remarriage.
He was influenced by the ideas of the Brahmo Samaj.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the given statements are correct regarding
Kandukuri Veerasalingam.
He is considered as the ‘Father of Renaissance
Movement’ in Telugu. He wrote the first novel in
Telugu language. He set up schools for the education of
girls and women. He also performed the first widow
remarriage in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Dharma Paripalana Yogam.

for the upliftment of lower castes by educating them and
opposed Brahmin domination.

the values and practices mentioned in Vedas. Arya
Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in 1875.

crusade against other religion became contributory

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:
Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College was

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Which reformer does the following passage relate to? “He insisted on the cooperation of the Muslims with the British Government and looked at all political movements with distrust. Thus, when the Indian National Congress was formed, he opposed it. He regarded education alone as the means of national progress.”

The following passage is related to Sir Syed
Ahmad Khan. He was one of the greatest Muslim
reformers of India. He interpreted Quran in the light of
modern rationalism and science. He took up the
struggle against fanaticism, ignorance, narrow
mindedness and bigotry and laid emphasis on free
thinking.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Who founded Rahanumai Mazdayasanan Sabha?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Western-educated progressive Parsis like
Dadabhai Naoroji, JB Wacha, SS Bengali and Naoroji
Furdunji founded the Rahanumai Mazdayasanan Sabha
(Religious Reform Association) in 1851. It’s object was
regeneration of the social condition of the Parsis and
the restoration of the Zoroastrian religion to its pristine
purity.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

At which of the following places, Singh Sabha Movement was formed?
1. Amritsar 2. Lucknow
3. Lahore 4. Delhi
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
The Sikh reform movement, namely Singh Sabha
movement was started in 1870s. Singh Sabha was
formed at Amritsar and Lahore. The two Sabhas were
later merged. It played an important role in the spread
of education.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements.

answerOptions.rationale:
All the statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct.

Movement. This campaign brought reform in the
Gurdwaras in India during the early 1920s.
This movement led to the introduction of Gurdwara Act
in 1925, which placed all the historical Sikh shrines in
India under the control of Shiromani Gurdwara
Parbandhak Committee.
Khalsa College in Amritsar was founded in 1892.

questions.question:

answerOptions.rationale:
The earliest and best known women social

questions.question:

Who founded the Widow Remarriage Association in the 1850’s?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Widow Remarriage Association was founded

questions.question:
(Chap 13, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Which social reformer founded the Gujarati weekly ‘Satya Prakash’ to promote widow remarriage?

answerOptions.rationale:
Karsondas Mulji founded the Gujarati weekly
‘Satya Prakash’ to promote widow remarriage, in 1852.
It was later merged with Rast Goftar, another
newspaper published in Bombay.
Jaganath Seth, Bhau Daji and Vishnu Shastri Pandit are
also some of the prominent social reformers who
advocated the women’s education. Vishnu Shastri pandit
founded the Widow Remarriage Association in the 1850s.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following statements with reference to the Tatvabodhini Sabha.

2. It promoted a systematic study of India’s past in the Bengali language.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are incorrect?

answerOptions.rationale:
Only statement (1) is incorrect regarding
Tatvabodhini Sabha. Tatvabodhini Sabha was founded
by Debendranath Tagore in 1839. The main objective
of the Sabha was to promote a more rational and
humanist form of Hinduism based on the Vedanta, the
Upanishads that form the last part of the Vedas.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2011)

Who founded the ‘Theosophical Society’?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Theosophical Society was founded by
Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott in New
York, in 1875. It was influenced by Indian philosophy
and Vedantic traditions and worked towards promoting
universal brotherhood of men.

questions.question:
(Chap 10, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

Which of the following statements about Theosophical Society are correct?
1. Its founders were non-Indians.
2. In India, its headquarters was in Calcutta.
3. Its advocates were in favour of the revival of Hinduism.
4. It recognised the doctrine of the transmigration of soul.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1), (3) and (4) are correct about
Theosophical Society.
The Theosophical Society was founded by Madam HP
Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott in New York, in 1875. The
Theosophists respected all religions.
Its advocates were however in favour of the revival of
Hinduism and Vedic learning. It recognised the
doctrine of Karma and transmigration of soul.
Statement (2) is incorrect because the society has its
centre in India in Adyar, near Madras.

questions.question:

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2010)

With, which uprising is Mangal Pandey associated?

answerOptions.rationale:
Mangal Pandey was associated with uprising at
Barrackpore in West Bengal. He was hanged on 29th
March, 1857 for revolting single handedly and attacking
his superior officers. This event is considered as the
precursor to the Revolt of 1857.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

To whom the rebel soldiers from Meerut declared the ‘Emperor of India’, after capturing Delhi in Revolt of 1857.

answerOptions.rationale:
The rebel soldiers from Meerut declared,
Bahadur Shah Zafar as the ‘Emperor of India’ after
capturing Delhi in the Revolt of 1857. Bahadur Shah
Zafar was the last Mughal Emperor. The Mughal
Emperor also got support from the rulers and chiefs of
the country and together they rose against the British
power. People were convinced that the Mughals would
make better rulers than the Britishers.

questions.question:
(BPSC Pre 2020)

Who spearheaded the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar? (Chap 8, Class-XII, Old NECRT)

answerOptions.rationale:
Kunwar Singh spearheaded the Revolt of 1857 in
Bihar. He was zamindar of Jagdishpur near Arrah. He
is considered as the most outstanding military leader
and strategist of the revolt. He fought with the British
in Bihar and later joining hands with Nana Saheb’s
forces, he also campaigned in Awadh and Central
India.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT)

Shah Mal was one of the many leaders who played an important part in the Revolt of 1857.
Which of the following statement is incorrect in his context?
1. Shah Mal mobilised the headmen and cultivators of Chaurasee Des.
2. He took over the bungalow of an English officer, turned it into a ‘Hall of Justice’.
3. He was killed in battle in July, 1860.
Codes

answerOptions.rationale:
Statement (3) is incorrect in the context of role
played by Shah Mal in the Revolt of 1857 because Shah
Mal was killed in battle in July, 1857. He lived in
Pargana Barout in Uttar Pradesh. He mobilised the
headmen and cultivators of Chaurasee Des, against the
British. He also attacked the government building of
British Company and made their building a ‘Hall of
Justice’.

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following Assertion

answerOptions.text: and Reason (R) and choose the correct code. Assertion
The Revolt of 1857 failed to secure freedom from British Government. Reason (R) British introduced many administrative reforms after the Revolt of 1857. Codes
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
answerOptions.rationale:
Both the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true,
but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of
Assertion (A). The Revolt of 1857 marked the end of the
East India Company’s rule in India. India now came
under the direct rule of the British crown.
Thus, it failed to secure freedom from the British
Government.
The Queen’s proclamation of 1858, promised to respect
the sovereignty of princely states. It also introduced few
administrative reforms.
The Governor-General’s office was replaced by that of
the Viceroy. The rights of Indian rulers were
recognised. The ratio of British officers to Indian
soldiers increased but the armoury remained in the
hands of the Britishers.

answerOptions.text: A is true, but R is false.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XII, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2008)

After the Revolt of 1857, the British recruited the soldiers from

answerOptions.text: Bengalis and Odias from the East
Gurkhas, Sikhs and Pathan in the North
answerOptions.rationale:
After the Revolt of 1857 in India, the British
recruited the soldiers in the British Indian army from
Sikh, Gurkha and Pathan communities on a large scale
and declared them as martial communities. These
communities supported Britishers in suppression of
Revolt of 1857.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Hindu-Muslim unity was the main pillar of the Revolt of 1857. In order to create disunity and rift between both the communities, what measures was/were taken by British?

answerOptions.text: In early years, Muslims were discriminated against in services.
They were shown as the oppressor of Muslims.
It was propagated that the interest of Hindus will be met only on being loyal to British rule.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (a) and (c) are correct regarding attempt
by the Britishers to create rift and disunity among
Hindu and Muslim community in the course of Revolt of
1857. British Government took various measures in order
to create disunity among Hindus and Muslims during
1857.
In early years, Muslims were discriminated in services.
The Britishers gave preference to Hindu soldiers in
recruitment in comparison to Muslim soldiers.
British colonial authorities also propagated through
propaganda that the interest of Hindus will be met only
on being loyal to British role.
Statement (b) is incorrect as Muslim Community was
Shown as oppressor of Hindus by the Britishers.

questions.question:

Consider the following statements with reference to the Indian National Congress.

2. British officials considered Congress as an organisation of masses.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal supported the policy of Petition and Prayers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) is correct with reference to the
Indian National Congress (INC). The time period from
1885 to 1905 of INS can be called the ‘Moderate
Phase’. The leaders of this phase are called moderates.
Statement (3) is incorrect as Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin
Chandra Pal belonged to the Extremist Phase of Indian

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

Consider the following in the context of initial phase of the Indian Freedom Struggle.
1. One section of the Congress supported the radical ideologies and it came to known as extremist.
2. The international events at the end of 19th and beginning of 20th century inspired the Indian Freedom Struggle.

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct in the
context of initial phase of the Indian Freedom Struggle.
In the beginning of the 20th century, a different group
emerged which had a rather aggressive approach against
the British Empire. This group was called the extremist
and did not believe in the peaceful stance of the
moderate leaders. The international events at the end of
19th and beginning of 20th century such as Boers war,
lrish struggle, etc inspired the Indian Freedom Struggle.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-X, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2017)

The declaration of Partition of Bengal was done on

answerOptions.rationale:
The declaration of Partition of Bengal was done on
19th July, 1905. Under this arrangement, the province
of Bengal was divided into two separate parts; Eastern
Bengal and Assam with a population of 31 millions, and
the rest of Bengal with a population of 54 millions of
whom 18 millions were Bengalis and 36 millions were
Biharis and Oriyas.
According to the British colonial authorities, existing
province of Bengal was too big to be efficiently
administered by a single provincial government.

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-VIII, New NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2020)

Which movement was started as a reaction to the Partition of Bengal?

answerOptions.rationale:
Swadeshi Movement was started as a reaction to
Partition of Bengal. It was initiated on 7th August, 1905
and was collectively led by Moderate leaders such as
Surendranath Banerjee and Krishna Kumar Mitra and
extremist leaders including Bal Gangadhar Tilak and
Lala Lajpat Rai.
The main aim of the Swadeshi Movement was to
encourage the idea of self-help, promote the
growth of indigenous enterprises and boycott the
British goods.
38. Consider the following statements with reference
to Swadeshi Movement.
(Chap 9, Class-VIII, Old NCERT)

2. The national education was promoted as a part of
Swadeshi Movement.

correct?

(c) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2
Ans.
j (c)
Exp. Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct with
reference to Swadeshi Movement.
After the Partition of Bengal, Swadeshi Movement was
formally started from Town Hall Calcutta on 7th August,
1905 to curb import of foreign goods by relying on
domestic production. It also promoted the idea of
Swadeshi enterprises and national education.
National education was also promoted in the Swadeshi
Movement. In 1906, the National Council of Education
was set up to organise National Education System. For
technical education, Bengal Institute of Technology was
established.

Deputy Subedar on behalf of Nawab. It held a great

questions.question:
(Chap 5, Class-XII, Old NCERT)  (BPSC Pre 2005)

Who among the following abolished ‘Dual Government’ system in Bengal?

answerOptions.rationale:
The ‘Dual Government’ system in Bengal was
abolished by Warren Hastings in 1772. With this,
Bengal was brought under direct control of East India
Company. The authority of Nawab of Bengal over
administration, also ended with, abolishment of ‘Dual
Government’ system in Bengal.

questions.question:
(Chap 1, Class-VIII, New NCERT)

Consider the following statements.
1. Charles Cornwallis was the Governor-General of India in 1793.
2. During his tenure many reforms were introduced.
3. Mahalwari system was implemented during his reign.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (2) are correct.
Charles Cornwallis was the Governor-General of India
from 1786 to 1793.
His tenure was marked by several constitutional as well
as administrative reforms. Notable among them include
- Introduction of Permanent Settlement and Cornwallis
code in 1793. He also initiated police reforms in India.
Statement (3) is incorrect because Mahalwari system
was introduced by Holt Mackenzie in 1822.

questions.question:

At a time when empires in Europe were crumbing before the might of Napolean, which one of the following Governor-General kept the British flag flying high in India?

answerOptions.rationale:
At a time when empires in Europe were crumbing
before the might of Napoleon, the British flag was kept
high by the Governor-General Lord Wellesley.
Lord Wellesley remained Governor-General of India
from 1798 to 1805. At the same time, European powers
including Britishers were facing defeat at the hands of
Napoleon.
However, under Wellesley who devised the system
of subsidiary Alliance in 1798, British imperialism
forces were able to consolidate their possessions in
India.

(Chap 4, Class-XII, Old NCERT)

The conquest of Sindh by British was completed during the period of

answerOptions.rationale:
The conquest of Sindh by British was completed
during the period of Lord Ellenborough. It was
accomplished in 1843. It occurred as a result of the
growing Anglo-Russian rivalry in Europe and Asia and
the consequent British fear that Russia might attack

questions.question:

Lord Dalhousie planned for the construction of a network of railways in India in order to

questions.question:
(Chap 9, Class-XII, Old NCERT)  (UPPSC Pre 2010)

Who was responsible for encouraging the Local Self-Government in India?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Viceroy, Lord Ripon encouraged the
establishment of the Local Self-Government in India.
During his tenure, a Government resolution laid down
the policy of administering local affairs largely through
rural and urban local bodies, a majority of whose members
would be non-official. This resolution also permitted
the election of non-official as Chairman of a local body.

Who was the Governor-General of India, when the Council Act, 1909 was enacted to consolidate the moderate nationalist?

answerOptions.rationale:
Lord Minto II was the Governor-General of India,
when the Council Act, 1909 was enacted. The Indian
Council Act, 1909 or Morley-Minto Reforms was
passed in an attempt to widen the scope of legislative
councils and placate the demands of moderates in Indian
National Congress. It introduced separate and
discriminatory electorate.

Lord Minto and Lord Hardinge were attacked

Lord Hardinge was the Governor-General of India from
1910 to 1916. He was attacked Delhi in 1912, while
carrying out royal procession on occasion of transfer of
capital from Calcutta to Delhi.

questions.question:
(Chap 16, Class-X, Old NCERT)

Name the Viceroy during whose tenure a system called dyarchy was introduced in provinces as a step towards Constitutional reforms.

answerOptions.rationale:
The system of Dyarchy was introduced during the
tenure of Lord Chelmsford in 1919.
Under this system, the provincial subjects were divided
into two parts–transferred and reserved. The transferred
subjects were to be administered by the Governor with
the aid of ministers responsible to the Legislative
Council.
The reserved subjects were to be administered by the
Governor and his executive council without being
responsible to the Legislative Council.

Who was the last Viceroy of independent India?

Among the given temples, which one is known as ‘Black Pagoda’ because it is made up of black stone?

answerOptions.rationale:
The Sun temple at Konark is also known as ‘Black
Pagoda’ as it is made up of black stone. It was built by
the King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga
dynasty between 1238-1250 AD.
It was built on the patterns of Kalinga architecture and
includes a depiction of a 100 ft high chariot being
pulled by horses and wheels carved out of a single
stone.

Statement (3) is incorrect regarding Vesra style of
temple architecture as Lad Khan temple is one of the

constructed in Panchayatana style of architecture.

Ramalingesvara temple at Gudur.

Consider the following statements with reference to the architectural development in the Deccan.
1. The Jama Masjid of Gulbarga is the only mosque in India to have a covered courtyard.
2. The madrasa of Mahmud Gawan is located at Bidar.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.rationale:
Both the statements (1) and (2) are correct
regarding architectural development in Deccan in the
medieval phase. The founder of Bahamani kingdom
Ala-ud-din Hasan Bahmani Shah constructed Jama
Masjid at Gulbarga in 14th century AD. It is the only
mosque in India to have a covered courtyard. The
Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan is located at Bidar. It was
built in 15th century AD. Mahmud Gawan was the
Prime Minister of the Sultanate of Bahmani.

questions.question:
(Chap 7, Class-XI, New NCERT Fine Arts)

Consider the following statements.
1. During the Gupta and Post-Gupta many standing Buddha images with right hand in abhaya mudra were cast in North India, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
2. Vakataka bronze images of the Buddha from Phophnar, Maharashtra shows influence of Mathura school of Art.

answerOptions.rationale:
Statements (1) and (3) are correct as during the
Gupta and Post-Gupta, many standing Buddha images
with right hand in abhaya mudra were cast in North
India, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
Notable examples of this sculpture include images of
Buddha at Dhaneshwar Khera (Uttar Pradesh) and
Sultanganj (Bihar). It was patronised by the Gupta and
Pala rulers.
In Buddhist centres like Nalanda, a school of bronze
casting emerged around the ninth century during the
rule of the Pala Dynasty in Bihar and Bengal regions.
Statement (2) is incorrect as Vakataka bronze images of
the Buddha from Phophnar, Maharashtra, are
contemporary with the Gupta period bronze. They show
the influence of the Amaravati style of art.

(Chap 5, Class-XII, New NCERT Fine Arts)

During the reign of which among the following rulers, Basohli developed a distinctive and magnificent style of painting?

answerOptions.rationale:
During the reign of the King, Kirpal Pal (1678 to
1695 AD) Basohli developed a distinctive and
magnificent style of painting. This school is
characterised by a strong use of primary colours and
warm yellows—filling the background and horizon,
stylised treatment of vegetation and raised white paint
for imitating the representation of pearls in ornaments.
The most popular theme of Basohli painters was the
Rasamanjari of Bhanu Datta. Devida (carpenter–painter)
was the most famous painter of this school.

questions.question:
(Chap 6, Class-XII, New NCERT Fine Arts)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List II (Famous Painters of (Paintings) Modern India ) A. Kshitindranath Majumdar 1. City in the Night B. Abdul Rehman Chughtai 2. Rasa-Lila C. Gaganendranath Tagore 3. Rama Vanquishing the Pride of the Ocean D. Raja Ravi Varma 4. Radhika
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.
The modern Indian painter Kshitindranath Majumdar
was associated with watercolour painting
Rasa-Lila which portrays the divine life of God Shri
Krishna.
The modern Indian painter Abdul Rehman Chughtai was
associated with the wash and tempera painting Radhika.
He was a descendant of Ustad Ahmed, the chief
architect of Shah Jahan.
The modern Indian painter Gaganendranath Tagore was
associated with watercolour painting ‘City in the Night’.
He was one of the earlier Indian painters, who made use
of language and syntax of Cubism to render his ideas.
The modern Indian painter Raja Ravi Varma was
associated with Puranic painting, ‘Rama Vanquishing
the Pride of the Ocean’.
He was one of the first Indian painters to use oil paint
and master the art of lithographic reproduction for
mythological subject.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT Fine Arts)

‘Madhubani’ painting is related to which state? (MPPSC Pre 2013)

answerOptions.rationale:
‘Madhubani’ painting is related to Bihar. Also
referred as mithila painting, this unique style of
painting is practised by the women. It is characterised
by use of geometric patterns, colourful motifs and
intense emotions. The themes of Madhubani paintings
usually include natural elements like fish, birds,
animals, turtle, sun, moon, etc.

questions.question:
(Chap 8, Class-XII, New NCERT Fine Arts)

Match the following lists correctly and choose the correct code. List I List I (Folk Painting) (Associated states) A. Warli painting 1. Bihar B. Mithila painting 2. Maharashtra C. Sawara painting 3. Odisha D. Pata Chitra painting 4. Madhya Pradesh
Codes A B C D A B C D

answerOptions.rationale:
The correct matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.
Warli is folk painting of Maharashtra. It is practised by
Warli tribes living in the Konkan areas of Maharashtra.
Mithila painting is a folk painting performed by women
of the Mithila region of the Bihar. It is also known as
Madhubani painting.
Sawara painting is practised by tribals of Madhya
Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha.
Pata Chitra painting is practised by the artists from
Odisha. Patachitras are done on small strips of cotton
cloth, which is prepared by coating the cloth with soft
white stone powder and glue made from tamarind seeds.
